item: `.env.example` ships `SPECSTRIDE_CRITIC=dsh`, which differs from the orchestrator's built-in default `claude` (and from the comment two lines above it that says the critic stays on `claude`); copying the template changes the critic backend.
`.env.example` ships `SPECSTRIDE_LOKI_URL=http://localhost:3110`, which differs from the built-in default port 3100.
`.env.example` documents the precedence as `built-in defaults < .env < CLI flags` and omits the caller-environment layer that the orchestrator actually applies between `.env` and flags.
The python deprecation line has the same text as the bash one: `specstride: deprecated WIGGUM_* variables read as SPECSTRIDE_*: <names> (rename them)`.

`specstride_env.apply()` copies every `WIGGUM_<X>` to `SPECSTRIDE_<X>` in the process environment when the new name is absent, returns the legacy names used and prints the deprecation line once per process to stderr.
`specstride_env.get(name)` accepts the name with or without the `SPECSTRIDE_` prefix and returns the new-name value, else the legacy-name value, else the default.

`specstride_env.state_dirname()` mirrors the bash rule: `.wiggum` only when `.specstride/` is absent and `.wiggum/` exists; it sets `SPECSTRIDE_STATE_NOTICE_SHOWN=1` and prints the legacy notice once.
`orchestrator.sh [options]` is the run entry point (the single driver of the proposer/critic phase loop); it takes only options, no positional arguments.
`-w|--workdir DIR` sets the run/work directory (default `$PWD`); the orchestrator `cd`s into it and canonicalises it to the physical `$PWD`.
`-s|--specs FILE` names the spec file explicitly (any name, any location) and bypasses spec discovery.
`--spec-format FMT` (`native` | `speckit-tasks` | `openspec-change`) forces the spec grammar; default empty = auto-detect; overrides `SPECSTRIDE_SPEC_FORMAT`.
`--feature SLUG` sets the feature namespace for durable state and selects among several discovered `tasks.md` candidates; overrides `SPECSTRIDE_FEATURE`.
`--proposer BACKEND` selects the proposer backend (default `$SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER` or `dsh`); the value is not validated by the flag parser itself.
`--critic BACKEND` selects the critic provider (default `$SPECSTRIDE_CRITIC` or `claude`); passed to `critic.py --provider`.
`--max-rejects N` sets the critic REJECTs per phase before halting (default 3); no numeric validation at parse time.
`--max-iter N` sets proposer passes per phase (default 30); passed to `proposer.sh --max-iter`.
`--proposer-timeout SECONDS` sets the global hard wall-clock ceiling of one proposer pass (default 1800).
`--proposer-timeout-phase N=SECONDS` (repeatable) overrides the pass ceiling for phase N only.
`--critic-timeout SECONDS` sets the hard wall-clock limit of one critic call (default 300); passed to `critic.py --timeout`.
`--start-phase N` overrides the derived resume phase; the value is used unvalidated as the first phase to run.
`--verification MODE` accepts `off` | `plan` | `required` (default `required`).
`--test-plan FILE` sets the TEST_PLAN.md projection path (default `<workdir>/testautomation/<slug>/TEST_PLAN.md` when verification is not `off`).
`--verification-commands FILE` names a JSON document of phase-scoped commands the gates must execute; passed to `verification_plan.py create --verification-commands`.
`--generate-tests DIR` sets the absolute directory for test scaffolds (default `<workdir>/testautomation/<slug>/generated` when verification is not `off`).
`--telemetry` turns Loki shipping of the event stream on (off by default).
`--loki-url URL` sets the Loki base URL (default `http://localhost:3100`).
`--otel` turns OTLP shipping on (off by default), independent of `--telemetry`.
`--otel-url URL` sets the OTLP/HTTP base URL (default `http://localhost:4318`).
`--live` forces the inline scrolling timeline in this terminal (`LIVE=true`).
`--no-live` forces the raw tee'd output even on a TTY (`LIVE=false`).
`--debug` sets `DEBUG=true`, which adds `--debug` to every `proposer.sh` and `critic.py` invocation (retains raw prompt/response under `<feature-dir>/debug/invocations/`).
`--long-job-phase N` names the phase that owns a long-running detached command.
`--long-job-cmd CMD` is the shell command launched detached (via `bash -c`) before each attempt of the long-job phase.
`-h|--help` prints the usage text to stdout and exits 0 before any state is touched.
`SPECSTRIDE_SPEC_FORMAT` (default empty = auto-detect) forces the spec grammar; overridden by `--spec-format`.
`SPECSTRIDE_FEATURE` (default empty) is the explicit feature slug; overridden by `--feature`.
`SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER` sets the proposer backend; built-in default `dsh`.
`SPECSTRIDE_CRITIC` sets the critic backend; built-in default `claude`.
`SPECSTRIDE_MAX_REJECTS` (default 3) is the per-phase attempt limit; overridden by `--max-rejects`.
`SPECSTRIDE_MAX_ITER` (default 30) is the proposer pass limit per phase attempt; overridden by `--max-iter`.
`SPECSTRIDE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED` (default `false`) enables Loki shipping; only the literal `true` enables it.
`SPECSTRIDE_LOKI_URL` sets the Loki base URL; built-in default `http://localhost:3100`.
`SPECSTRIDE_OTEL_ENABLED` (default `false`) enables OTLP shipping.
`SPECSTRIDE_OTEL_URL` sets the OTLP/HTTP base URL; default `http://localhost:4318`.
`SPECSTRIDE_LIVE` (`auto` | `true` | `false`, default `auto`) controls the inline live timeline; overridden by `--live` / `--no-live`.
`SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_TIMEOUT` (default 1800 seconds) is the global per-pass ceiling; overridden by `--proposer-timeout`.
`SPECSTRIDE_CRITIC_TIMEOUT` (default 300 seconds) is the per-call critic limit, also used for the diagnostician call.
`SPECSTRIDE_CRITIC_MALFORMED_LIMIT` (default 3, `0` disables, no flag) is the number of consecutive MALFORMED verdicts that halts the run.
`SPECSTRIDE_MAX_WALL_MIN` (default 0 = unlimited, no flag) is the whole-run wall-clock budget in minutes.
`SPECSTRIDE_GIT_COMMITS` (default `auto`, no flag) enables per-phase git checkpoints; any value other than `auto` disables them.
`SPECSTRIDE_VERIFICATION` (default `required`) sets the verification mode; overridden by `--verification`.
`SPECSTRIDE_TEST_PLAN` (default empty) sets the TEST_PLAN.md path; overridden by `--test-plan`.
`SPECSTRIDE_VERIFICATION_COMMANDS` (default empty) names the declared-commands JSON document; overridden by `--verification-commands`.
`SPECSTRIDE_GENERATE_TESTS` (default empty) sets the scaffold directory; a non-empty value also upgrades verification `off` to `plan`.
`SPECSTRIDE_LONG_JOB_PHASE` (default empty) names the long-job phase; overridden by `--long-job-phase`.
`SPECSTRIDE_LONG_JOB_CMD` (default empty) is the long-job shell command; overridden by `--long-job-cmd`.
The orchestrator exports the unprefixed `LONG_JOB_PHASE` and `LONG_JOB_CMD` so `proposer.sh` can call `ensure_long_job` from its own per-pass loop.
Every set shell variable named `SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_TIMEOUT_PHASE_<N>` is read as a per-phase pass ceiling for phase N (value = positive integer seconds).

The `SPECSTRIDE_<BACKEND>_OVERLAY` scope knob is validated at startup by `backend_overlay.py scope <proposer-backend> --quiet`; an invalid value or registry declaration ends the run before any attempt.
The resolved spec format is exported as `SPECSTRIDE_SPEC_FORMAT` once per run, so the spec shims, `proposer.sh` and `critic.py` all use the same adapter and never re-sniff mid-run.
The orchestrator exports `LOCK_FD` (the flock file-descriptor number, empty under the mkdir fallback) so child processes can close their inherited copy before backgrounding a detached job.
`SPECSTRIDE_BACKEND_LABEL` has the shape `prop:<proposer-backend>/crit:<critic-backend>` and becomes the `backend` field of every lifecycle event.
`SPECSTRIDE_TRACE_ID` is an optional inbound distributed-trace id, passed through untouched (never synthesised) and added to every emitted event as `trace_id` when set.

The orchestrator exports `SPECSTRIDE_EVENTS` (the run's events.jsonl path), `SPECSTRIDE_RUN_ID`, `SPECSTRIDE_TASK` (basename of the workdir), `SPECSTRIDE_BACKEND_LABEL` and `SPECSTRIDE_SHIP` (path of `lib/ralph_loki_ship.py`) to proposer and critic.

The orchestrator exports `SPECSTRIDE_TELEMETRY`, `SPECSTRIDE_LOKI_URL`, `SPECSTRIDE_OTEL_SHIP` (path of `lib/ralph_otel_ship.py`), `SPECSTRIDE_OTEL_ENABLED` and `SPECSTRIDE_OTEL_URL` with the resolved (flag-applied) values.
The orchestrator exports `SPECSTRIDE_FEATURE` (the resolved sanitised slug), `SPECSTRIDE_TRACE_ID` and `SPECSTRIDE_MAX_REJECTS` (the resolved limit) to child processes.
When running as root (EUID 0) with `IS_SANDBOX` unset or empty, the orchestrator exports `IS_SANDBOX=1` and logs `  note     : root + IS_SANDBOX unset -> auto-set IS_SANDBOX=1`.
The orchestrator exports `SPECSTRIDE_RUN_START_EPOCH` (run start, epoch seconds) and `SPECSTRIDE_MAX_WALL_MIN` so `proposer.sh` can enforce the wall-clock budget inside a yield wait.
`SPECSTRIDE_BANNER_BG` is, when unset and stdout is a TTY, detected once with `lib/theme.py bg` and exported for `banner.py` and the backgrounded presenter.
`SPECSTRIDE_DIAGNOSTICIAN` (default `true`) enables the diagnostician; any value other than `true` disables it.
The diagnostician call runs `critic.py` with `SPECSTRIDE_ROLE=diagnostician` in its environment.
`SPECSTRIDE_ACCELERATOR` (default `true`) enables the accelerator attempt; any value other than `true` disables it.
`SPECSTRIDE_ACCELERATOR_BACKEND` (default empty = the proposer backend) selects the backend used for accelerator passes.
`SPECSTRIDE_OSC_MAX` (default 2) is the oscillation threshold: the run halts when one criterion reappears more than this many times.
`SPECSTRIDE_PROMPT_MAX_BYTES` (default 180000; `0` disables the budget) is the byte budget of the assembled proposer/accelerator prompt applied when appending budgeted blocks.
`SPECSTRIDE_PROMPT_PROTECTED_BLOCKS` (comma-separated, default `yield_contract`; set-but-empty protects nothing) lists prompt blocks that are kept even over budget.
`SPECSTRIDE_LEARNING=apply` is the only value under which learned `proposer_timeout` / `yield_poll_interval` decisions are applied at run time (via `learn.py resolve`).
`SPECSTRIDE_YIELD_POLL`, when set at all (set-ness, not value), is treated as an operator override of the yield poll interval with source `override`.
Any non-empty `SPECSTRIDE_LEARNING` value other than `off` turns the learning layer on: tamper bracket, `learn.py observe` and `learn.py evaluate` at phase_done, and the exit summary.
The resolved poll interval is passed to `proposer.sh` as a one-command `SPECSTRIDE_YIELD_POLL=` prefix and is deliberately not exported, so it never reads as an operator override at the next phase.
Each critic call is given `SPECSTRIDE_ROLE=critic` and `SPECSTRIDE_ITERATION=0` as a per-subprocess environment prefix (never exported, so it cannot leak into the next proposer pass).
Each critic call gets `SPECSTRIDE_INVOCATION_ID=<run-id>-critic-phase-<N>-attempt-<A>` and `SPECSTRIDE_INVOCATION_DIR` pointing at its artifact directory.
`SPECSTRIDE_TICK_TASKS` (default `true`) – the literal `false` turns off ticking of task checkboxes after approval.
Event `gates_migrated` with fields `count` (items moved) and `dir` (the `features/default` directory), emitted only when at least one item was migrated.
Event `progress_swept` with fields `from` (stray path) and `to` (canonical path).

Event `run_start` with fields `workdir`, `phases` (count), `feature`, `proposer`, `critic`, `resume` (phase number or `done`), `states` (comma-separated rail letters), `verification` (mode), `verification_plan` (path).
Event `verification_release_passed` with field `evidence`.
Event `git_checkpoint` with field `phase`, emitted only when the commit succeeded.
Event `diagnostician_trigger` with fields `phase`, `attempt`.
Event `attempt_archived` with fields `phase`, `attempt`, `dir`.
Event `prompt_block_protected` with fields `block`, `assembled_bytes`, `block_bytes`, `budget_bytes`.
Event `prompt_block_dropped` with fields `block`, `assembled_bytes`, `block_bytes`, `budget_bytes`.
Event `phase_start` with fields `phase`, `title`, `total` (phase count), `shape` (phase shape digest, empty if unreadable).
Event `accelerator_start` with fields `phase`, `attempt`, `backend`, `criteria` (signature without trailing comma).
Event `proposer_start` with fields `phase`, `attempt`, `backend`.

Event `proposer_cap` with fields `phase`, `attempt`, `role`, `seconds`, `source`, `arm`, `yield_poll`, `yield_poll_source`, `yield_poll_arm`, `tamper_bracket` (`on` or empty), emitted before every proposer/accelerator pass.
Event `events_tampered` with fields `phase`, `attempt`, `file`, emitted when a bracketed file shrank or its pre-pass bytes changed.
Event `acceleration_note` with fields `phase`, `attempt`, `note` (path of `GATE<N>-ACCELERATION.md`).
Event `verification_start` with fields `phase`, `attempt`, `plan`.
Event `verification_failed` with fields `phase`, `attempt`, `rc`, `evidence`.
Event `verification_passed` with fields `phase`, `attempt`, `evidence`.
Event `phase_done` with fields `phase`, `attempt`, `title`.
Event `tasks_ticked` with fields `phase`, `count`.
Event `learning_observed` with fields `phase`, `path`.
Event `reject` with fields `phase`, `attempt`; emitted for REJECTED, MALFORMED and deterministic-gate failures alike.
Event `critic_malformed` with fields `phase`, `attempt`, `streak`, `limit`.
Event `gate_oscillation` with fields `phase`, `attempt`, `criterion`, `reappears`.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 on an unknown argument, after printing `orchestrator.sh: unknown arg: <arg>` and the usage text to stderr.

`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 with `orchestrator.sh: <source> must be N=SECONDS with positive integers (got '<spec>')` when a `--proposer-timeout-phase` value or a `SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_TIMEOUT_PHASE_<N>` variable is not `<digits>=<digits greater than 0>`.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 with stderr `workdir not found: <dir>` when the `-w` directory does not exist.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 1 when it cannot `cd` into the workdir.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 with `orchestrator.sh: --verification must be off, plan, or required (got: <value>)` on any other mode value (flag or env).
`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 when `--generate-tests` / `SPECSTRIDE_GENERATE_TESTS` is not an absolute path.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 when `--test-plan` is a relative path; the check is skipped entirely when verification is `off`.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 when `backend_overlay.py scope` returns non-zero (invalid overlay value or declaration); this check runs before spec resolution and before the lock is taken.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 for every spec-resolution failure (no match, unknown feature, ambiguous candidates).
`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 with `spec not found: <path> (pass -s FILE — any name/location)` when the resolved or explicit spec path is not a regular file.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 1 with `python3 required on PATH` when `python3` is missing (checked after spec resolution, which itself already calls python3).
`orchestrator.sh` exits 5 when `flock -n` on the lock file fails.

`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 with `orchestrator.sh: invalid spec (see errors above): <spec>` when `specstride_spec.py validate` fails (zero phases, duplicate or non-contiguous numbers, a phase without criteria).
`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 with `orchestrator.sh: --verification-commands not found or empty: <path>` when the document is missing or zero bytes.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 with `orchestrator.sh: verification preflight failed (see <run.log>)` when `verification_plan.py create` returns non-zero; its output goes to `run.log` only.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 when a `phaseTimeouts` entry is not `<digits>` mapped to positive integer seconds.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 2 when the release verification gate fails, both after the last phase and on the already-all-approved path.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 0 when all phases were already approved at start (and release verification passed or was not required).
`orchestrator.sh` exits 6 when `stop.flag` exists at the top of an attempt; the flag is deleted first so a rerun resumes.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 4 when its own wall-clock budget is exceeded at the top of an attempt.
Proposer exit 6 maps to orchestrator exit 6; the orchestrator deletes `stop.flag`; this is checked before the evidence test, so it wins even if evidence exists.
Proposer exit 4 (max-iter without evidence) maps to orchestrator exit 4.
Proposer exit 8 (consecutive no-progress passes) maps to orchestrator exit 4.
Proposer exit 7 (consecutive agent errors / watchdog kills) maps to orchestrator exit 4.
Proposer exit 9 (yield budget, yield deadline or wall clock spent during a yield) maps to orchestrator exit 4.
Proposer exit 10 (consecutive hard-cap kills) maps to orchestrator exit 4.
Any other proposer exit without evidence (including 0, 1 and 3) maps to orchestrator exit 1.
Critic exit 3 (config/usage error) maps to orchestrator exit 3.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 1 when the consecutive MALFORMED limit is reached.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 2 when a phase is detected as oscillating.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 2 when a phase reaches `MAX_REJECTS` rejected attempts.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 0 after every phase from the start phase on was approved in this run.
`run_stop reason=release_verification` with fields `rc` (gate exit status) and `evidence` (release.json path).
`run_end outcome=all_approved` on the already-approved path carries no `phases` field.
`run_stop reason=stop_flag` with field `phase` when `stop.flag` is found at the top of an attempt.
`run_stop reason=wall_budget` with field `phase`.
`run_stop reason=stop_flag` with field `phase` is also emitted when the proposer itself exited 6.
`run_stop reason=proposer_max_iter` with field `phase`.
`run_stop reason=proposer_no_progress` with field `phase`.
`run_stop reason=proposer_consecutive_errors` with field `phase`.
`run_stop reason=proposer_yield_budget` with field `phase`.
`run_stop reason=proposer_cap_exhausted` with field `phase`.
`run_stop reason=proposer_no_evidence` with fields `phase`, `rc` (the proposer exit status).
`run_stop reason=critic_config` with field `phase`.
`run_stop reason=critic_unavailable` with fields `phase`, `attempts`, `streak`.
`run_stop reason=gate_oscillation` with fields `phase`, `attempts`.
`run_stop reason=max_rejects` with fields `phase`, `attempts`.
`run_end outcome=all_approved phases=<count>` is emitted after the last phase is approved and release verification passed.
`<install-dir>/.env` (next to `orchestrator.sh`) is sourced with `set -a` when present, as a source of defaults.
All durable per-feature state lives under `<workdir>/<state-dir>/features/<slug>/`.
Unless verification is `off`, the human-readable plan defaults to `<workdir>/testautomation/<slug>/TEST_PLAN.md`.
Unless verification is `off`, generated test scaffolds default to `<workdir>/testautomation/<slug>/generated`, so `--generate-tests` is always passed to the plan creator in `plan`/`required` mode.
The canonical verification plan is written per run to `<feature-dir>/runs/<run-id>/verification/verification-plan.json`.
The single-run lock file is `<workdir>/<state-dir>/lock`, held with a non-blocking exclusive `flock` on an open file descriptor for the life of the process.
On acquiring the flock the orchestrator writes the owner line `<run-id> <ISO-8601 time>` into the lock file; the file itself is never deleted on exit.
Without the `flock` binary the lock is the directory `<state-dir>/lock.d` created with `mkdir`; failure to create it exits 5.
Under the mkdir fallback the owner line `<run-id> <ISO time>` is written to `<state-dir>/lock.d/owner`.
At start the orchestrator creates `<feature-dir>/runs/<run-id>/`, `verdicts/`, `attempts/`, `debug/`, `gates/proofs/` and `runs/<run-id>/verification/`.
`<run-dir>/run.log` and `<run-dir>/events.jsonl` are created empty (truncated) at start.
`<state-dir>/run.log` is a symlink retargeted (`ln -sfn`) to the relative path `features/<slug>/runs/<run-id>/run.log`.
`<state-dir>/events.jsonl` is a symlink retargeted to the relative path `features/<slug>/runs/<run-id>/events.jsonl`.
`<feature-dir>/last-run.conf` is overwritten at every run start with the resolved configuration.
`<state-dir>/last-run.conf` (the active-feature pointer for a bare resume) is overwritten at every run start with the same content.
`<state-dir>/stop.flag` is the stop request file; the orchestrator deletes it when it honours it.
Release-gate evidence is written to `<feature-dir>/runs/<run-id>/verification/release.json`.
`gates/.diagnosed-phase<N>` is overwritten with the signature after every diagnostician call, whether or not the call succeeded or wrote a hint.

After an accelerator pass the orchestrator writes `gates/GATE<N>-ACCELERATION.md`: header `# Phase <N> — accelerator pass (attempt <M>)`, the criteria acted on, the list of files that pass changed (lines new in the after-snapshot) and the accelerator's own notes.
An optional agent-written `gates/GATE<N>-ACCELERATOR-NOTE.md` is appended to the acceleration note under `## The accelerator's own notes` and then deleted.
A rejected attempt is archived to `<feature-dir>/attempts/phase<N>/attempt<M>/`.
The yield artifact path told to the agent is `<feature-dir>/yield/phase<N>-attempt<M>-<run-id>.json`.
The prompt handed to the agent is written to `<feature-dir>/proposer-prompt.phase<N>.txt` or `<feature-dir>/accelerator-prompt.phase<N>.txt`, overwritten at every attempt.
`gates/.accelerated-phase<N>` is written with the signature before the accelerator pass starts, so an interrupted accelerator pass is never repeated for the same signature.

Around an accelerator pass the orchestrator writes `<run-dir>/accelerator/phase<N>-attempt<M>.before` and `.after`: sorted `git diff --numstat HEAD` lines plus untracked files (`<path>\tnew`); empty files outside a git work tree.
Phase-gate evidence is written to `<feature-dir>/runs/<run-id>/verification/phase-<N>-attempt-<M>.json`.

On a gate failure the orchestrator itself writes `gates/GATE<N>-FEEDBACK.md`, starting `# Phase <N> deterministic verification gate rejected`, with a `## What actually failed` digest from `verification_failure_digest.py` (or `(failure digest unavailable — read the evidence document below)`) and a `## References` section naming the plan and evidence paths.
The critic's artifact directory is `<feature-dir>/debug/invocations/<run-id>/critic/phase-<N>/attempt-<A>/iter-0/<invocation-id>/`.

On approval any leftover `GATE<N>-FEEDBACK.md`, `GATE<N>-HINT.md` and `GATE<N>-ACCELERATION.md` are moved into `<feature-dir>/attempts/phase<N>/approved/` (overwriting an earlier approval's copies) so they cannot leak forward.
On approval the markers `gates/.diagnosed-phase<N>` and `gates/.accelerated-phase<N>` are deleted; the approved `GATE<N>-EVIDENCE.md` stays in the gates directory.
With the learning layer on, `learn.py observe --events <feature-dir>/runs --phase N [--phase-shape] --out <feature-dir>/learning/phase-<N>.json` writes one observation after each approved phase.
The usage text documents that each agent invocation records a capability mode (structured / raw-text / degraded) and that `SPECSTRIDE_AGENT_STREAM=false` forces the raw-text fallback.
The usage text substitutes `@PROPOSER_BACKENDS@` / `@CRITIC_BACKENDS@` with the backend list printed by `lib/backends.py display --role <role>`, so help always reflects the registry.
When `--feature` matches no candidate the orchestrator prints `spec not found: no feature/change '<feature>' tasks.md under <workdir>` and exits 3 without listing the locations tried.

With several candidates and no `--feature` the orchestrator prints `multiple feature specs found under <workdir> — disambiguate (nothing auto-selected):` followed per candidate by its path and the two `→ specstride run -w … -s …` / `--feature …` forms, then exits 3.
With nothing resolved the orchestrator prints `spec not found: no spec resolved for <workdir> (pass -s FILE — any name/location).` and a `tried:` list of the four locations.
A lost lock prints `orchestrator.sh: another run holds the lock on <workdir> (<lock path>). Exiting.` to stderr.
Log line `----- migrated <n> stray control item(s) into features/default/ -----`.
Log line `----- swept stray PROGRESS.md (<from>) into <to> -----`.
At start the banner from `lib/banner.py --phases <count> --states <list>` is printed to the terminal only when stdout is a TTY; a `--plain` copy is always appended to `run.log`.
If `lib/banner.py` is missing the fallback title `specstride: from specs to tested code` is printed to stdout and `run.log`.
A plain rail (`banner.py --rail-only --plain`) is appended to `run.log` at each approved phase, each critic-judged rejection, every `run_stop` and at run end.

Log line `>>> stop.flag detected during proposer — halting cleanly (exit 6; rerun resumes).`.
Log line `>>> proposer hit max-iter (<n>) without evidence for phase <N> — halting (exit 4).`.
Log line `>>> proposer made no progress for phase <N> — halting (exit 4).` followed by `#` guidance lines pointing at `PROGRESS.md` and `specstride resume -w <workdir>`.

Log line `>>> proposer aborted on consecutive agent errors for phase <N> — halting (exit 4).` followed by guidance naming `pass-checkpoints` and the `SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_TIMEOUT` / `_MAX_ERRORS` / `_REPEAT_LIMIT` / `_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT` remedies.
Log line `>>> proposer's yield budget is spent for phase <N> — halting (exit 4).` followed by guidance naming `<feature-dir>/yield-jobs/` and `--proposer-timeout-phase`.
Log line `>>> proposer hit the pass ceiling repeatedly for phase <N> — halting (exit 4).` followed by guidance preferring a long job or a phase split over raising the ceiling.
Log line `>>> proposer exited (<rc>) without writing evidence for phase <N> — internal error.`.
Log line `----- verification: phase <N> attempt <M> (fixed argv) -----`.
Log line `----- critic: phase <N> attempt <M> (<critic backend>) -----`.
Log line `===== PHASE <N> APPROVED (attempt <M>) =====`.
Log lines `      ticked <n> task checkbox(es) of phase <N> in <spec>` or `      WARN: could not tick phase <N> task checkboxes in <spec> (approval stands)`.
Log line `>>> critic config/usage error (exit 3) — halting.`.
Log line `----- phase <N> REJECTED on attempt <M>/<MAX_REJECTS> -----`.
Log line `>>> critic returned no usable verdict (MALFORMED <streak>/<limit>)`.
Halt banner framed by `####…` lines: `# HALT — the critic is not answering (exit 1).` with the critic backend, timeout and three resume options.
Halt banner framed by `####…` lines: `# HALT — phase <N> is OSCILLATING (exit 2). Not converging.` with the criterion, reappearance count and attempt-history path.

Halt banner framed by `####…` lines: `# HALT — phase <N> exceeded MAX_REJECTS (<n>). Human needed.` with `latest evidence`, `latest feedback`, optional `diagnostician hint` and `acceleration note`, `attempt history` and a `rejection trail:` of one gist line (100 characters) per archived attempt.
Final log line `# DONE — all <n> phase(s) approved. <ISO time>`.

Precedence is built-in defaults < `.env` < caller-exported environment < flags: the caller's exported environment is snapshotted with `export -p` before `.env` is sourced and re-asserted afterwards, so a caller-exported variable beats `.env`.
After `.env` is sourced the legacy-name mapping runs a second time, so a `.env` that still uses `WIGGUM_*` names is mapped like the caller environment.
Every value-taking flag reads its value with `${2:?}`, so a flag given without a value aborts the shell with a bash parameter error (non-zero exit, not the documented exit 3).

The per-phase flag values are applied after the per-phase environment variables into the same map, so `--proposer-timeout-phase` wins over `SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_TIMEOUT_PHASE_<N>` for the same phase, and a later repeated flag wins over an earlier one.
A relative `-s` path is resolved against the directory the command was launched from (captured before `cd` into the workdir), not against the workdir; an absolute path is kept as is.
Supplying a generate-tests directory while verification is `off` silently upgrades the mode to `plan`.
Spec resolution step 1: `<workdir>/SPECS.md` wins whenever it exists and `-s` was not given, even when `--feature` is set.
Spec resolution step 2: `.specify/feature.json` is parsed as JSON and its `feature_directory` (relative values resolved against the workdir) yields `<dir>/tasks.md`.
If `feature.json` is unparseable, has no `feature_directory`, or that directory has no `tasks.md`, resolution silently falls through to the glob discovery step instead of failing.
Spec resolution step 3 collects candidates from `<workdir>/specs/*/tasks.md` then `<workdir>/openspec/changes/*/tasks.md`; exactly one candidate is used.
With `--feature`, the first candidate whose parent directory basename equals the raw feature value is selected; the comparison uses the unsanitised value.
The spec path is canonicalised to an absolute path (physical directory + basename) before it is handed to `proposer.sh`, `critic.py` and `last-run.conf`.
When no format is forced the format is auto-detected once via `specstride_spec.py detect`; if detection fails the orchestrator falls back to `native` instead of failing.
An explicit feature value is sanitised to a slug by replacing every character outside `A-Za-z0-9._-` with `-` and stripping leading/trailing `-`; an empty result becomes `default`.
Without an explicit feature the slug comes from `specstride_spec.py feature-slug` (Spec Kit feature or OpenSpec change directory basename), falling back to `default` on failure or empty output.
The run id is `<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>-<orchestrator pid>`.
The lock is acquired before the run directory, the root symlinks and `last-run.conf` are written, so a launch that loses the lock leaves the live run's log/event pointers and saved config untouched.
End-of-run work (lock-dir release, presenter stop, learning summary) is registered as a chain of EXIT hooks run in registration order, each failure ignored.

The mkdir-fallback lock is released by an EXIT hook that runs `rmdir lock.d`; because `lock.d/owner` is never removed first, the `rmdir` of the non-empty directory fails silently and the fallback lock stays behind.
Migration (3): a flat pre-v2 `<state-dir>/{gates,attempts,verdicts,debug,runs}` tree and `<state-dir>/PROGRESS.md` are moved once into `features/default/`.
When a migration target already exists the target wins: source entries with a name already present in the target are deleted (`rm -rf`), the others are moved.
Migration (1): `GATE*-EVIDENCE.md`, `GATE*-APPROVED` and `GATE*-FEEDBACK.md` at the workdir root are moved to `features/default/gates/` (deleted if already there).
Migration (2): a `PROGRESS.md` under `features/default/gates/` or at the workdir root is moved to `features/default/PROGRESS.md` (deleted if one already exists).

At each phase start a stray `PROGRESS.md` in the gates directory or the workdir root is swept to `<feature-dir>/PROGRESS.md`: newest file wins (the stray is deleted if the canonical copy is newer, otherwise it replaces it).

`last-run.conf` is a sourceable file of `KEY=<%q-escaped value>` lines with two comment header lines; keys: WORKDIR, SPECS, SPEC_FORMAT, FEATURE (the sanitised slug), PROPOSER_BACKEND, CRITIC_BACKEND, MAX_REJECTS, MAX_ITER, PROPOSER_TIMEOUT, PROPOSER_TIMEOUT_PHASES, TELEMETRY, LOKI_URL, OTEL, OTEL_URL, VERIFICATION, TEST_PLAN, GENERATE_TESTS, VERIFICATION_PLAN, VERIFICATION_COMMANDS, LONG_JOB_PHASE, LONG_JOB_CMD, GIT_COMMITS, ORCHESTRATOR.

`PROPOSER_TIMEOUT_PHASES` holds only the operator overrides (flag/env), serialised as numerically sorted space-separated `N=SECONDS`; ceilings declared in the verification-commands document are not included.
`last-run.conf` records `VERIFICATION_PLAN` as this run's plan path and `VERIFICATION_COMMANDS` as the value before it is resolved to an absolute path (resolution happens later, at line 834).

`last-run.conf` does not persist CRITIC_TIMEOUT, CRITIC_MALFORMED_LIMIT, MAX_WALL_MIN, START_PHASE, LIVE or DEBUG, and a failed write is ignored; the file is written before spec validation and the verification preflight, so a run that then exits 3 has already replaced the saved config.
`log()` appends to `run.log` only in live mode and tees to stdout and `run.log` otherwise; `term()` always writes to stdout.
The rail state list has one letter per phase in spec order: `A` approved (`GATE<n>-APPROVED` exists), `R` rejected (`GATE<n>-FEEDBACK.md` exists, not approved), `C` the phase in flight, `P` pending.
Every halt goes through `emit_run_stop`: the `run_stop` event is emitted with its key/value fields, then a rail is appended to `run.log` with the phase named by the `phase` field in flight.
`LIVE=auto` resolves to `true` only when stdout is a TTY and `lib/present.py` exists, else `false`.
In live mode one background `present.py --events <events.jsonl> --mode timeline --follow` process renders the timeline; it is killed by an EXIT hook after a 0.6 s grace sleep.
Raw proposer, critic and verification-gate output goes to `run.log` only in live mode, and is tee'd to the terminal and `run.log` otherwise.

Unless verification is `off`, `verification_plan.py create --workdir --specs --format --output <TEST_PLAN> --json-output <plan.json>` runs before the loop; `--required` is added only in `required` mode and `--generate-tests <dir>` whenever the directory is set.
A relative verification-commands path is resolved against the launch directory; the document is only consulted when verification is not `off`.

An optional top-level `phaseTimeouts` object (`{"N": SECONDS}`) in the verification-commands document supplies declared per-phase pass ceilings; an unparseable document is silently treated as having none.
The wall-clock budget is ignored (never trips) when `SPECSTRIDE_MAX_WALL_MIN` is non-numeric or 0; otherwise it trips when whole elapsed minutes since start are greater than or equal to the limit.
The resume phase is derived from disk as the first phase lacking `GATE<N>-APPROVED` in the feature's gates directory (no stored counter).
Migration always targets the `default` feature regardless of the current slug, and runs before the resume phase is derived so migrated `GATE<N>-APPROVED` markers are honoured.
`--start-phase` replaces the derived phase without validation against the spec or the approval markers.
Release verification runs only in `required` mode: `verification_plan.py run --plan <plan.json> --specs <spec> --phase release --evidence-output <run-dir>/verification/release.json`.
When every phase is already approved the orchestrator runs release verification, logs the outcome, emits `run_end` and exits 0 without invoking proposer or critic.
A git checkpoint is made after an approved phase only when `GIT_COMMITS` is `auto`, the workdir is inside a git work tree and `git status --porcelain` is non-empty.
Because `git add -A` runs in the workdir, the checkpoint also commits the state directory (gates, run logs, events) unless the project ignores it.
The checkpoint runs `git add -A` then `git commit -q -m "specstride: phase <N> approved — <title or 'phase N'>"`; a failed commit is ignored silently (no log, no event).

The one-line gist of a feedback file is, in order: the first line matching `NOT (MET|VERIFIED|SUBSTANTIATED)` / `is not (met|verified|substantiated)` (case-insensitive), else the first ``- `FAILED …` `` / ``- `ERROR …` `` roster line, else the first non-heading non-blockquote line that is not `The following must be addressed…`; truncated to 160 characters.
The unmet-criteria signature is the sorted unique list of task IDs matching `T<2+ digits><optional lowercase letter>` in the feedback, joined with trailing commas.
For feedback with no task IDs the signature is `text:<sha256>` of the feedback with every `VERDICT <hex>:` line removed, so the per-call nonce does not make identical feedback look new.
The diagnostician runs after a rejection only when enabled, `GATE<N>-FEEDBACK.md` exists and its signature differs from the content of `gates/.diagnosed-phase<N>`.
The diagnostician call is `critic.py --workdir --specs --phase --attempt --provider <critic backend> --timeout <critic timeout> --format --feature <slug> --diagnose`; its exit status is ignored.

An accelerator attempt is due only when enabled, the previous attempt in this run was not an accelerator, `GATE<N>-HINT.md` and `GATE<N>-FEEDBACK.md` exist, `.diagnosed-phase<N>` is non-empty and differs from `.accelerated-phase<N>`.
The accelerator prompt points at the most recently modified archived `GATE<N>-EVIDENCE.md` under `attempts/phase<N>/*/` as the evidence to copy and splice.

The accelerator prompt includes only heading lines and lines naming an unmet task ID from the phase slice (the whole slice for a prose signature), the feedback, the hint as primary instruction, a footprint rule, the evidence contract, a splice-the-previous-evidence instruction, `This is attempt <M> of <MAX_REJECTS>` and the verification obligations for the unmet IDs only.

The kind of a critic verdict (`APPROVED` | `REJECTED` | `MALFORMED`) is read back from the last `verdict` event in this run's events.jsonl whose `phase` and `attempt` match, because the critic exit code is 10 for both REJECTED and MALFORMED.
Oscillation detection is skipped unless at least 4 feedback files exist for the phase (archived `attempts/phase<N>/attempt*/` plus the live one), counted before the run-start filter.
Oscillation detection only considers feedback files modified at or after this run's start time, so a resumed run starts a new convergence window.
Oscillation detection keys only on `T<2+ digits>[a-z]?` task IDs, so prose-only feedback (native or OpenSpec phases without such IDs) can never trip it.

A criterion oscillates when its ID goes present, absent, present again across the ordered feedback files more than `SPECSTRIDE_OSC_MAX` times (default: 3 reappearances needed); the detector prints `OSCILLATING <criterion> <count>`.
If the attempt directory already exists the archive goes to `attempt<M>-<run-id>` instead, never overwriting an earlier run's history.

Archiving moves `GATE<N>-EVIDENCE.md` out of the gates directory (so the proposer's file-existence gate is not satisfied by stale evidence) and copies `GATE<N>-FEEDBACK.md`, `GATE<N>-HINT.md` and `GATE<N>-ACCELERATION.md`, which stay live in the gates directory.
The newest `verdicts/phase<N>.attempt<M>.*.txt` transcript is copied into the archive as `verdict.txt`.

Both prompts carry an `## Evidence contract` block telling the agent to cite exact workdir-relative file paths, stage line-numbered proof slices under `<gates>/proofs/`, and how the critic's grounding snapshot works (anchored ±15-line excerpts, byte budget, no RPC method names as files).

A budgeted block (currently only `yield_contract`, appended last) is appended only if assembled bytes plus block bytes fit `SPECSTRIDE_PROMPT_MAX_BYTES`; an over-budget protected block is kept, an over-budget unprotected block is dropped; the rest of the prompt is never truncated by the orchestrator.

The prompt's yield contract block shows a `specstride-pass-yield/v1` JSON example (`reason`, `job.mode` launch/adopt, `resume_when.kind`, required `deadline_sec`, `on_resume`) and tells the agent to write it atomically and stop without evidence instead of waiting inside a pass; the `command` predicate is not advertised.

The proposer prompt tells the agent the workdir, the `PROGRESS.md` path under the feature state directory, the phase title, and to write evidence atomically (`.tmp` then `mv`) to `<state-rel>/gates/GATE<N>-EVIDENCE.md` only when the phase is truly done.

The criteria heading in the proposer prompt depends on the format: `## OpenSpec tasks to complete …`, `## Tasks to complete …` (speckit-tasks) or `## Acceptance criteria (the phase spec)` (native), followed by the full phase slice.
The proposer prompt (not the accelerator prompt) appends the rendered document-set context block and, unless verification is `off`, the phase's `verification_plan.py slice` block.

When `GATE<N>-FEEDBACK.md` exists the proposer prompt adds `## A PRIOR ATTEMPT WAS REJECTED — this is attempt <M> of <MAX_REJECTS>`, the full feedback, one gist line per archived attempt (anti-fixation digest), the hint if present and the acceleration note if present.

The pass ceiling of a phase is resolved once per phase: operator override (flag or env) first; else a learned value when `SPECSTRIDE_LEARNING=apply` and `learn.py resolve` reports arm `applied`; else the document's `phaseTimeouts` entry; else the global `--proposer-timeout`.

A learned value is used only if `learn.py resolve --knob proposer_timeout --phase --default --feature-dir --phase-shape` prints an integer and arm `applied`; the source is then `learned` and the arm `applied`, otherwise sources are `override` / `declared` / `global` with arm `baseline`.

The yield poll interval is resolved once per phase: operator-set `SPECSTRIDE_YIELD_POLL` (source `override`), else a learned `yield_poll_interval` under `apply` (source `learned`), else 30 seconds (source `default`).
On every exit (EXIT hook), when the learning layer is on and `<feature-dir>/learning/applied.json` exists, each line of `learn.py evaluate --report` is printed to stdout and appended to `run.log`.

The attempt counter is a local variable that starts at 1 for every phase in every orchestrator process; it is not persisted, so a resume restarts attempt numbering and gives the phase a full fresh `MAX_REJECTS` budget regardless of earlier rejections.

At phase start, if both `GATE<N>-EVIDENCE.md` and `GATE<N>-FEEDBACK.md` are present in the gates directory (left by a halted rejection), the evidence is archived under the attempt label `resume-<run-id>` (directory `attempts/phase<N>/attemptresume-<run-id>/`) before the proposer runs; the feedback stays for the repair prompt.

The previous-role memory is local to one `run_phase` call, so after a resume the first attempt may be an accelerator even if the last attempt before the stop was one (subject to the `.accelerated-phase<N>` marker).
The MALFORMED streak counter is local to one phase in one process: it starts at 0 on every phase and every resume.

The loop bound allows `MAX_REJECTS + 1` iterations but the halt test `attempt >= MAX_REJECTS` ends the run on the MAX_REJECTS-th rejection, so at most `MAX_REJECTS` attempts are made per phase per process.
The orchestrator tests `stop.flag` and the wall-clock budget only at the top of each attempt (before the proposer starts), not between proposer and critic.
Before every attempt the orchestrator calls `ensure_long_job` and then the prestage step, in that order, before building the prompt.

The accelerator pass is `proposer.sh` run with `--role accelerator`, the narrowed prompt and the accelerator backend (default the proposer backend); it consumes an attempt number like any other attempt.

`proposer.sh` is invoked with `--workdir`, `--evidence <gates>/GATE<N>-EVIDENCE.md`, `--prompt-file`, `--backend`, `--max-iter`, `--timeout <phase ceiling>`, `--yield-dir <feature-dir>/yield`, `--feature`, `--role`, `--phase`, `--attempt`, `--invocation-id`.
The proposer invocation id is `<run-id>-<role>-phase-<N>-attempt-<M>`.
With telemetry on the proposer gets `--stream-json --loki-url <url>`; with OTEL on `--stream-json --otel-url <url>`; with `--debug` it gets `--debug`.

With the learning layer on, the orchestrator records size and SHA-256 of `events.jsonl`, `learning/applied.json` and `learning/phase-<N>.json` before each pass and checks afterwards that those leading bytes are unchanged (appends allowed).

Proposer exit codes other than 6 are examined only when the evidence file is absent; if `GATE<N>-EVIDENCE.md` exists after the pass, any proposer exit status is ignored and the attempt proceeds to verification and critic.
Only in `required` mode does a deterministic gate run before the critic: `verification_plan.py run --plan --specs --phase <N> --evidence-output <run-dir>/verification/phase-<N>-attempt-<M>.json`.
A failing phase gate (non-zero exit) is treated as a rejection with synthetic critic status 10; the LLM critic is not called for that attempt, and the attempt counts toward `MAX_REJECTS`.

The critic is invoked as `python3 lib/critic.py --workdir --specs --phase --attempt --max-rejects --provider <critic backend> --timeout <critic timeout> --format <spec format> --feature <slug>` plus `--verification-plan` and `--debug` when applicable.

In `plan` and `required` mode the critic is passed `--verification-plan <plan.json>`; in `off` mode no plan is created, no slice is put in the prompt, no gate runs and the critic gets no plan argument.
A phase counts as approved only when the critic exited 0 and `gates/GATE<N>-APPROVED` exists; critic exit 0 without the marker is handled as a rejection.
After approval the phase's task checkboxes are ticked in the spec file via `specstride_spec.py tick` unless disabled or the format is `native`; a failure logs a WARN and the approval stands.

With the learning layer on, `learn.py evaluate` runs after each approved phase and writes its events into this run's stream; a failed observe or evaluate is logged (`#   (learning: … failed — continuing; the run is unaffected)`) and never undoes the approval.

Order after approval: archive leftovers, delete markers, `phase_done`, rail, tick tasks, learning observe, learning evaluate, git checkpoint; ticked checkboxes are therefore part of the checkpoint commit.
Any critic exit status other than 0-with-marker and 3 (10, a crash, a timeout status) is handled as a rejection of the attempt.
After a gate failure no new `verdict` event exists for the attempt, so the verdict lookup returns empty: no rail is logged and the MALFORMED streak is reset to 0.
The MALFORMED breaker is active only when the limit is greater than 0; each attempt whose newest verdict event is `MALFORMED` increments the streak and any other result resets it to 0.
A MALFORMED attempt below the limit still counts as an ordinary rejected attempt: it emits `reject`, may trigger the diagnostician, is archived and consumes one of the `MAX_REJECTS` attempts.
When the streak reaches the limit the attempt is archived before the halt, and the check precedes the diagnostician, oscillation and MAX_REJECTS checks.

The diagnostician also runs after a deterministic verification-gate rejection and on the final attempt before a MAX_REJECTS or oscillation halt; it does not run on the attempt that trips the MALFORMED limit.
On an oscillation halt the rejected attempt is archived first, so a later resume cannot resend the unchanged evidence to the critic.
After a rejection the run halts when the attempt number has reached `MAX_REJECTS`; otherwise the attempt is archived and the counter is incremented.

The halt banner's `HYPOTHESIS` is `TOOLING BLIND SPOT` (naming the `paths` of the last `grounding_gap` event) when this run's events.jsonl contains any `grounding_gap` event for any phase, otherwise `likely an under-specified acceptance criterion`.
On a MAX_REJECTS halt the final attempt is not archived: evidence and feedback stay in the gates directory and are archived as `resume-<run-id>` by the next run.

The driver runs `run_phase` for every spec phase numbered at or above the start phase, in spec order, without checking approval markers, so a later phase that already has `GATE<N>-APPROVED` is run again.
`specstride-digest.sh [output-path]` writes a short markdown digest of one live run; the single positional argument is the output path (default `/tmp/specstride-digest.md`).
The digest script reads `<state-dir>/proposer.pid` and `<state-dir>/critic.pid` to prefer the pid the loop currently owns.
The digest is written atomically: to `<output>.tmp`, then moved onto the output path.

The digest has the fixed sections `# specstride phase-8 digest — <time>`, `## processes`, `## loop`, `## watchdog kills / errors this run`, `## cycles job — section exit codes (last run)` and a static `## known-open defects (do not re-derive)` list.
Digest process lines read `- <script> RUNNING pid=<pid> etime=<elapsed>[ (+<n> stale/other)]` or `- <script> not running` for `orchestrator.sh`, `cycles_runner.sh`, `proposer.sh` and `critic.sh`.
The digest script prints `wrote <path> (<n> lines, <n> bytes)` to stdout.

The digest script is hard-wired to one workdir, one feature (`<machine-specific feature>`) and phase 8 (`GATE8-*`); it takes no workdir or feature option and reads the newest run directory by modification time.

The digest script depends on the `pass_killed`, `iter_error` and `iter_done` event names and their `iter`, `reason`, `subtype`, `consec` and `evidence` fields, and on `proposer pass <i>/<n>` lines in `run.log`.

Every shell variable named `WIGGUM_<X>` is copied to `SPECSTRIDE_<X>` and exported when `SPECSTRIDE_<X>` is unset (a set-but-empty new name still wins); this runs whenever `specstride-lib.sh` is sourced.
`SPECSTRIDE_STATE_NOTICE_SHOWN=1` is exported after the legacy-state-dir notice so child scripts (bash and python) do not repeat it.
`ensure_long_job` exports `SPECSTRIDE_LONG_JOB_LOG` with the long job's log path (or the still-alive prior run's log path) so the proposer prompt can point the agent at it.
Event `long_job_ended` with fields `phase`, `attempt`, `log`.
Event `long_job_start` with fields `phase`, `attempt`, `cmd`, `log`.
Event `prestage_done` with fields `phase`, `attempt`, `rc`, `summary`; a failing prestage never halts the run.
Events are appended to the file named by `SPECSTRIDE_EVENTS`; a failed write is ignored and nothing is written when the variable is empty.
Long-job state lives in `<feature-dir>/long-jobs/phase<N>-attempt<M>-<run-id>.{pid,log,done}`, scoped per attempt and per run because attempt numbers restart at 1 in every run.
Using the legacy state directory prints one stderr line `specstride: using legacy state dir <wd>/.wiggum (no .specstride/ there; it is not moved)` once per process tree.

Using a legacy variable prints one stderr line per process: `specstride: deprecated WIGGUM_* variables read as SPECSTRIDE_*: <names> (rename them)`; the bash shown-flag is not exported, so each child shell that maps a name prints it again.
When `lib/backends.py display` cannot run or prints nothing, help shows `(backend list unavailable: could not run lib/backends.py; see README "Configuration")` and the function still returns 0.
If the telemetry probe cannot run, the status line falls back to `<sink>: export configured (<url>)`.

Log lines `>>> long-job(phase <N> attempt <M>): launching detached — <cmd>` and `>>> long-job(phase <N> attempt <M>): process <pid> no longer running — treating as ended, NOT auto-restarting. See <log>`.
Log line `----- prestage: phase <N> attempt <M> (rc <rc>) — <summary> -----`.

State-dir resolution: the legacy directory `.wiggum` is used only when `<workdir>/.specstride/` is absent and `<workdir>/.wiggum/` exists; it is never moved or renamed; otherwise `.specstride` is used.
JSON escaping of event values escapes backslash, double quote, tab (`\t`) and newline (`\n`) and deletes carriage returns; other control characters are written raw.

Every bash-emitted event is one JSON object per line with `ts` (epoch seconds with nanoseconds), `time` (ISO-8601) and `event`, then `run_id`, `task`, `backend`, `feature`, `trace_id` when their variables are set, then the call's key/value pairs, all values as JSON strings.
Event key/value arguments are consumed in pairs; a trailing key without a value is silently dropped.
When `SPECSTRIDE_TELEMETRY` is `true` each event line is also piped to `$SPECSTRIDE_SHIP event --loki <url> --task --backend --run-id --event --json-stdin`, synchronously and best-effort.
When `SPECSTRIDE_OTEL_ENABLED` is `true` each event line is also piped to `$SPECSTRIDE_OTEL_SHIP event --otel <url> …`, independently of the Loki sink.
Every `specstride_spec_*` shim delegates to `lib/specstride_spec.py` and appends `--format $SPECSTRIDE_SPEC_FORMAT` when that variable is non-empty.
`specstride_spec_validate` prints `spec not found: <path>` and returns 1 for a missing file, otherwise prints the phase count on stdout and returns the parser's status.
A long job is managed only for the phase equal to `LONG_JOB_PHASE` and only when `LONG_JOB_CMD` is non-empty.
A long job with a `.done` marker for this run's attempt is never touched or relaunched.
If another run's pid file for the same phase and attempt names a live process, no second instance is launched and `SPECSTRIDE_LONG_JOB_LOG` points at that run's log.

If this run's pid file exists but the process is gone, the job is marked ended (empty `.done` file) and is never auto-restarted within the attempt; a new attempt or a new run launches a fresh instance.
The launching subshell closes its inherited copy of the workdir lock descriptor before starting the job, so a detached job never keeps the run lock held after the orchestrator exits.
An owned job is started in the given working directory with `setsid nohup`, stdin from `/dev/null`, stdout and stderr truncating the log file, and its pid written to the pid file.

`long_job_status_line` prints a prompt block headed `## Long-running verification job: DONE`, `STILL RUNNING (~<s>s so far)` or `launching now`, telling the agent not to re-run or wait on the job and to end the pass without evidence while it runs.

The prestage step runs `verification_plan.py prestage --plan --specs --phase --attempt` before each attempt in both `plan` and `required` mode; its last output line is the summary, and an empty summary or one starting `No pre-stage commands` produces no log and no event.
`wiggum` is a deprecated alias that `exec`s the `specstride` front door next to its resolved real path with all arguments unchanged.
`wiggum` prints `wiggum: this command was renamed to specstride; the alias will be removed in a future release` to stderr on every invocation.

Sourcing `wiggum-lib.sh` sources `specstride-lib.sh` and defines a `wiggum_<name>` forwarding function for every `specstride_<name>` function (helpers without that prefix such as `ensure_long_job` get no alias).
`.env.example` documents `SPECSTRIDE_DSH_PLUGIN_ALLOWLIST=` (empty, disabled) and that installed plugins persist in the dsh profile.
`.env.example` shows the overlay scope variable commented out, with `pass` as the documented default and exit 3 for any other value.
`.env.example` documents `SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_MAX_ERRORS=2` and says a non-erroring pass resets the count.
`.env.example` documents `SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_MAX_CAPS=3` (exit 10).
`.env.example` documents `SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_REPEAT_LIMIT=12` as the repetition threshold.
`.env.example` documents `SPECSTRIDE_YIELD_COUNTS_AS_ITER=false`: yield plus resume is one logical pass.

`.env.example` does not list `SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_MAX_NOPROGRESS`, `SPECSTRIDE_SHORT_PASS_SEC`, `SPECSTRIDE_SHORT_PASS_NUDGE_AFTER`, `SPECSTRIDE_YIELD_WAIT_EVERY`, `SPECSTRIDE_YIELD_LOG_HEAD/TAIL`, `SPECSTRIDE_FAILURE_LEDGER*` or `SPECSTRIDE_WATCHDOG_TICK`; its yield block ends at `SPECSTRIDE_YIELD_ALLOW_COMMAND`.
`backend_overlay.py scope <backend> [--quiet]`: print the scope word; `--quiet` suppresses the no-declaration warning.
`backend_overlay.py populate <backend> <dir> --scope pass|attempt --owner-pid N --workdir DIR`: fill an existing empty directory as an overlay.
`backend_overlay.py remove <root>`: remove one overlay tree; always exits 0.
`backend_overlay.py reap --owner-pid N [--scope S]`: remove one owner's overlays; always exits 0.
`backend_overlay.py sweep`: remove overlays whose owner is gone; always exits 0.
`backend_overlay.py startup <backend>`: sweep stale overlays, validate declarations, print the scope word on stdout.
`SPECSTRIDE_<BACKEND>_OVERLAY` (upper-cased registry name without qualifier) selects the overlay scope; no variable exists when the upper-cased name is not a valid shell identifier.
`backend_overlay.py populate` exits 1 on failure after printing `proposer.sh: could not create overlay for backend '<b>' in <dir>: <cause>`.
`backend_overlay.py` exits 3 when a declaration or scope value is invalid (`startup` and `scope` verbs), printing the error on stderr.
`<overlay>/specstride-overlay.json` is the marker (contract `specstride-overlay/v1`) written FIRST and atomically, with `backend`, `scope`, `owner_pid`, `owner_start`, `created_at`, `vars`.
One `0700` subdirectory per declared variable is created under the overlay root and the variable is set to that path for the harness.
Seed files are created with `O_EXCL` and mode `0600` (parents `0700`), and a seed whose resolved path escapes its variable directory is refused.
`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` is always set for the harness to `<overlay>/specstride-overlay.gitconfig`.
stderr warning `specstride: warning: <VAR> is set but backend '<b>' has no overlay; ignoring it` when a valid explicit scope is set for a backend with no declaration.
stderr line `specstride: removed stale overlay <root> (owner <pid> gone)` for each stale tree the startup sweep removes.
stderr warning `specstride: warning: could not remove overlay <root>: <cause>`, exactly one line per failed removal.
A missing or broken `lib/backends.py` degrades to an empty declaration table (scope `none` for every backend, exit 0), never to a traceback.
Overlay seed rule: content matching api key, secret, token, password, bearer or authorization (case-insensitive) is rejected as looking like a credential.

When a declaration overlays `HOME`, every XDG base directory variable (`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`) it does not itself overlay is explicitly unset for the harness.
Overlay declaration rule: the key must match `[a-z][a-z0-9]*` with no qualifier, and `dsh` may never declare an overlay because it keeps its own `DSH_HOME` overlay.
Overlay declaration rule: only the fields `vars` and `seeds` are allowed and `vars` must be a non-empty list of names matching `[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*` without duplicates.
Overlay declaration rule: a variable named `PATH`, `PWD`, `SHELL`, any `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*` identity variable, or anything starting with `SPECSTRIDE_` is reserved and rejected.
Overlay seed rule: each seed has exactly `var`, `path`, `content`; the path must be relative without `.`, `..` or empty parts; the var must be declared; duplicates are rejected.
The scope value is validated for EVERY backend: anything other than unset, empty, `pass` or `attempt` raises `<VAR>='<v>' is invalid; accepted values: pass, attempt`.
A backend without a declaration always resolves to scope `none`; a declared backend resolves to the variable's value, or `pass` when it is unset or empty.
An overlay owner is considered live when its pid exists (or `kill 0` raises EPERM) and the recorded process start time is null, unreadable or equal to the current one.

The operator's git identity is exported into the overlay environment as `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/EMAIL` and `GIT_COMMITTER_NAME/EMAIL`, resolved with `git config --get` (specific key, then `user.*`) in the real environment; an identity is never invented and an already exported variable is left alone.
Env file record order: every `unset` first, then one `set` per declared variable, then `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, then the git identity records.
A critic call's overlay ignores the scope variable: it is always created per call with scope word `critic` and removed when the call ends, even on exception.
Overlay removal retries each failing entry once after `chmod` and never raises; symlinks are unlinked, not followed.
Sweep and reap consider only real directories named `specstride-overlay.*` in the real temp dir that are owned by the current uid and carry a valid marker.
`reap` removes the given owner's overlays without a liveness check, optionally filtered by scope; `sweep` removes only overlays whose owner is no longer live.
`backends.py invocation-model --backend SPEC [--model M]` prints the invocation model or nothing; an unknown name exits 1.
`backends.py names --role proposer|critic` prints one backend name per line in registry order.
`backends.py stream --backend NAME` prints the entry's stream format (nothing when absent) and exits 0; an unknown name exits 1.
`backends.py names|display` require `--role` with choices `proposer` and `critic`.
`backends.py display --role <role>` prints one line: the spellings serving the role joined with ` | `.
A registry entry's `stream` field defaults to `None`, meaning raw text; no shipped entry sets it, so no backend is registry-routed to a stream adapter at this commit.
A registry entry's `overlay` field defaults to `None`; no shipped entry sets it.
The registry holds exactly five entries and registry order is display order; no entry named gemini, copilot, pi, opencode, openrouter or zai exists at this commit.
Registry entry `dsh` serves roles proposer and critic, each with an OPTIONAL qualifier labelled `provider/model` (spelling `dsh[:provider/model]`); it sets no `stream` and no `overlay`.
Registry entry `claude` serves proposer and critic with qualifier form `none` (spelling `claude`); no `stream`, no `overlay`.
Registry entry `codex` serves proposer and critic with qualifier form `none` (spelling `codex`); no `stream`, no `overlay`.

A locally registered backend (`<local-backend>`) serves the proposer with an OPTIONAL qualifier labelled `name` (spelling `<local-backend>[:name]`) and the critic with qualifier form `none`; no `stream`, no `overlay`.
Registry entry `prime` serves proposer and critic, each with an OPTIONAL qualifier labelled `variant` (spelling `prime[:variant]`); no `stream`, no `overlay`.
Qualifier spelling rule: form `none` renders `name`, `optional` renders `name[:label]`, `required` renders `name:label`.

Invocation model rule: an explicit `--model` is reported unless a qualifier is also present (then nothing is reported); a qualifier counts as a model only when the proposer qualifier label is `provider/model` (dsh only).

`dsh_plugin_requests.py` flags: `--request` and `--archive-dir` (required), `--allowlist`, `--dsh-bin` (default `dsh`), `--profile` (default `headless`), `--timeout` (default 600), each defaulting to its `SPECSTRIDE_DSH_*` variable.
`dsh_plugin_requests.py` exits 2 on any request error, printing `dsh plugin request: <cause>` on stderr, and 0 with the JSON result on stdout otherwise.
Installs are serialised with an exclusive `flock` on `<DSH_HOME>/profiles/<profile>/.specstride-plugin-install.lock`.
The receipt (contract `specstride-dsh-plugin-install/v1`) records `status=installed`, `profile`, `plugins`, `reason`, `requested_at`, `completed_at`, `request_archive`.
With no request file the processor prints `{"plugins": [], "status": "none"}` and exits 0.
The request must be a regular file, not a symlink, of at most 16384 bytes.
Request schema: keys must be EXACTLY `contract`, `plugins`, `reason`; `contract` must be `specstride-dsh-plugin-request/v1`.
`plugins` must hold 1 to 8 unique exact `package@semver` specs (optional npm scope, optional pre-release and build metadata); ranges, tags, URLs and paths do not match.
`reason` must be a non-empty string of at most 2048 bytes.
Every requested plugin must appear literally in the allowlist, otherwise the request is denied; allowlist entries themselves must be exact `package@semver` specs.
The installer command is `<dsh-bin> plugin --profile <profile> add --save-exact <plugins...>`, run as an argv array without a shell and with the configured timeout.
Kill reason to class table in the breaker module: `hard_cap` budget, `repeat_stall` futility, `progress_stall` futility, `idle_timeout` hang; unknown reasons default to futility.

An invocation's `result.json` is located by identity: `///phase-

/attempt-/iter-//result.json`, never by newest mtime.
Selecting the terminal event picks the `agent_result` record whose `invocation_id` equals the requested one, never the last record in the log.
A result whose `run_id`, `feature`, `role`, `phase` or `attempt` differs from the breaker scope is rejected with a `ValueError`.
A duplicate finalisation of the same invocation id is never counted twice.
The breaker charges one invocation to exactly one counter: a `budget` kill to the cap counter (error count untouched), anything else to the error counter (which also clears the cap streak).
The error breaker halts when `count >= limit`; the cap breaker halts only when `cap_limit > 0` and `cap_count >= cap_limit`.
`failure_ledger.py --log FILE --ledger FILE --job KEY [--max N] [--pattern RE]` prints a Markdown section for the resume prompt.
`SPECSTRIDE_FAILURE_PATTERN` overrides the failure-ledger line regex when `--pattern` is not passed.
`failure_ledger.py` always exits 0: any exception prints nothing and never breaks the resume prompt.
Ledger records: one `{"kind":"job","job","ts","log","failures"}` line per job and one `{"kind":"failure","job","sig"}` line per distinct signature; a job already in the ledger is not appended again.
Ledger section heading `### Every failure the job reported (<n> distinct, <m> matching lines in the whole log)`.
Each failure is listed as `- [NEW] <example>` or `- [RECURRING <k>/<n> earlier jobs] (x<count>) <example>`; recurring ones are sorted first.
Default failure pattern matches `FAIL`, `FAILED`, `FAILURE`, `ERROR` as whole words, `Traceback (most recent`, `RC=<non-zero>` and `exit [code] <non-zero>`.
Failure signatures strip timestamps, hex ids of 12+ chars, uuids and numbers, collapse whitespace and are cut to 300 chars; the example line is cut to 240 chars.
The whole log is scanned, not just the slice shown in the prompt, and failures are deduplicated by signature with a repeat count.
With no failure in the log, the section is printed (`None: no line of the log matched the failure pattern.`) only when earlier jobs exist; otherwise nothing is printed.
At most `--max` (default 150) failures are listed; the rest are summarised as `- ... <n> more distinct failure(s) not shown; grep the log for the rest`.
`proposer.sh --workdir DIR --evidence FILE --prompt-file FILE [options]` is the proposer entry point: it runs one fresh headless coding-agent pass per iteration until the evidence file exists.

`-w|--workdir DIR` (required): directory the agent operates in; must be an existing directory or the script prints `--workdir DIR required (got '...')` and exits 1; the script then `cd`s into it and uses `$PWD` as the canonical workdir.
`-e|--evidence FILE` (required): the gate file; empty value prints `--evidence FILE required` and exits 1; a relative path is resolved against the workdir and its parent directory is created.
`-f|--prompt-file FILE` (required): file whose contents are the standing prompt of every pass; a missing file prints `--prompt-file FILE required (got '...')` and exits 1.
`--backend NAME` selects the provider backend (default `$SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER`, else `dsh`); accepted spellings are rendered from the registry into the usage text.
`--model MODEL` sets the model id passed to the backend (no default; empty means the backend's own configured model).
`-n|--max-iter N` sets the maximum number of passes (default `$SPECSTRIDE_MAX_ITER`, else 30); the value is not validated as a number.
`-s|--sleep SECONDS` sets the sleep between passes (default 2; there is no environment variable for it).
`--timeout SECONDS` sets the absolute per-pass ceiling (hard cap), default `$SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_TIMEOUT` else 1800.
`--idle-timeout SECONDS` sets the idle (no cpu growth) watchdog, default `$SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_IDLE_TIMEOUT` else 900.
`--progress-timeout SECS` sets the disk-progress watchdog, default `$SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT` else 1800; 0 disables it.
`--progress-path PATH` (repeatable) restricts the disk-progress check to the given roots; explicit flags win over `SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_PROGRESS_PATHS`, and the default is the whole workdir.
`--repeat-limit N` sets the repetition watchdog threshold, default `$SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_REPEAT_LIMIT` else 12; 0 disables both repetition checks.
`--yield-dir DIR` sets where a pass declares a yield; default `<FEATURE_DIR>/yield`.
`-j|--stream-json` turns on the telemetry add-on; it requires `lib/ralph_loki_ship.py` and `python3` (else exit 1) and plays no part in the structured-stream routing decision.
`--feature NAME` (not listed in the usage text) sets `SPECSTRIDE_FEATURE`, which names the feature state directory.
`--role NAME` (not listed in the usage text) sets `SPECSTRIDE_ROLE` (default role `proposer`), used in invocation paths and events.
`--phase N` (not listed in the usage text) sets `SPECSTRIDE_PHASE` (default 0), used in yield, checkpoint and invocation names.
`--attempt N` (not listed in the usage text) sets `SPECSTRIDE_ATTEMPT` (default 1).
`--invocation-id ID` (not listed in the usage text) sets the invocation id base; each pass then uses `<ID>-iter-<n>` instead of a random `inv-<iter 6 digits>-<8 hex>` id.
`--loki-url URL` sets the Loki base URL and enables the Loki sink.
`--otel-url URL` sets the OTLP/HTTP base URL and enables the OTEL sink.
`--debug` retains each pass's `prompt.txt` and `response.txt` in that pass's invocation directory.
`-h|--help` prints the usage text on stdout and exits 0.
`SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER` is the default for `--backend`; default `dsh`.
`SPECSTRIDE_MAX_ITER` is the default for `--max-iter`; default 30.
`SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_TIMEOUT` is the default absolute per-pass ceiling in seconds; default 1800.
`SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_IDLE_TIMEOUT` is the idle watchdog threshold in seconds; default 900.
`SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT` is the disk-progress watchdog threshold in seconds; default 1800; 0 disables.
`SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_REPEAT_LIMIT` is the repetition watchdog threshold; default 12; 0 disables.

`SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_REPEAT_IGNORE` is an extended regex of command lines the process-level repetition counter skips; it is read with `-` (not `:-`), so an explicitly EMPTY value disables the built-in default and counts everything except `sleep`.
`SPECSTRIDE_LOKI_URL` is the default Loki base URL; default `http://localhost:3100`.
`SPECSTRIDE_OTEL_URL` is the default OTLP/HTTP base URL; default `http://localhost:4318`.
`SPECSTRIDE_AGENT_STREAM` (default `true`) turns the local stream tap on; `false` restores raw output; it is forced to `false` when `lib/agent_stream.py` or `python3` is missing.
`SPECSTRIDE_EVENTS` is the event stream path; default `<workdir>/<state dir>/events.jsonl`; it is exported to every child process.
`IS_SANDBOX=1` is exported when the effective uid is 0 and `IS_SANDBOX` is unset or empty, so that a root-run headless agent accepts the skip-permissions flag.
`SPECSTRIDE_BACKEND_LABEL` overrides the backend label used for telemetry and tap arguments; default is the `--backend` value.
`SPECSTRIDE_TASK` is the task name passed to the tap and shippers; default is the basename of the workdir.
`SPECSTRIDE_RUN_ID` is the run id; default `<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>-<pid>` generated by the proposer itself.
`SPECSTRIDE_FEATURE` names the feature; default `default`.
`SPECSTRIDE_ROLE` names the role recorded in invocation paths and events; default `proposer`.
`SPECSTRIDE_PHASE` is the phase number; default 0.
`SPECSTRIDE_ATTEMPT` is the attempt number; default 1.
`SPECSTRIDE_INVOCATION_ID` is the invocation id base for every pass; default empty (random id per pass).
`SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_PROGRESS_PATHS` is a colon-separated list of disk-progress roots, used only when no `--progress-path` flag was given.
`YIELD_DIR` from the environment is honoured as the yield directory when `--yield-dir` is not passed, because the variable is only defaulted when empty.
`SPECSTRIDE_DSH_PROVIDER` supplies the dsh provider for a model id without a `provider/` prefix; a different provider embedded in the model ref is a conflict error.
`DSH_HOME` (default `$HOME/.dsh`) is the real dsh home that is read, symlinked into the overlay and exported to the dsh process.
`SPECSTRIDE_DSH_REASONING_EFFORT`, when non-empty, is written as `reasoningEffort` into the dsh settings overlay.
`BACKEND_OVERLAY_MAKE_SCOPE` selects the `--scope` handed to `backend_overlay.py populate`; default `pass`; the startup path sets it to `attempt`.
`TMPDIR` (default `/tmp`) is where the prompt temp file, the dsh home overlay and the config-home overlay trees are created.
`SPECSTRIDE_DSH_BIN` names the dsh executable; default `dsh`.
`SPECSTRIDE_DSH_PROFILE` names the dsh profile passed as `--profile`; default `headless`.
`SPECSTRIDE_DSH_MODEL` is the dsh model reference used when `--model` is empty; it takes precedence over the `dsh:<qualifier>` part of the backend name.
`DSH_PERMISSION_MODE` is exported to the dsh process as `$SPECSTRIDE_DSH_PERMISSION_MODE`, else the inherited `$DSH_PERMISSION_MODE`, else `workspace-write`.
`SPECSTRIDE_PRIME_AGENT_BIN` names the bare `prime` backend executable; default `prime-agent`.
`SPECSTRIDE_PRIME_FLEET_BIN`, else legacy `SPECSTRIDE_PRIME_BIN`, names the `prime:<variant>` fleet launcher; default `prime`.
`SPECSTRIDE_<LOCAL_BACKEND>_BACKEND` names the inner backend of a locally registered backend when the `--backend` value carries no qualifier; default `<gateway>`.
`<LOCAL_BACKEND>_SH` is the path of the shell file that defines the locally registered backend's function; default is a fixed absolute path under `<machine-specific path>/`.
`SPECSTRIDE_WATCHDOG_TICK` is the watchdog poll interval in seconds; default 15.
`SPECSTRIDE_STDIN_FILE` names a file fed to the watched command on stdin; the claude arm sets it to the prompt temp file.
`SPECSTRIDE_YIELD_POLL` is the yield predicate poll interval in seconds; default 30.
`SPECSTRIDE_YIELD_MAX_PER_ATTEMPT` caps yields per proposer invocation; default 4; 0 disables the cap.
`SPECSTRIDE_YIELD_ALLOW_COMMAND` (default `false`) must be exactly `true` for the `command` resume predicate to be accepted.
`SPECSTRIDE_YIELD_COUNTS_AS_ITER` (default `false`): when not `true` a satisfied yield gives its iteration back.
`SPECSTRIDE_YIELD_WAIT_EVERY` (default 10): a `yield_wait` event is emitted every Nth poll tick; 0 disables the event.
`SPECSTRIDE_YIELD_LOG_HEAD` (default 40) is the number of leading job-log lines shown to the resuming pass.
`SPECSTRIDE_YIELD_LOG_TAIL` (default 80) is the number of trailing job-log lines shown to the resuming pass.
`SPECSTRIDE_FAILURE_LEDGER` (default `true`) enables the failure-ledger section in the yield resume block.
`SPECSTRIDE_FAILURE_LEDGER_MAX` (default 150) caps the number of distinct failures listed.
`SPECSTRIDE_MAX_WALL_MIN` (whole minutes, >0) together with `SPECSTRIDE_RUN_START_EPOCH` makes a yield wait end with outcome `wall_budget` once the run's wall-clock budget is spent.
`SPECSTRIDE_RUN_START_EPOCH` is the run start time the wall-budget check during a yield is measured from; when unset the check is skipped.
`SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_SKILLS=1` re-enables slash-command skills for the claude and locally registered backends; any other value adds `--disable-slash-commands`.
`SPECSTRIDE_AGENT_TAP` substitutes an executable for the built-in `python3 lib/agent_stream.py` adapter; it receives the same tap arguments.
`SPECSTRIDE_DSH_PLUGIN_ALLOWLIST` (comma-separated exact `package@semver` specs) enables the dsh plugin request protocol; empty disables it.
`SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_MAX_ERRORS` is the consecutive-error breaker limit; default 2.
`SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_MAX_CAPS` is the consecutive hard-cap breaker limit; default 3; on the legacy path 0 disables it.
`SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_MAX_NOPROGRESS` is the consecutive no-progress breaker limit; default 3; 0 disables it.
`SPECSTRIDE_SHORT_PASS_SEC` is the duration below which a clean pass without evidence or yield counts as short; default 180.
`SPECSTRIDE_SHORT_PASS_NUDGE_AFTER` is the number of consecutive short passes after which the next prompt carries the yield nudge; default 2; 0 disables.
`SPECSTRIDE_DSH_PLUGIN_TIMEOUT` is the plugin installer timeout in seconds; default 600.
`pass_killed` is emitted on every watchdog kill; fields: `iter`, `reason`, `class` (budget|futility|hang), `elapsed`, `detail`, `checkpoint` (file path).
`yield_invalid` is emitted for a refused yield; fields: `iter`, `reason`, `artifact`, and `log` for a launched job that never reported a pid.
`yield_job_start` is emitted when a job is launched or adopted; fields: `iter`, `mode` (launch|adopt), `pid`, `log`, `sid`, plus `argv` for launch.
`yield_wait` is emitted every `SPECSTRIDE_YIELD_WAIT_EVERY` ticks during the wait; fields: `iter`, `elapsed`, `predicate_kind`, `yield_index`.

`agent_observability` is emitted at the start of a prime pass running in raw-text mode; fields: `mode=raw-text`, `reason` (`structured schema unavailable — parsing plain output`), `role`, `supported_signals=text,result`.

`agent_observability` is also emitted per pass when a registry stream format exists but is not routed; fields: `mode=raw-text`, `reason` (the route reason), `role`, `provider_format`, `supported_signals=text,result`.
`evidence_present` is emitted when the evidence file already exists at startup; fields: `file` (basename of the evidence file), `iters` (`0`).
`iter_start` is emitted before each pass; fields: `iter`, `max_iter`.
`plugin_install_denied` fields: `iter`, `reason=allowlist_empty`.
`plugin_install_failed` fields: `iter`, `reason` (the processor's full output).
`plugin_installed` fields: `iter`, `profile`, `plugins` (comma-joined).
`pass_yield` is emitted when a yield is accepted; fields: `iter`, `reason`, `predicate_kind`, `deadline_sec`, `job_mode`, `job_log`, `yield_index`.
`yield_resume` is emitted when the predicate is satisfied; fields: `iter`, `waited_sec`, `job_rc` (or `unknown`), `job_duration_sec` (same value as `waited_sec`), `yield_index`, `predicate_kind`.
`yield_timeout` is emitted when a yield wait is abandoned; fields: `iter`, `reason` (`deadline` or `wall_budget`), `waited_sec`, `deadline_sec`, `predicate_kind`, `job_log`.
`evidence_written` is emitted when evidence appears after a pass; fields: `file` (basename), `iters` (the pass number).
`iter_short_pass` is emitted when the nudge is armed; fields: `iter`, `elapsed`, `consec`.
`iter_cap` is emitted for a hard-cap kill; fields: `iter`, `reason`, `elapsed`, `consec`, `max`.
`pass_cost_unknown` is emitted for a hard-cap kill because the severed stream reports no usage; fields: `iter`, `reason`, `elapsed`.
`iter_error` is emitted for an erroring pass; fields: `iter`, `subtype`, `consec`, `reason` (kill reason or `agent_error`), `kill_class` (kill class or `agent`).
`iter_no_progress` is emitted for each pass without disk progress; fields: `iter`, `consec`.
`iter_done` is emitted after a pass without evidence; fields: `iter`, `evidence=missing`; the yield variant adds `yielded=true` and `waited_sec`; the plugin variant adds `plugin_restart=true`.
proposer.sh exits 1 when `--workdir` is empty or not a directory.
proposer.sh exits 1 when `--evidence` is empty.
proposer.sh exits 1 when `--prompt-file` is empty or not a regular file.
proposer.sh exits 1 when it cannot `cd` into the workdir.
proposer.sh exits 1 when `-j` is given and `lib/ralph_loki_ship.py` is missing.
proposer.sh exits 1 when `-j` is given and `python3` is not on PATH.
The overlay exec wrapper exits 127 with `proposer.sh: <bin> not found` when the harness binary is not on PATH, and 1 on a truncated or unknown env record.
A pass returns 127 when the dsh executable is not found (`DeepSeek Harness not found`).
A pass returns 127 when the prime-agent executable is not found (`Prime Agent not found`).
A pass returns 127 when the prime fleet launcher is not found (`Prime fleet launcher not found`).
A pass of the locally registered backend returns 127 when its shell file is missing or does not define the function.
