An unknown backend makes every pass return 127 with `proposer.sh: unknown backend '<name>' (<registry display>)`; the proposer process itself keeps looping until a breaker or max-iter ends it.
The watchdog returns 124 for every kill reason (the `timeout` convention); this is the pass's producer status, not the proposer's exit code.
proposer.sh exits 0 immediately, running no pass, when the evidence file already exists at startup (resume-to-critic case); this check happens before the prompt is read.
proposer.sh exits 1 with `proposer.sh: prompt is empty` when the prompt file contains only whitespace.

proposer.sh exits with the status of `backend_overlay.py startup <backend>` when that helper fails: 3 for an invalid overlay declaration or scope value, 1 for an internal failure; this happens before pass 1 and after the evidence fast-exit.
proposer.sh exits 1 when the attempt-scope overlay directory cannot be created with `mktemp -d`.
proposer.sh exits 1 when populating the attempt-scope overlay fails; the half-made directory is removed first.
With an attempt-scope overlay only, SIGINT makes proposer.sh exit 130 through the EXIT cleanup path.
With an attempt-scope overlay only, SIGTERM makes proposer.sh exit 143 through the EXIT cleanup path; for every other scope no INT/TERM trap is installed.
proposer.sh exits 6 when `<state>/stop.flag` exists before a pass starts; no event is emitted on this path.
proposer.sh exits 7 when a dsh plugin request file exists but the allowlist is empty.
proposer.sh exits 7 when the plugin request is invalid, denied, timed out or the installer fails.
proposer.sh exits 4 when a plugin was installed on the final pass, since no pass is left to use it.
proposer.sh exits 9 when the attempt yields more than `SPECSTRIDE_YIELD_MAX_PER_ATTEMPT` times (the yield after the 4th by default); the artifact is deleted and no job is started.
proposer.sh exits 6 when `stop.flag` appears during a yield wait; the yielded job is left running.
proposer.sh exits 9 when the yield's own `deadline_sec` expires (or the predicate is unsatisfiable); the job is left running.
proposer.sh exits 9 when the run's wall-clock budget expires during a yield; the job is left running.
proposer.sh exits 0 when the evidence file exists after a pass.
proposer.sh exits 10 when the consecutive hard-cap count reaches `SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_MAX_CAPS` (default 3).
proposer.sh exits 7 when the consecutive error count reaches `SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_MAX_ERRORS` (default 2).
proposer.sh exits 8 when the consecutive no-progress count reaches `SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_MAX_NOPROGRESS` (default 3).
proposer.sh exits 6 when `stop.flag` exists after a pass that produced no evidence (checked on both the structured and the legacy path).
proposer.sh exits 4 when `MAX_ITER` passes ended without the evidence file; it prints `max-iter (<n>) reached without <evidence>` and emits NO `run_stop` event.
Stream route reason literal `structured capture disabled by SPECSTRIDE_AGENT_STREAM=false — parsing plain output`.
Stream route reason literal `stream tap unavailable (agent_stream.py or python3 missing) — parsing plain output`.
Stream route reason literal `stream format '<fmt>' has no registered adapter — parsing plain output`.
Watchdog kill reason literal `idle_timeout` (class `hang`).
Watchdog kill reason literal `repeat_stall` (class `futility`), produced by both the process-level and the tool-level repetition check.
Watchdog kill reason literal `progress_stall` (class `futility`).
Watchdog kill reason literal `hard_cap` (class `budget`).
Yield wait outcome words: `satisfied`, `timeout`, `stop`, `wall_budget`.
Kill class literals are `budget` (hard_cap), `hang` (idle_timeout) and `futility` (repeat_stall, progress_stall); an unknown reason is classed `futility`.
`run_stop reason=proposer_yield_budget` with fields `iter`, `yields`, `max`.
`run_stop reason=stop_flag` with fields `iter`, `yield=true`, `job_pid`, `job_log`, emitted only when the stop happens during a yield wait.
`yield_timeout reason=deadline`.
`run_stop reason=proposer_yield_timeout` (field `iter`) for both the deadline and the wall-budget case.
`yield_timeout reason=wall_budget`.
Finaliser decision literals acted on by the loop: `cap_halt` (exit 10) and `halt` (exit 7); any other value continues.
`run_stop reason=proposer_cap_exhausted` with fields `iter`, `kill_reason`, `consec`.
Literals `agent_error` (reason) and `agent` (kill_class) are used when an erroring pass was not killed by the watchdog.
`run_stop reason=proposer_consecutive_errors` with fields `iter`, `subtype`, `kill_reason`, `kill_class`.
`run_stop reason=proposer_no_progress` with fields `iter`, `consec`.
The state directory and the evidence file's parent directory are created at startup if missing.
The dsh plugin request artifact is `<state>/features/<feature>/dsh-plugin-request.json`, written by the model.
Processed requests are archived under `<state>/features/<feature>/plugin-installs/` as `<UTC stamp>.request.json` plus an atomically written `<UTC stamp>.receipt.json`.

The yield artifact path is `/phase

-attempt-.json`; it is deleted before every pass, so only an artifact written by the pass that just ended is acted on.

The dsh overlay `settings.yaml` is written with an `agent-default-model:` block (`provider`, `model`, optional `reasoningEffort`) followed by the real `settings.yaml` minus its own `agent-default-model` block.
With scope `pass` a fresh tree `$TMPDIR/specstride-overlay.<key>.XXXXXX` is created and populated before each pass and removed after the watchdog returns.
`<overlay>/specstride-overlay.env` is read as NUL-delimited records: `unset <name>` and `set <name> <value>`; any other record kind is an error.

With a dsh model override, a throwaway `DSH_HOME` is created per pass at `$TMPDIR/specstride-dsh-home.XXXXXX`: every entry of the real home except `settings.yaml` is symlinked in, and it is removed with `rm -rf` after the pass.
The claude arm writes the prompt to `$TMPDIR/specstride-prompt.XXXXXX` and removes it after the pass; this avoids the 128 KiB single-argument limit.

`<invocation_dir>/producer.json` (contract `specstride-producer-status/v1`) is written atomically with `producer_exit_code`, `producer_signal`, `parser_exit_code`, `timed_out`, `launch_failed`, `duration_ms`.

`<invocation_dir>/metadata.json` (contract `specstride-invocation/v1`) is written atomically (tmp, fsync, replace) for prime and registry-routed passes with `run_id`, `feature`, `role`, `backend`, `phase`, `attempt`, `iteration`, `invocation_id`, `observability_mode=structured`, `provider_format`, `expected_evidence`.

Each watchdog kill writes a markdown checkpoint `/pass-checkpoints/-phase

-attempt-pass-.md` with run, phase, attempt, pass, reason, elapsed, optional detail, the last 25 tool calls and the last 5 text blocks (600 chars each).
`<state>/.last-watchdog-kill.path` holds the path of the checkpoint file; both sidecars are deleted at the start of the next pass, after their content was put into the prompt.
`<state>/.last-watchdog-kill` holds one line `<reason>|<elapsed>|<detail>` for the pass that was just killed.

A launched yield job gets `/yield-jobs/phase

-attempt--yield.pid`, `.rc` and `.log`; the pid and rc files are written atomically (tmp then mv) by the job wrapper itself.
The failure ledger is `<FEATURE_DIR>/failure-ledger.jsonl`, an append-only JSON-lines file shared by all jobs of the feature.

Each structured pass gets an invocation directory `/features//debug/invocations///phase-

/attempt-/iter-/`.
`<state>/.last-invocation-dir` holds the path of the newest pass's invocation directory, so the controller loop can find the artifacts to finalise.
`<invocation_dir>/prompt.txt` holds the exact assembled prompt of the pass, written only with `--debug`.
`<invocation_dir>/provider-terminal.json` is the terminal sidecar path handed to the tap for prime and registry-routed passes.
`<state>/.breaker-state.<run-id>.json` is the persisted breaker state of the structured path; it is deleted at proposer startup, so counters never carry over between invocations.
`<state>/proposer.pid` holds the pid of the background subshell running the current pass; it is written after the pass starts and removed when the pass ends and on exit.
The usage text documents exit codes 0, 1, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 under an `EXIT` heading; exit 3 (overlay config error) is not listed there.
The usage text replaces the `@PROPOSER_BACKENDS@` placeholder with the registry's proposer display line, so the listed backends always come from `lib/backends.py`.
stderr line `proposer.sh: could not create overlay for backend '<b>' in <dir>: mktemp failed` when the overlay directory cannot be created; the pass fails.
stderr line `proposer.sh: could not build DSH_HOME overlay for <provider/model>` when the dsh home overlay cannot be built; the pass returns 1.
Checkpoint file heading `# Pass terminated by the specstride watchdog`.
stderr line `run_with_idle_watchdog: <message> -- killing pid <pid>.` on every watchdog kill.

Prompt block heading `## Your previous pass was terminated by the harness, not by you`, followed by `Reason: **<reason>** after <n>s.`, an optional `What it caught:` line, reason-specific advice and the checkpoint path.
stderr line `proposer.sh: refusing the pass yield — <detail>` for a schema violation.
stderr line `proposer.sh: refusing the adopt yield — pid <n> is in this pass's own session (<sid>); ... Start it with setsid, or use mode 'launch'.`

Prompt block heading `## The job you yielded on has ENDED — resume from its result`, carrying the yield reason, waited seconds, job log path, exit code, the pass's own `on_resume` text and a log slice.
stderr line `proposer.sh: evidence already exists (<path>); nothing to do.` on the fast exit.
Prompt section `## Optional DSH plugin request protocol` is appended to the standing prompt only when the backend is exactly `dsh` (no qualifier) and the allowlist is non-empty.
Prompt block heading `## You have ended <n> passes in a row within <sec>s without evidence`, which prints the yield artifact path and a sample `specstride-pass-yield/v1` JSON.
stderr banner `----- proposer pass <i>/<max>  <ISO time> -----` before each pass.
stderr line `proposer.sh: DSH plugin request found but SPECSTRIDE_DSH_PLUGIN_ALLOWLIST is empty`.
stderr line `proposer.sh: installed DSH plugin(s): <list>; restarting with fresh profile`.
stderr line `proposer.sh: pass <i> was terminated by the watchdog (<reason>, class <class>); its checkpoint is carried into the next pass.`
stderr line `proposer.sh: this attempt has already yielded <n> times — aborting (exit 9). ...`
stderr line `proposer.sh: pass <i> yielded — <reason>. Waiting on '<kind>' with NO model session open (deadline <n>s).`
stderr line `proposer.sh: stop.flag detected during a yield — stopping (exit 6). The job is specstride-owned and is LEFT RUNNING (pid <n>); its log is <path>.`
stderr line `proposer.sh: evidence appeared after pass <i> (<path>).`
stderr line `proposer.sh: pass <i> ended after <n>s with no evidence and no yield — <k> short passes in a row; the next pass is told to yield instead of waiting.`
stderr line `proposer.sh: pass <i> hit the pass ceiling (<reason>, <n>s) — consecutive cap kills: <k>/<max>`.

stderr line `proposer.sh: <n> consecutive passes hit the pass ceiling — aborting (exit 10). ... do NOT just raise the cap. Declare the long step as a yield, or pre-stage it as a verification command, or split the phase.`
stderr line `proposer.sh: pass <i> errored (subtype '<s>', is_error) — consecutive errors: <n>/<max>`.
stderr line `proposer.sh: <n> consecutive agent errors — aborting (exit 7). Raise --timeout or SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_MAX_ERRORS, or fix the phase harness ...`.
stderr line `proposer.sh: pass <i> changed nothing outside .specstride — consecutive no-progress passes: <k>/<max>`.
stderr line `proposer.sh: <k> consecutive passes wrote nothing — the phase is blocked on something the agent cannot decide for itself (exit 8). ...`
stderr line `proposer.sh: max-iter (<n>) reached without <evidence path>`.
The script runs with `set -uo pipefail` and deliberately WITHOUT `-e`, so a non-zero agent exit in one pass never ends the loop.

The default repeat-ignore regex covers pytest and the pytest-xdist bootstrap, ruff, mypy, black, flake8, eslint, prettier, tsc, jest, vitest, `go test|vet`, `cargo test|clippy|fmt`, `make test|lint|check`, and command-name-anchored batch tools tesseract, convert, magick, compare, ffmpeg, pdftotext, identify.
Every value-taking flag uses `${2:?}`, so a flag given without a value aborts the shell with a parameter error instead of the usage message.
proposer.sh accepts no positional arguments: every token that is not a known flag falls into the `*)` arm, prints `proposer.sh: unknown arg: <tok>` plus usage on stderr and exits 1.
`-j` alone (no `--loki-url` and no `--otel-url`) enables Loki only, the original single-sink behaviour; when either URL flag is passed only those sinks ship.
The stream tap degrades silently: when `agent_stream.py` or `python3` is absent `AGENT_STREAM` becomes `false` with no message, except that a registry-routed backend announces the reason per pass.
The feature directory is derived as the grandparent of the evidence path, so yield, checkpoint and ledger paths follow the evidence location rather than `--feature`.

Stream route resolution runs once per run from the registry `stream` field of the bare backend name; a named format is routed only when the operator did not disable the stream, the tap is available and an adapter is registered for that format.
A provider embedded in the model ref that differs from `SPECSTRIDE_DSH_PROVIDER` fails the pass with `conflicting DSH providers`.
dsh model resolution: `provider/model` is used as given; a bare `glm-*` id maps to provider `zai`; bare `qwen3.8-27b` or `qwen3.8-27b-q5` maps to `local-high/qwen3.8-27b-q5`.
A dsh model id with no resolvable provider fails the pass with `DSH model '<raw>' needs a provider; use provider/model or set SPECSTRIDE_DSH_PROVIDER`.
A dsh model ref is rejected as `invalid DSH model ref` unless the provider matches `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` and the model matches `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+`.
With scope `none` every overlay helper is a no-op: no process is started and the harness command runs with the operator's real environment.
With scope `attempt` ONE overlay is created before pass 1 and reused by every pass of the invocation; it is removed by the EXIT cleanup.
A failed overlay populate removes the half-made directory and fails the pass (return 1) without running the harness.

The harness binary is resolved to an absolute path with the REAL `PATH`/`HOME` before any overlay variable is applied, and the overlay environment reaches only the harness process tree, never the proposer shell, watchdog or tap.
Releasing a pass overlay calls `backend_overlay.py remove` and always succeeds: a failed removal prints a warning and never changes the pass's status.
Backend dispatch in `run_agent` matches `dsh|dsh:*`, `claude`, `codex`, `prime`, `prime:*` and the locally registered backend with or without qualifier; `claude:<x>` or `codex:<x>` match no arm.
dsh refuses `--backend dsh:<model>` together with `--model`: the pass returns 1 with `use either --backend dsh:<provider/model> or --model, not both`.
dsh model precedence is `--model`, then `SPECSTRIDE_DSH_MODEL`, then the qualifier after `dsh:`; with none set no overlay is built and the profile's own settings select the model.

dsh is invoked as `<dsh-bin> --profile <profile> <prompt>`: the whole prompt is ONE positional argument and no allow-all-tools flag is passed; permissions come from the `DSH_PERMISSION_MODE` environment variable.

claude is invoked as `claude -p --dangerously-skip-permissions --verbose [--disable-slash-commands] [--output-format stream-json] [--model M]` with the prompt on stdin from a temp file, not as an argument.
The codex bypass flag `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` is the codex allow-all flag; the shared claude flags are not passed to codex.
codex is invoked as `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox [--model M] <prompt>`; the prompt is a positional argument and the output is always raw text.
prime uses `--mode json` when the stream tap or `-j` is on, otherwise `--mode text`.
Bare `prime` is invoked as `<prime-agent-bin> -p --mode text|json --no-session --cwd <workdir> [--model M]` with the prompt piped on stdin; no allow-all-tools flag is passed.
`prime:` with an empty variant fails the pass with `empty Prime variant; use 'prime' or 'prime:<variant>'`.
`prime:<variant>` rejects `--model` (`--model is unsupported with prime:<variant>; the variant selects its model`) and the pass returns 1.
`prime:<variant>` is invoked as `<fleet-bin> <variant> -p --mode text|json --no-session --cwd <workdir>` with the prompt on stdin.

The locally registered backend is a shell function: its defining file is sourced inside `bash -c` and called as `<fn> <inner-backend> -p <prompt> --dangerously-skip-permissions --verbose [--disable-slash-commands] [--output-format stream-json]`; `--model` is not forwarded.
Producer status mapping: rc 127 sets `launch_failed`, rc 124 sets `timed_out`, rc above 128 sets `producer_signal = rc - 128`; in each of those cases `producer_exit_code` is null.
Disk progress ignores everything under `.git`, the state directory (current and legacy name), `node_modules` and `.venv`.

The tool-call attribution signature is the tool name plus the length, first 96 and last 96 characters of the target of the newest `agent_tool` event; with no tool event yet the key is the command line alone.
Tool-level repetition never kills on an empty target.
Tool-level repetition never treats `Edit`, `Write`, `MultiEdit` or `NotebookEdit` as the offender, but those calls stay in the sequence so moving on to editing counts as moved on.
Tool-level repetition: counts identical `(tool, target)` pairs among this pass's `agent_tool` events and kills only when the pair that reached the limit is also the MOST RECENT call.
The watchdog reads only events appended after the pass started (byte offset of events.jsonl taken at pass start).
Every watchdog kill sends TERM to the agent pid, waits 3 seconds, then sends KILL, after writing the checkpoint.

The watchdog runs the agent command in the background and polls every tick (default 15 s); on each tick it checks, in order: idle, process-level repetition, tool-level repetition, disk progress (every 4th tick), hard cap.
Idle watchdog: cpu-time seconds are summed over the WHOLE process tree of the pass; the pass is killed only after `idle_timeout` seconds in which that sum did not change.
A process whose command basename is `sleep` is never counted by the process-level repetition check.
A command line matching the repeat-ignore regex is never counted by the process-level repetition check; the tool-level check still applies.

Process-level repetition: each tick samples every process of the pass tree (command line cut to 400 chars), counts each distinct `<pid>|<command line>` once, and kills when one `<latest tool call> x <command line>` key reaches the repeat limit.
Disk-progress watchdog: checked every 4th tick; any file created or modified under the progress roots resets the timer; with no change for `PROGRESS_TIMEOUT` seconds the pass is killed.
Hard cap: the pass is killed once elapsed wall time reaches the `--timeout` value, regardless of progress; it is checked last on each tick.
`resume_when.kind` must be one of `pid`, `exit_code_file`, `file_exists`, `file_stable`, `grep`, `command`.
Yield artifact field `contract` must equal `specstride-pass-yield/v1`.
Yield artifact field `reason` must be a non-empty string.
Yield artifact field `deadline_sec` is REQUIRED and must be a positive integer (a boolean is rejected).
Yield artifact field `on_resume` is optional and must be a string; it is handed to the resuming pass verbatim on one line.
Yield artifact field `job.mode` must be `launch` or `adopt`.
`job.argv` (mode `launch`) must be a non-empty array of non-empty strings without newlines or NULs; it is a fixed argv, never a shell string.
`job.pid` (mode `adopt`) must be a positive integer.
`job.cwd` is optional (default the workdir), resolved against the workdir, and must be an existing directory.
`resume_when.path` is required for kinds `file_exists`, `file_stable` and `grep`; `resume_when.pattern` (a valid regular expression) is required for `grep`.
The `command` predicate is refused unless `SPECSTRIDE_YIELD_ALLOW_COMMAND=true`; when allowed `resume_when.argv` must be a non-empty array of non-empty strings.
Predicate `pid`: satisfied when the target pid (`resume_when.pid`, else the launched or adopted job pid) is no longer alive.
Predicate `exit_code_file`: satisfied when `resume_when.path` (default the job's own rc file) exists.
Predicate `file_exists`: satisfied when the resolved path exists.
Predicate `file_stable`: satisfied when the file's mtime is at least `resume_when.stable_sec` seconds old (default 60, positive integer); a missing file is not yet stable.
Predicate `grep`: satisfied when the pattern matches within the LAST 4 MiB of the file; a missing file is not yet satisfied.
Predicate `command`: runs the fixed argv in the job cwd without a shell, output discarded, 120 s timeout; exit 0 satisfies; a command that cannot be run is unsatisfiable.
An artifact that violates the schema is refused, reported once, deleted, and the pass is accounted exactly as a pass that wrote no evidence.
`job.log` is optional; when empty the log defaults to `<FEATURE_DIR>/yield-jobs/<base>.log`.
Mode `adopt` is refused when the pid is not running or when it shares the proposer's session id, because it would die with the pass.
A launched job runs in the proposer's OWN session (not the pass's), so no watchdog kill can reach it; the wrapper records its own pid and the job's exit code.
After launching, the proposer waits up to 10 s (100 x 0.1 s) for the pid file; without a pid the yield is refused (`the launched job never reported a pid`).
The wait loop checks, on every tick and in this order: `stop.flag`, the predicate, the yield deadline, the run wall-clock budget; then sleeps `SPECSTRIDE_YIELD_POLL` seconds.
Predicate evaluation exit codes: 0 satisfied, 1 not yet, 2 unsatisfiable; an unsatisfiable predicate ends the wait with outcome `timeout` (fail closed).
The resume block shows the job log in full when it has at most head+tail lines, otherwise the first 40 and last 80 lines with an explicit `[<n> lines elided from the middle ...]` marker.
The ledger section is produced only when the job log file exists and `SPECSTRIDE_FAILURE_LEDGER` is exactly `true`.
The ledger job key is `<run-id>:attempt<A>:yield<k>`.
The shared agent flags `--dangerously-skip-permissions --verbose` are added only for claude and the locally registered backend.
`--disable-slash-commands` is added for claude and the locally registered backend unless `SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_SKILLS=1`.
`--output-format stream-json` is added for claude and the locally registered backend when the stream tap or `-j` is on.
Invocation id: `<SPECSTRIDE_INVOCATION_ID>-iter-<n>` when a base is given, otherwise `inv-<iter zero-padded to 6>-<8 hex chars>`.

The backend name given to the tap is `SPECSTRIDE_BACKEND_LABEL` for claude and the locally registered backend, but the raw `--backend` value (qualifier included) for prime and registry-routed backends.
claude and locally-registered-backend passes get an invocation directory but NO `metadata.json`, so the finaliser path is never taken for them.

Tap arguments always carry `--events`, `--run-id`, `--task`, `--backend`, `--iteration`; prime and registry-routed passes add `--feature --role --phase --attempt --invocation-id --expected-evidence --provider-format --terminal-sidecar`.
The prime provider format passed to the tap and written to metadata is the literal `prime-v3`.
The tap receives `--invocation-model <model>` only for a registry-routed backend with a resolvable invocation model.
The tap receives `--loki <url>` and/or `--otel <url>` only for the sinks that are enabled.
With `--debug` the pipeline becomes `run_agent 2>&1 | tee <invocation_dir>/response.txt | <tap>` and the parser exit is read from the third pipeline stage.

Structured pipeline (tap on for claude or the locally registered backend, prime structured, or registry-routed): the agent's stdout and stderr are merged and piped as `run_agent 2>&1 | <tap>`; the tap is `python3 lib/agent_stream.py` or `$SPECSTRIDE_AGENT_TAP`.
In the structured pipeline `run_iteration` always returns 0: the producer and parser exits are persisted to `producer.json`, never turned into the pass status.

Legacy shipper pipeline (tap off, `-j` on, claude or the locally registered backend): the stream is piped to `ralph_loki_ship.py stream` and/or `ralph_otel_ship.py stream` with `--task --backend --run-id --iter`; with both sinks a `tee` feeds the OTEL shipper.
With neither tap nor shipper (dsh, codex, or stream off without `-j`) the agent runs unpiped and its raw output goes to the proposer's own stdout/stderr.
proposer.sh itself injects no feedback, hint, acceleration note or progress file: it sends the `--prompt-file` content as given, so those sections are the caller's responsibility.
The prompt file is read ONCE at startup; a change to it during the run is not seen by later passes.
A backend written as `dsh:<model>` never gets the plugin protocol and its plugin request file is never processed, because both checks compare the backend to the bare string `dsh`.

Overlay scope is resolved once before pass 1 by `backend_overlay.py startup <backend>`, which also sweeps stale overlays and validates the declaration table; the printed word is `none`, `pass` or `attempt`.

The EXIT cleanup removes `proposer.pid` and, when the scope is not `none`, first stops the in-flight pass's process tree (TERM, then KILL after up to 10 s) and then reaps every overlay this proposer owns.
Writes to the state directory (including the agent's own progress notes kept there) do not count as progress; a file written by a background job under the workdir DOES count.
The loop runs passes `i = 1..MAX_ITER`; each pass is a fresh agent process with no carried session.
The pass start stamp is taken one second in the past because `find -newermt` is strictly greater-than.
The long-job status block is recomputed and the phase's long job is (re)ensured before every pass, not once per invocation.

Pass prompt assembly order: the standing prompt file content (plus the dsh plugin protocol when enabled), then the long-job status block, then the killed-pass checkpoint block, then the yield resume block, then the short-pass nudge block; blocks are joined with a blank line and each is present only when non-empty.
The yield resume block and the short-pass nudge block are each consumed by exactly one pass: they are cleared right after being appended.
The pass runs as a background job and the loop waits for it, so an external `stop --now` can kill the in-flight agent tree through the pid file.
After every pass with scope `pass` the parent runs `backend_overlay.py reap --owner-pid <proposer pid> --scope pass` to remove overlays a killed pass left behind.
A plugin install is handled BEFORE the evidence check: a pass that wrote both a request and the evidence still triggers the install and a restart pass.
A pass that ended with a dsh plugin install is exempt from every breaker and from the short-pass counter.
The yield artifact is read only AFTER the pass process has exited.
A yield written by a pass the watchdog killed is ignored (`yield_invalid`, reason `the pass was killed by the watchdog (<reason>)`) and the kill is accounted normally.
The yield counter is per proposer invocation and is never reset inside it; only an accepted or over-budget yield advances it.
The job exit code shown to the resuming pass comes from the job's rc file; for an adopted job, or when the file is missing, it is `unknown`.
A yielded pass is exempt from the no-progress breaker and leaves the error counter untouched (neither incremented nor reset).
A satisfied yield does not consume an iteration by default: the loop counter is decremented so yield plus resume is one logical pass; with `SPECSTRIDE_YIELD_COUNTS_AS_ITER=true` it is consumed.
After a satisfied yield the next pass starts immediately: the inter-pass sleep is skipped.
A refused adopt gives the yield index back and the pass is accounted as an ordinary no-evidence pass (breakers and short-pass counter apply).
Evidence wins outright: after each pass, if the evidence file exists the proposer exits 0 regardless of how the pass ended (error, kill or a simultaneous yield artifact).
Short-pass nudge: a pass that was not killed, wrote no evidence, did not yield and lasted under `SPECSTRIDE_SHORT_PASS_SEC` increments a counter; any other such pass resets it to 0.
Once the short-pass counter reaches `SPECSTRIDE_SHORT_PASS_NUDGE_AFTER` the NEXT pass's prompt carries the nudge block; nothing halts on it and the counter keeps growing while passes stay short.
The finaliser is skipped when `.last-invocation-dir` is missing or the directory has no `metadata.json`; the pass is then not counted by any breaker.

Structured path: after a pass, `lib/finalize_invocation.py <invocation_dir> <events> <breaker_state> <max_errors> <kill_reason> <max_caps>` is run and must print six lines: decision, reason_code, is_error, error count, kill class, cap count.
On the structured path the watchdog kill reason is handed IN to the finaliser, because a kill severs the provider stream and no artifact can name it.
The no-progress breaker is never evaluated on the structured path (prime structured or registry-routed): that branch ends the iteration with `continue` before the check.
Backends that emit no `agent_result` event (dsh, codex, raw text) can only trip the error breaker through a futility or hang watchdog kill: a crashed pass reads as clean.

Legacy error accounting (every backend except structured prime and registry-routed ones): the LAST `agent_result` event of the whole events file decides; `is_error` true (bool or the string `true`) counts as an error, false or no such event counts as clean.
A futility or hang kill overrides the agent result: the pass counts as an error with subtype `watchdog_<reason>`.
A `hard_cap` kill increments only the cap counter: it neither increments nor resets the error counter.
An erroring pass increments the error counter and resets the cap counter; a clean pass resets both counters to 0.

No-progress is measured on disk: a pass made progress when any file under the progress roots (minus `.git`, the state directory, `node_modules`, `.venv`) has a modification time later than one second before the pass started.
Any pass with disk progress resets the no-progress counter to 0; an erroring or hard-capped pass is still measured.
The loop sleeps `--sleep` seconds between passes, but not after the last one.
`lib/critic.py` is a standalone entry point (`python3 lib/critic.py ...`) that judges one phase's evidence and writes the gate marker or feedback; stdlib only.
`--workdir` is required; it is made absolute and is the root for state, grounding resolution and the backend cwd.
`--specs` is required; a path that is not a file exits 3 with `specs not found: <path>`.
`--phase` is a required integer; a phase that the spec slicer cannot find exits 3 with `phase <N> not found in <specs>`.
`--attempt` is an integer, default 1; it is used only in event fields, the transcript name/header, the debug prompt file name and the hint header.
`--max-rejects` is an integer, default from `SPECSTRIDE_MAX_REJECTS` else 3; the critic only echoes it as the `max_rejects` field of a non-approved `verdict` event.
`--provider` selects the critic backend, default from `SPECSTRIDE_CRITIC` else `claude`; an unknown value is not refused at parse time but makes the call raise, which is scored MALFORMED (exit 10).
`--timeout` is an integer number of seconds, default from `SPECSTRIDE_CRITIC_TIMEOUT` else 300; it bounds the HTTP request or the backend subprocess.
`--grounding` defaults to `SPECSTRIDE_CRITIC_GROUNDING` else `true`; only `1`, `true`, `yes`, `on` (case-insensitive) enable the grounding pass, any other value disables it silently.
`--format` (`native`, `speckit-tasks`, `openspec-change`) defaults to `SPECSTRIDE_SPEC_FORMAT` else auto-detect; an invalid format exits 3.
`--verification-plan` (default `SPECSTRIDE_VERIFICATION_PLAN`) names an absolute VerificationPlan v1 JSON; an invalid, stale or relative plan exits 3 with `invalid verification plan: ...`.
`--debug` creates `<feature>/debug/`, writes the assembled prompt there and prints `[debug]` lines with nonce, provider, prompt length, verdict and parse detail on stderr.
`--diagnose` switches to diagnostician mode: no verdict flow, no gate marker or feedback is written, a hint file is written and the process returns normally.
`--feature` is the feature slug, default `SPECSTRIDE_FEATURE`, else derived from the spec location; characters outside `A-Za-z0-9._-` become `-` and an empty result becomes `default`.
Legacy environment names are mapped onto `SPECSTRIDE_*` at import, before any knob is read.

`SPECSTRIDE_GROUNDING_MAX_FILES` (default 80) caps the number of presence lines in the grounding snapshot; it is parsed with `int()` at import, so a non-integer value crashes the critic before any verdict.
`SPECSTRIDE_CRITIC_CONTEXT_TOKENS` overrides the context window for every backend when set to an integer; a non-integer prints a warning and is ignored.
`SPECSTRIDE_ANCHOR_MAX_BYTES_CEIL` (default 49152) is the per-file ceiling for anchored excerpts and the size limit under which a priority file is emitted whole.
`SPECSTRIDE_CLAUDE_CRITIC_API_KEY` is the key for the `claude` critic, preferred over `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is the fallback key for the `claude` critic; with neither key set the call raises and the verdict is MALFORMED.
`SPECSTRIDE_CLAUDE_CRITIC_BASE_URL` is the preferred base URL of the `claude` critic.
`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is the second-choice base URL of the `claude` critic; the final default is `https://api.anthropic.com`.
`<LOCAL_BACKEND>_SH` is the path of the shell file that defines the <local-backend> function; a missing file raises and the verdict is MALFORMED.
`IS_SANDBOX` is set to `1` for the <local-backend> CLI subprocess unless already set.
`DSH_HOME` (default `~/.dsh`) is read as the real home and, when a model override exists, exported to the subprocess as a throwaway overlay directory.
`SPECSTRIDE_DSH_CRITIC_REASONING_EFFORT` adds `reasoningEffort` to the overlay settings of the `dsh` critic.
`SPECSTRIDE_DSH_REASONING_EFFORT` is the fallback reasoning effort for the `dsh` critic.
`SPECSTRIDE_DSH_BIN` (default `dsh`) is the launcher of the `dsh` critic.
`SPECSTRIDE_DSH_PROFILE` (default `headless`) is the profile passed as `--profile`.
`SPECSTRIDE_DSH_CRITIC_MODEL` is the model override of the `dsh` critic when the provider string carries no `dsh:<ref>` qualifier.
`SPECSTRIDE_DSH_MODEL` is the fallback model override after `SPECSTRIDE_DSH_CRITIC_MODEL`.
`SPECSTRIDE_DSH_CRITIC_PROVIDER` is the preferred provider for the `dsh` model override.
`SPECSTRIDE_DSH_PROVIDER` is the fallback provider; a model ref `provider/model` naming a different provider raises `conflicting DSH providers`.
`DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=read-only` is exported to every `dsh` critic subprocess.
`SPECSTRIDE_PRIME_FLEET_BIN` is the launcher for `prime:<variant>`.
`SPECSTRIDE_PRIME_BIN` (default `prime`) is the fallback launcher for `prime:<variant>`.
`SPECSTRIDE_PRIME_AGENT_BIN` (default `prime-agent`) is the launcher for bare `prime`.
`SPECSTRIDE_CLAUDE_CRITIC_MODEL` (default `claude-opus-4-8`) is the model id sent by the `claude` critic and the key for its context-window lookup.
`SPECSTRIDE_CODEX_CRITIC_MODEL` (default `gpt-5`) is the model id sent by the `codex` critic and the key for its context-window lookup.
`OPENAI_BASE_URL` (default `https://api.openai.com/v1`) is the base URL of the `codex` critic.
`OPENAI_API_KEY` is required by the `codex` critic; when empty the call raises `this critic path needs OPENAI_API_KEY`.
`SPECSTRIDE_CRITIC_VIA` (default `<local-backend>`) picks the transport of the <local-backend> critic: `http` uses the OpenAI-compatible gateway, anything else uses the CLI path.
`SPECSTRIDE_<LOCAL_BACKEND>_BACKEND` (default `<gateway>`) is the sub-backend passed to the <local-backend> CLI and the fallback model name on the HTTP path.
`SPECSTRIDE_<GATEWAY>_URL` (default `http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions`) is the gateway URL; a trailing `/chat/completions` is stripped before it is re-appended.
`SPECSTRIDE_<GATEWAY>_KEY` is the bearer key for the HTTP gateway path; when empty the call raises.
`SPECSTRIDE_<LOCAL_BACKEND>_CRITIC_MODEL` names the model on the HTTP gateway path; with sub-backend `<gateway>` and no model the call raises `critic model is unset` (no hardcoded default).
`SPECSTRIDE_AGENT_STREAM` (default `true`) decides what the critic announces for a Prime backend in `agent_observability`: `structured` when exactly `true`, else `raw-text`.
`SPECSTRIDE_TELEMETRY=true` together with a non-empty `SPECSTRIDE_LOKI_URL` makes every critic event also ship to Loki.
`SPECSTRIDE_OTEL_ENABLED=true` together with a non-empty `SPECSTRIDE_OTEL_URL` makes every critic event also ship to the OTEL endpoint.

`SPECSTRIDE_RUN_ID`, `SPECSTRIDE_TASK`, `SPECSTRIDE_FEATURE` and `SPECSTRIDE_TRACE_ID` are added as `run_id`, `task`, `feature`, `trace_id` to the remotely shipped copy of a critic event only (not to the events.jsonl line).
`SPECSTRIDE_BACKEND_LABEL` (default `specstride`) is the `backend` label on shipped critic events; `SPECSTRIDE_TASK` (default `specstride`) is the `task` label.
`SPECSTRIDE_MAX_REJECTS` (default 3) is the default of `--max-rejects`; a non-integer value crashes argument setup.
`SPECSTRIDE_CRITIC` (default `claude`) is the default of `--provider`.
`SPECSTRIDE_CRITIC_TIMEOUT` (default 300) is the default of `--timeout`.
`SPECSTRIDE_CRITIC_GROUNDING` (default `true`) is the default of `--grounding`.
`SPECSTRIDE_SPEC_FORMAT` is the default of `--format`; empty means auto-detect.
`SPECSTRIDE_VERIFICATION_PLAN` is the default of `--verification-plan`; empty means no plan.
`SPECSTRIDE_EVENTS` is the events file the critic appends to; default `<workdir>/<state-dir>/events.jsonl`.
`diagnostician_start` — fields `phase`, `attempt`, `provider`.
`diagnostician_error` — fields `phase`, `attempt`, `error`; emitted when the backend call raises, after which no hint is written.
`diagnostician_done` — fields `phase`, `attempt`, `bytes` (reply length), `case` (`grounding`, `real_gap` or `unknown`).
`grounding_carried` — fields `phase`, `attempt`, `paths` (comma-joined); emitted when paths marked `NEEDS-GROUNDING` in the previous feedback are carried into this attempt's priority set.
`critic_start` — fields `phase`, `attempt`, `provider`; emitted after the prompt is assembled and before the backend call.

`agent_observability` — fields `mode` (`structured` or `raw-text`), `reason`, `provider_format` (`prime-v3`, omitted in raw-text), `role=critic`, `supported_signals=text,result`; emitted only for `prime` and `prime:<variant>`.
`grounding_gap` — fields `phase`, `attempt`, `paths` (comma-joined, at most the first 20 gap tokens); emitted only when the loose pass found files on disk that the strict extractor missed.
`verdict` (approved) — fields `phase`, `attempt`, `result=APPROVED`, `title`; emitted after the marker and transcript are written.
`verdict` (not approved) — fields `phase`, `attempt`, `result` (`REJECTED` or `MALFORMED`), `reason`, `title`, `max_rejects`.
The module documents exit 1 as internal error (an uncaught Python exception); bad command-line usage is handled by argparse, which exits 2, not the documented 3.
`lib/critic.py` exits 3 when the spec file is missing.
`lib/critic.py` exits 3 when the spec format is invalid.
`lib/critic.py` exits 3 when the phase is not found in the spec.
`lib/critic.py` exits 3 when the verification plan is invalid, stale or not absolute.
`lib/critic.py` exits 3 when `GATE<N>-EVIDENCE.md` is missing, with `evidence not found: <path>`.
In `--diagnose` mode the process returns normally (exit 0) whether the hint was written, the call failed or the hint could not be written.
`lib/critic.py` exits 0 when the verdict is APPROVED.
`lib/critic.py` exits 10 for REJECTED and for MALFORMED alike.

`<feature>/gates/GATE<N>-HINT.md` is written by the diagnostician with the header `# Phase <N> — diagnostician hint (attempt <M>)`, a three-line notice that it is not a critic verdict, and the reply verbatim or `(empty diagnostician reply)`.
State root is `<workdir>/<state-dir>/features/<slug>/`, where the state dir is `.specstride` or a legacy name found in the workdir.
The critic creates `<feature>/gates/` and `<feature>/verdicts/` if absent, so a standalone invocation works.
Input contract: `<feature>/gates/GATE<N>-EVIDENCE.md` must exist; it is read with replacement decoding.
`<feature>/debug/critic-prompt.phase<N>.att<M>.txt` holds the assembled prompt under `--debug`.
The transcript is `<feature>/verdicts/phase<N>.attempt<M>.<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>.txt`, timestamped in local time before the backend call; two calls in the same second overwrite each other.
`<feature>/gates/GATE<N>-APPROVED` is written as an empty file on approval (plain open-and-close, not atomic); stale feedback is left in place for the orchestrator.

Transcript content: `# Specstride critic transcript`, then `phase:`, `attempt:`, `provider:`, `nonce:`, `verdict:`, `parse:`, then a PROMPT section with the full prompt and a REPLY section with the reply or `(empty)`.
A transcript is written for APPROVED, REJECTED and MALFORMED alike, including failed backend calls; a write error only prints a warning.
`<feature>/gates/GATE<N>-FEEDBACK.md` is overwritten on REJECTED and MALFORMED (plain write, not atomic); a write error only prints a warning and the exit code stays 10.
Feedback starts with `# Phase <N> — critic feedback (<REJECTED|MALFORMED>)`.
MALFORMED feedback adds a quote block stating the reply was malformed (`<detail>`) and is treated as REJECTED fail-safe.

Feedback then has the line `The following must be addressed before re-writing GATE<N>-EVIDENCE.md:` followed by the complete critic reply verbatim (including its verdict line), or `(no critic output)`.
When a grounding gap exists, feedback ends with `## Grounding transparency (machine-generated — read this)` and one backticked line per gap file, telling the proposer not to re-create them.
Every warning and fatal message goes to stderr with the prefix `critic.py: `.
Gitignore probe lines read `<path> — IGNORED: PASS (<how>)`, `<path> — NOT ignored: FAIL (<how>)` or `gitignore status UNKNOWN (...)`.

Secret scan result lines read `### secret scan (deterministic) — <n> committed config file(s) scanned, NO literal secret assignments found (PASS)` or `... POSSIBLE LEAKS:` with one line per file naming the variable, never the value.
Probe results are appended under `## Deterministic probe results (harness-computed, not LLM)`.
The snapshot block starts with the heading `## Grounding snapshot (verified by the critic, read-only)`.
An unresolved path that is a declared build export renders `**NEEDS-GROUNDING** (declared build export not found on disk; ...)` instead of MISSING.
An unresolved path renders `- `<path>` — **MISSING** (does not exist on disk)`.
A directory renders `- `<path>` — directory, <n> entries`.
A file renders `- `<path>` — exists, <bytes> bytes, mtime <YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS>` (local time), labelled with the resolved workdir-relative path rather than the cited token.
A file whose excerpt does not fit renders `(content excerpt omitted — grounding byte budget reached; file verified present above)` under its presence line.

File dump markers: `NOT FOUND on disk`, `directory (<n> entries)` (at most 200 listed), `binary (...), <n> bytes on disk; content not dumped`, `SKIPPED (diagnostician total budget reached; file verified present on disk)`, `(truncated at <n> bytes — file is larger)`.
stdout carries `HINT-WRITTEN` when the diagnostician wrote its hint file.
With grounding on and no cited path, the block is `## Grounding snapshot` followed by `(No file paths cited in the evidence.)`.
A non-empty gap appends the prompt section `## CITED BUT NOT AUTO-GROUNDED — verified PRESENT by direct stat` with one `- `<token>` — verified on disk (stat)` line each.
stderr line `critic prompt trimmed to fit the <N>-token window: <block> <old>-><new> B; ...` is printed when a block was shrunk.

stderr line `[debug] nonce= provider=

prompt bytes=` is printed under `--debug` (the number is the character length of the prompt).
stderr line `[debug] verdict=<v> detail=<d>` is printed under `--debug` after parsing.
stdout carries exactly `APPROVED` on approval.
stdout carries `REJECTED` or `MALFORMED` on a non-approval.
The reference grounding byte budget is 327680 bytes (320 KB) at the 200000-token window.
The reference window the byte budgets were tuned for is 200000 tokens; every budget is scaled linearly by `window / 200000`.
Bytes-per-token is a fixed 3.18 for every backend.
Context window for locally routed models: `qwen3.8-27b`, `-q5`, `-q4` = 229376 tokens.
Context window for locally routed models: `muse`, `muse-glimmer-30b`, `nemotron`, `nemotron-lightning-30b`, `auto`, `qwen-auto` = 131072 tokens.
Context window for locally routed models: `glm-5.3`, `glm-5.3-flash` = 128000 tokens.
Context window for locally routed `gpt-5`, `gpt-5.5`, `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-5.2` = 200000 tokens.
The default window for an unrecognised locally routed model and for every Prime backend is 98304 tokens.
Context window for the `codex` backend: `gpt-5` 400000, `gpt-5.5` 1000000, `gpt-5.4` and `gpt-5.4-pro` 1050000; an unlisted model falls back to 128000.
Context window for the `claude` backend: 1000000 tokens for the listed Opus, Sonnet, Fable and Mythos ids and 200000 for `claude-haiku-4-5`; an unlisted model falls back to 200000.
For `dsh:<provider>/<model>` the window is looked up by the part after the last `/`; bare `dsh` looks up an empty model and therefore gets the 98304 default.
A scaled budget never drops below 65536 bytes.
An anchored excerpt quotes 15 lines before and after every line containing an anchor token, line-numbered, with merged windows separated by `…`.

A priority directory is expanded into its files only when it holds at most 40 files; build and vendor directories (`node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `.git`, `__pycache__`, `.venv`, `.next`, `coverage`, `.pytest_cache`, `.ruff_cache`) and `*-lock.json` / `*.lock` files are skipped.
Directory expansion is capped at 45 added files in total, smallest directories first.
The diagnostician file dump reads whole files, capped at 200000 bytes per file and 600000 bytes in total (both scaled by the window).
The reply reserve is 8000 tokens (`PROMPT_REPLY_RESERVE_TOKENS`).
The rejection history is capped at 120000 bytes scaled by the window, with head-and-tail elision.
A shrunk block keeps its head and tail and carries the marker `… [<label>: <n> bytes elided to fit the critic's context window; this is a BUDGET elision, not missing content] …`.
A block is shrunk only when it is larger than 4096 bytes and never below 4096 bytes.
When the prompt is still over budget after shrinking, the note `STILL OVER by <n> B after shrinking <order>` is reported on stderr and the oversized prompt is sent anyway.
The grounding pass never executes project commands; the only subprocess it starts is the fixed-argv `git check-ignore`.
A citation candidate is a backticked token, a multi-segment slash path, a bare dotted filename, or a leading-dot dotfile.
A line locator is stripped from a citation before resolution: `x.py:101`, `x.py:10-20`, `x.py:12:5`, `x.py#L12-L20`, `test_x.py::test_y`.
A leading ellipsis prefix (`…/` or `.../`) is stripped from a citation.
Brace shorthand `a-{x,y}.json` is expanded into each alternative, bounded to 16 expansions per citation.
Candidates starting with `http://`, `https://` or `ftp://` are never grounded.
Candidates containing whitespace are dropped (a backticked command is not a path).
A candidate containing `@v<digit>` (an RPC method name) is dropped.
A bare leading-dot token counts as a dotfile only when the character after the dot is lowercase; an optional extension of 1 to 11 characters is allowed.
Any other token counts as a path only when it ends in an alpha-led extension of 2 to 12 characters, or is a slash path with a segment that has an extension.
Trailing `.`, `,`, `:`, `;` and `)` are trimmed from a citation.
A no-slash token that does not resolve on disk is dropped (no MISSING line); a slash path is always kept, so a genuinely missing slash path shows MISSING.
Extraction stops after `3 x GROUNDING_MAX_FILES` paths (240 by default) per text.

Search directories for a citation, in order: workdir root, `<gates>/proofs`, `<gates>`, `out`, then every immediate subdirectory of `<gates>` and of `<gates>/proofs`, then the spec file's own directory when it lies inside the workdir.
Workspace members come from `pnpm-workspace.yaml` `packages:` globs; only a trailing `*` or `**` segment is expanded, negations are skipped, and a member must contain `package.json`.
Declared build exports are the `exports`, `main`, `module`, `types` and `typings` targets of each member's `package.json`; targets containing `*` are ignored.
A placeholder citation such as `runs/d0-<dd>.md` (`<...>` of 1 to 40 characters without `/`) is resolved as a glob where only the placeholder is a wildcard; the first hit in sorted order wins.
An absolute citation is honoured as-is, including a path outside the workdir.
A relative citation that normalises to escape the workdir (`../x`) never resolves and is shown MISSING.

Resolution order for a relative citation: exact path under the workdir, then each pnpm workspace member (hinted member first), then the whole relative path under each search directory, then the basename under each search directory.
The carry-over pattern is `NEEDS-GROUNDING:` followed by optional whitespace and an optionally backticked token.
Up to 12 paths that the previous `GATE<N>-FEEDBACK.md` marked `NEEDS-GROUNDING:` and that resolve to files are added to the path list and the priority set.
The grounding gap is every loosely cited token (from evidence plus section) that the strict extractor did not return and that resolves to a file on disk; directories are never gaps.
The gitignore probe runs `git -C <workdir> check-ignore -q <path>` with a 10 second timeout and falls back to an exact-basename match in `.gitignore` when git gives no answer.
The gitignore probe runs only when the section or evidence mentions `gitignore`; it checks cited `.env*` files inside the workdir (not `*.example`), or `.env` when none is cited.

The secret scan runs only when the section or evidence mentions `secret`; it scans config-shaped files (not `.env` itself, not git-ignored, at most 512 KB) at most two directory levels deep, skipping state, vendor and output directories.
Anchor tokens are backticked identifiers or dotted calls from the section (no slash, no source extension, at least 3 characters); a dotted token also contributes its last segment.

An anchored excerpt is capped per file at `min(ceiling, max(6000, file size))` bytes and ends with `… (anchored excerpt truncated at <n> bytes)` when cut; only the first 512 KB of the file are searched.

The inherited-obligations block (from `### Inherited obligations from earlier approved phases` up to `Create or update automated tests for these obligations`) stays in the prompt but is excluded from priority extraction, directory extraction and anchor extraction.
Paths under a `proofs/` directory are ordered first and treated as priority.

The presence-line cap is the only thing that stops the snapshot loop; the remaining paths are summarised as `… (<n> further cited path(s) omitted: presence-line cap reached — omission here means NOT-SHOWN ...)`.
Glob characters in a citation (`*`, `?`, `[`) are not expanded during extraction; they are tried only at snapshot time, relative to the workdir, when the literal path does not resolve.
A wildcard citation that matches files renders one presence line `present: wildcard matches <n> file(s) on disk: ...` listing at most 20 names followed by ` …`; no file content is excerpted for it.
An unreadable file keeps its presence line and adds `(could not read: <error>)`.

A file whose first 4000 bytes contain a NUL byte is described as `binary (<kind>[, <WxH>]); content not excerpted`; kinds recognised are PNG and GIF (with dimensions), JPEG, WEBP, PDF, else `binary data`.
A priority file no larger than the anchor ceiling (49152 bytes by default) is emitted whole, line-numbered, with the label `(complete file, line-numbered)`.
A whole-file emission that would exceed the byte budget degrades to an anchored excerpt, and that to head/tail.
The head/tail excerpt is the first 4000 bytes and, for files longer than 5000 bytes, the last 1000 bytes joined by `… (truncated) …`.
The excerpt budget is the full scaled cap for priority files and half of it for every other file; both draw on one running total.
The diagnostician prompt demands the first line be `CASE: GROUNDING` or `CASE: REAL-GAP`.

The declared case is read from the first non-empty reply line, tolerant of leading markdown characters, case and `REAL_GAP` / `REAL GAP` spellings; it is recorded only as the `case` metric and nothing in the gate reads it.

The rejection history is every `attempts/phase<N>/<dir>/GATE<N>-FEEDBACK.md` in sorted directory-name order, each under `--- <dir> ---`, followed by the current feedback under `--- latest (attempt <M>) ---`; with none it is `(no prior rejection recorded)`.
The diagnostician prompt is fitted to the window by shrinking `files_block`, then `history`, then `evidence`.
The diagnostician uses the same backend, the same `--timeout` and one call, with no nonce and no verdict grammar.
The diagnostician never writes the approval marker or feedback and never raises: a failed call or a failed hint write only warns.
The design-context block is included only when the rendered context is non-empty and is framed as read-only background that can never become a new criterion.
The critic prompt opens with the role line `You are the CRITIC (an automated approval gate). Be adversarial, not helpful.`
The prompt rule: every acceptance criterion is checked individually and any unmet, unclear or merely asserted criterion means REJECTED.
The prompt tells the critic to trust the grounding snapshot over the evidence prose when they conflict.
The prompt tells the critic to answer `NEEDS-GROUNDING:<path>` in its feedback when it cannot judge a criterion for lack of content, instead of rejecting it as unimplemented.
The prompt demands the reply end with exactly one line `VERDICT <nonce>: APPROVED` or `VERDICT <nonce>: REJECTED`, and repeats that demand after the END marker.
Prompt block order: rules, `SPEC — Phase <N>`, `EVIDENCE (proposer-written)`, grounding snapshot (plus gap list, probes and pin block), optional `DESIGN CONTEXT`, `END`.
The verdict grammar is a whole line matching `^\s*VERDICT\s+<nonce>\s*:\s*(APPROVED|REJECTED)\s*$`, case-insensitive and multi-line, searched anywhere in the reply (not only the last line).
A reply with a `VERDICT ...:` line but no line carrying the right nonce is MALFORMED with detail `verdict line present but nonce missing/mismatched`.
A reply with no verdict line is MALFORMED with detail `no verdict line found`.
A reply with more than one nonce-bearing verdict line is MALFORMED with detail `multiple verdict lines (<n>)`, even when all of them agree.
The parsed verdict is upper-cased, so `verdict <nonce>: approved` approves.

The `claude` critic is an HTTP POST to `<base>/v1/messages` with headers `x-api-key` and `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`, `max_tokens` 2048 and one user message; the reply is the concatenation of the `text` content blocks.
The `codex` critic is an HTTP POST to `<base>/chat/completions` with a bearer key and one user message; no `max_tokens` is sent; empty `choices` raises.
The <local-backend> critic on the CLI path pipes the prompt on stdin to `bash -c` which sources the shell file and calls the function with `-p --dangerously-skip-permissions`.
The `dsh` prompt is passed as argv, split only at ASCII spaces into chunks of at most 120 KiB, and no chunk may start with `-`; a single token over 120 KiB raises.
A bare `glm-*` model maps to provider `zai`; `qwen3.8-27b` and `qwen3.8-27b-q5` map to provider `local-high` with model `qwen3.8-27b-q5`; any other bare model without a provider raises.
A `dsh` provider must match `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` and a model `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+`, else `invalid DSH model ref` is raised.

A `dsh` model override is applied through a throwaway home directory (`specstride-dsh-home.*`) that symlinks every entry of the real home except `settings.yaml` and writes a new `settings.yaml`; it is removed after the call.
The `dsh` patch file disables 18 model-facing tools (shell, filesystem, search, skills, sub-agents, workflow, web, todo, user questions), so the critic is tool-free.
The `dsh` critic runs `<launcher> --profile <profile> --patch <tmp.yml> -- <task args>` with cwd set to the workdir and captures stdout as the reply.
A subprocess timeout is reported as `<backend> critic timed out after <n>s` and scored MALFORMED.
A non-zero `dsh` exit raises with the first 300 characters of stderr, or of stdout when stderr is empty; empty stdout also raises.
The Prime critic runs `<launcher> [<variant>] -p --mode text --no-session --no-tools --no-skills --no-context-files [--cwd <workdir>]` with the prompt on stdin.
The CLI critic calls for Prime and for <local-backend> run inside a per-call backend overlay context; an overlay declaration or overlay error raises and is scored MALFORMED.
Dispatch is by provider string, tested in this order: `dsh` / `dsh:<ref>`, `claude`, `codex`, `prime`, `prime:<variant>`, <local-backend>; there is no fallback from one transport to another.
A JSON-mode Prime critic function exists in the module but the dispatcher never calls it; the verdict path always uses text mode although `agent_observability` may announce `structured`.
`prime:` with an empty variant raises `empty Prime variant; use prime or prime:<variant>`.

An unknown provider raises `unknown SPECSTRIDE_CRITIC provider:

()`, which becomes a MALFORMED verdict and exit 10, not exit 3.
Every critic event record has `ts` (epoch with 6 decimals, as a string), `time` (`%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z`) and `event`; fields whose value is `None` are dropped; other values keep their JSON type.
Events are appended to the events file best-effort: an `OSError` on write is swallowed, and an empty events path disables emitting.
Remote shipping uses Loki stream labels `job=ralph`, `task`, `backend`, and drops `event` and `time` from the shipped field set; any exception is swallowed.
OTEL shipping uses resource attributes `service.name=ralph`, `task`, `backend`.
When a verification plan is given, the rendered phase obligations are appended to the phase section itself, so they are judged as acceptance criteria and also feed path extraction.
The evidence file is read up to 60000 characters plus one; a longer file is cut to 60000 and gets the marker `… (evidence truncated) …`.
In diagnostician mode the spec, format, phase, verification plan and evidence checks still run first, so they can still exit 3.
Paths are extracted from the evidence first and then from the phase section; section-only paths are appended after the evidence paths.
Backticked tokens in the phase section that name an existing directory inside the workdir are added to the path list as directories.
Priority paths are the cited paths that the phase's own section names; when the section names none, every evidence path becomes priority.
The preferred workspace member is the one whose directory basename appears in the section plus evidence text, longest basename first.
With grounding disabled the priority list is empty, so the backing hash is the hash of nothing and pins stay valid regardless of file changes.

Before the call the critic hashes the priority files and appends a pin block for criteria confirmed earlier against the same hash; any failure only warns `W9 pin load skipped` and disables pin updates for this call.
The nonce is `secrets.token_hex(8)`: 16 lowercase hex characters, generated fresh for every critic call and never in diagnostician mode.
The assembled prompt is fitted to `(context_tokens - 8000) * 3.18` bytes by shrinking blocks in the order `context`, `grounding`, `evidence`; the criteria section is never shrunk.
The critic makes exactly one backend call per invocation; there is no retry inside `critic.py`.
A transport or HTTP error of the backend call is scored MALFORMED with detail `critic call failed: <error>`, an empty reply, and the normal reject path (feedback, transcript, event, exit 10).
Any other exception from the backend call (timeout, non-zero exit, empty stdout, missing key, unknown provider) is scored MALFORMED with detail `critic call error: <error>`.
On APPROVED the phase's pin file is deleted.
Pins are updated only on a genuine REJECTED verdict with a computed hash and at least one criterion id in the section; MALFORMED never updates pins.

The `reason` field of a non-approved verdict is the first non-empty reply line that does not start with `VERDICT`, stripped of leading `-*# ` and cut to 120 characters; with no such line it is the parse detail.
The pin file is `<feature>/verdict-pins.phase<N>.json` with keys `phase`, `hash`, `confirmed` (sorted ids), indented and key-sorted.
The pin file is written atomically through `<path>.tmp` and `os.replace`; a write error is swallowed.
A criterion id is `T` followed by 1 to 4 digits at word boundaries; a letter-suffixed id such as `T044a` is not matched.
The unmet set is every criterion id that appears anywhere in the critic reply, so an id merely mentioned as satisfied also counts as unmet.
Pin paths are joined to the workdir literally (no search-directory resolution), so a bare citation that lives under `gates/proofs/` hashes as `MISSING`.
The backing hash is SHA-256 over sorted `path=<sha256 of content>` entries separated by NUL; an unreadable or missing file contributes `MISSING`.
Stored pins are honoured only when the stored hash equals the current hash; a mismatch, unreadable or corrupt file yields no pins.
Confirmed pins are `(all section ids ∪ prior valid pins) − ids named in the current reply`.

The pin prompt block is headed `PREVIOUSLY CONFIRMED (W9 verdict pins)`, lists the ids and tells the critic to re-examine one only when current evidence contradicts it; it is empty on a first attempt.
`lib/verification_failure_digest.py <evidence.json>` prints a markdown failure digest of a gate evidence document on stdout.
`SPECSTRIDE_VERIFY_TAIL_LINES` (default 80) is the number of trailing stdout lines shown per failing command.
`SPECSTRIDE_VERIFY_TAIL_ERR_LINES` (default 40) is the number of trailing stderr lines shown per failing command.
`verification_failure_digest.py` exits 0 in every other case, including an unreadable evidence file.
`verification_failure_digest.py` exits 2 with a usage line on stderr when not given exactly one argument.
An unreadable evidence file prints `Could not read the verification evidence (<error>).`
An evidence document without a failing command prints a two-line note telling the reader to inspect the document directly.
Each failing command prints `### <commandId> — exit <code>` and then the argv in backticks with `(cwd: <dir>)`.
Output tails are printed as `stdout (last <n> lines):` and `stderr (last <n> lines):` in fenced blocks; an empty stream is skipped.
stdout lines starting with `FAILED `, `ERROR ` or `E   ` are listed first under `Failing assertions / tests:`, at most 40, then `… <n> more`.

`verification_plan.py create` builds the plan, persists the JSON and markdown, optionally scaffolds tests, and prints one JSON object with `planId`, `contentHash`, `markdownPath`, `canonicalPath`, `declaredCommands`, `generated`.
`verification_plan.py validate --plan <json> [--specs <path>]` prints `valid` and exits 0, or exits 3.
`verification_plan.py slice --plan --phase <int> [--specs] [--prestage-dir]` prints the phase's obligation context for prompts.
`verification_plan.py scaffold --plan --output <dir> [--specs]` writes the test scaffolds and prints the artifact list as JSON.
`verification_plan.py run --plan --phase <int|release> [--specs] [--evidence-output] [--attempt] [--prestage-dir]` executes the gate's commands and prints the gate summary.
`verification_plan.py prestage --plan --phase <int> --attempt <int> [--specs] [--evidence-output] [--prestage-dir]` runs the phase's pre-stage commands once and writes the pre-stage document.
`verification_plan.py prestage-report --plan --phase <int> [--attempt] [--specs] [--prestage-dir]` prints the pre-stage prompt block without a trailing newline added.
`--prestage-dir` must be absolute (else exit 3); the default is the directory of `--plan`.
`run --attempt` defaults to the number parsed from `-attempt-<n>` in the `--evidence-output` file name; when unknown, per-attempt reuse is refused.
`create --workdir` is required and must be an absolute existing directory.
`create --specs` is required and must be an absolute path of an existing file that validates in the detected format.
`create --format` optionally forces the spec format.
`create --output` is required: the absolute markdown plan path inside the workdir.
`create --json-output` is required: the absolute canonical JSON plan path inside the workdir.
`create --required` marks every gate `required: true` and refuses to write a plan that has any ambiguity.
`create --generate-tests <dir>` writes test scaffolds into that directory (inside the workdir).
`create --verification-commands <json>` names an absolute document of phase-scoped commands the gates must execute.
`run --phase` accepts an integer or the literal `release`; anything else exits 3 with `--phase must be an integer or release`.
`create`, `validate`, `slice`, `scaffold` and `prestage-report` exit 0 on success.
`verification_plan.py prestage` exits 0 when every pre-stage command passed (or none exists) and 11 otherwise; the code is informational.
`verification_plan.py run` exits 0 when the gate passed and 10 when it failed.
Every `VerificationError` exits 3 with `verification_plan.py: <message>` on stderr.
`create --required` with any ambiguity fails with `required verification is blocked: <ambiguities>` (exit 3) and writes no plan.

The markdown plan starts with `<!-- specstride-verification-plan content-hash: <hash> -->` and has sections Provenance, Coverage obligations, Phase gates, Effect-witness policy, Automated commands, Ambiguities and blockers.
Plan outputs must be absolute, lie inside the real workdir and not be symbolic links, else `verification output escapes the authorized workdir` or `... cannot be a symbolic link`.
The declared-commands document is a JSON object with a non-empty `commands` array and optional `schema_version` and `discovery`; its path must be absolute.

The canonical plan JSON has `id`, `kind=verification-plan`, `version=1`, `source`, `project`, `obligations`, `commands`, `suites`, `gates`, `assumptions`, `ambiguities`, `unsupportedCapabilities`, optional `declaredCommands`, and `contentHash`.

An existing file with different content is overwritten only when it starts with the expected generation marker; otherwise `refusing to overwrite a non-generated or changed artifact`. The canonical JSON plan has no marker, so a changed plan at the same path is refused.
Plan files are written atomically: temp file `.verification-*` in the target directory, flush, fsync, mode 0600, `os.replace`; identical content is left untouched.
Scaffold for vitest: `verification.generated.test.ts` with one `it.todo` per obligation; for jest (only when vitest is absent): `verification.generated.test.js` with `test.todo`.
Scaffold for pytest: `test_verification_generated.py` with one skipped test per obligation.
Scaffold manifest `verification.generated.json` (kind `verification-test-scaffold`, version 1) is always written, listing every obligation.
Pre-stage evidence is `prestage-phase-<N>-attempt-<M>.json` in the pre-stage directory and is overwritten on re-run.
Detached pre-stage jobs write `prestage-logs/<name>.log` and `prestage-logs/<name>.status.json` in the pre-stage directory; stale copies are deleted before launch.
Gate evidence is written once to `--evidence-output` (absolute path); a second write with different content is refused because the file has no marker.
Phase context starts with `## Verification obligations`, then `Canonical verification plan: <id>`, `Verification plan hash: <hash>`, `Source semantic hash: <hash>`.
`prestage` prints `Pre-stage phase <N> attempt <M>: <n> command(s), <n> passed, <n> running, <n> failed`.
`run` prints `Verification gate <id> passed <n> command(s)` or `Verification gate <id> failed: <command ids>`.
`validate` prints `valid`.
`prestage` prints `No pre-stage commands for phase <N>` when the phase has none.

An obligation is kind `effect-witness` (level `integration`) when the phase title or criterion contains a mutation verb such as start, create, write, delete, publish, send, update, deploy, install, commit or push; otherwise kind `positive` (level `contract`).
When no `test` command is discovered the plan records the ambiguity `No safe automated test command was discovered below <workdir>; required verification cannot start until one is configured`.

Optional declared fields: `stage` (`gate`, `pre`, `prestage`, `both`; default `gate`), `reportPath` (workdir-relative), `reusePolicy` (`per-attempt`, `per-phase`, `per-run`; default `per-attempt`), `detached` (boolean), `cumulative` (boolean, default true), `kind` (default `verify`), `label`.
The pre-stage document has kind `specstride-prestage-evidence`, version 1, `planId`, `planHash`, `phase`, `attempt`, `sourceRevision`, start and finish epochs, `commands`, `passed`, `summary`.
Obligation ids are `VO-` plus 20 hex characters of a hash over bundle id, phase, index and criterion text; command ids are `CMD-` plus 20 hex characters.
`sourceRevision` records `available`, `revision`, `workingTreeDirty`, `capturedAt`, or `available: false` with a `reason` when git or the repository is missing.

A declared command needs `id` (non-empty string), `phase` (positive integer), `executable`, `cwd` (absolute existing directory) and `timeoutSec` (positive integer); `args` is a list of strings and `env` a string-to-string object.
`detached: true` on a command with stage `gate` is refused.
A bare executable name is resolved on PATH at plan time; an unresolvable or non-executable file is refused.
A duplicate declared id is refused.
`discovery` may only be `none`, which removes every discovered command from the plan; any other value is refused.
A missing manager or interpreter on PATH is recorded as an ambiguity, not an error.

Node discovery: with `package.json`, the manager is `packageManager` (before `@`), else `pnpm` when `pnpm-lock.yaml` exists, else `npm`; scripts `test`, `build`, `lint`, `format:check` become commands with timeouts 1800, 1800, 900, 900 seconds.
Node command argv is `--dir <workdir> <script>` for pnpm, `--prefix <workdir> run <script>` for npm and `--cwd <workdir> <script>` for any other manager.
Python discovery: when `pyproject.toml`, `pytest.ini` or `tox.ini` mentions `pytest`, the command is `<python3> -m pytest <workdir>` with a 1800 second timeout.
Rust discovery: `Cargo.toml` yields `cargo test --manifest-path <Cargo.toml>`, timeout 1800 seconds.
Go discovery: `go.mod` yields `go test ./...`, timeout 1800 seconds.

`project.fingerprint` is a hash over the workdir and the SHA-256 of these root files when present: `package.json`, the four JS lock files, `pyproject.toml`, `pytest.ini`, `tox.ini`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `go.mod`, `go.sum`.

`source.contentHash` hashes a projection of the spec (`tasks-v2`): format, ordered phase numbers and titles, and criteria text with the checkbox removed; ticking a task or editing surrounding prose does not make the plan stale.
A declared command naming a phase the spec does not define is refused.
`source.bundleId` is a deterministic 26-character ULID-shaped id derived from spec path, format and spec hash.
One obligation is created per phase criterion; a phase without criteria gets one obligation from its title, or `Complete phase <N>`.
Each obligation has `acceptanceRefs` `phase-<N>-criterion-<i>`, `oracle`, `witnesses`, `negativeCases` and `automationStatus` (`planned` when a discovered test command exists, else `manual`).

A phase suite runs every discovered `test` command; the discovered `build` command is added only when the phase's title or criteria mention build-artifact words (build, dist, artifact, tsc, compile, bundle, transpile, typecheck, declaration file, `.d.ts`).
Declared commands run after the discovered ones, in document order.
Each phase gets suite `SUITE-phase-<N>` and gate `GATE-phase-<N>`; a gate's `obligationRefs` and `suiteRefs` are cumulative over phases 1..N, and `cumulative` is false only for the first phase.
Every gate's `required` flag is the value of `create --required`.
A declared command with `cumulative: false` is listed in `excludedCommandRefs` of every other phase's gate and still runs at its own phase and at the release gate.
The no-test-command ambiguity is removed only when every phase has at least one declared command; otherwise a second ambiguity names the uncovered phases.
The release gate `GATE-release` references `SUITE-release`, which carries every obligation and every command.

The declared document's path, content hash, schema version, command count and phases are stored in the plan under `declaredCommands`, inside the hashed body, so editing the document invalidates the plan.
`contentHash` is SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (sorted keys, compact separators, non-ASCII kept) of the plan without `contentHash`.
Plan validation requires kind `verification-plan`, version 1, an absolute workdir, an absolute spec path, and an absolute `executable` and `cwd` on every command.
A plan is refused with `verification plan hash mismatch` when its recorded `contentHash` differs from the recomputed one.
A plan is refused with `verification plan source mismatch` when `source.specPath` differs from the real path of the given spec.
A plan without `source.projection` is checked by the older rule: SHA-256 of the raw spec text with `- [x]` read as `- [ ]`.
A plan whose projection name is unknown is refused with `unsupported source projection`.
A plan is refused as `verification plan is stale` when the spec's current hash differs from `source.contentHash`.
The plan path itself must be absolute.
A phase without a gate yields an empty context.

Only the current phase's obligations are rendered in full (`### <id> — <title>` with Level, Kind, Action, Oracle, Witness, Negative case); earlier phases' obligations are one-line entries under the inherited heading.
Phase context lists every command of the cumulative gate under `### Commands this phase's gate will execute`, with env prefix, cwd and timeout, ignoring `excludedCommandRefs`.
Generated scaffolds are TODO or skipped tests and the prompt context states they are never passing evidence.
Commands run with `shell=False`, the declared cwd, the process environment overlaid with the command's `env`, and the command's `timeoutSec`.
Captured stdout and stderr are cut to the first 64000 characters each.
A timeout records `exitCode: null`, `signal: TIMEOUT` and appends `command timed out` to stderr; a launch error records `signal: EXEC_ERROR`; both count as failed.
Command record fields: `commandId`, `declaredId`, `source`, `executable`, `args`, `env`, `cwd`, `exitCode`, `signal`, `durationMs`, `stdout`, `stderr`, `passed`.
A command passes only when its exit code is 0.
After a successful `build` command, every declared workspace export is recorded in `buildArtifacts` with `exists`, `sizeBytes`, `mtimeEpoch` and `fresh`; this record does not fail the gate.
Pre-stage commands are the phase's own commands with stage `prestage` or `both`; they are not cumulative.
A detached pre-stage command is started in its own session with stdin closed; it is never killed on its deadline, only reported as `deadline_exceeded` with signal `DEADLINE`.

A gate adopts a pre-stage result only for stage `prestage`, only when the record passed and is completed, the plan hash matches, the git revision is the same and the working tree is clean in both the document and the gate.
Reuse scope: `per-attempt` needs the same phase and attempt, `per-phase` the same phase, `per-run` neither.
An adopted record carries `reused: true` and `reusedFrom` with evidence path, stage, phase, attempt, plan hash, revision, reuse policy, run time and duration.
A phase without a gate in the plan fails with `gateId: missing-<phase>-gate` and summary `No verification gate exists for <phase>`.
A required gate with no executable command fails with summary `Required gate <id> has no safe executable verification commands`; an advisory gate with none passes.
A gate runs every selected command even after one fails, and passes only when all pass.
Gate evidence fields: `planId`, `planHash`, `gateId`, `phase`, `passed`, `sourceRevision`, `commands`, `buildArtifacts`, `summary`.
`verification_plan.py` emits no events itself; the events around it are emitted by the orchestrator.
`verification_release_passed` — field `evidence`.
`verification_start` — fields `phase`, `attempt`, `plan`.
`verification_failed` — fields `phase`, `attempt`, `rc`, `evidence`.
`verification_passed` — fields `phase`, `attempt`, `evidence`.
A failing plan creation halts the launch with `verification preflight failed (see <log>)` and the spec/config exit code.
`run_stop reason=release_verification` with fields `rc` and `evidence` is emitted when the release gate fails in mode `required`; the run exits with the rejects code.
Release gate evidence is `<run-dir>/verification/release.json`.
Gate evidence of a phase attempt is `<run-dir>/verification/phase-<N>-attempt-<M>.json`.

The gate-written feedback starts with `# Phase <N> deterministic verification gate rejected`, contains the failure digest under `## What actually failed` and ends with `The phase cannot be approved solely from the proposer or critic claim.`
When the digest helper fails the feedback says `(failure digest unavailable — read the evidence document below)`.
Only mode `required` passes `--required` to plan creation.

The unmet-criteria signature is the sorted unique set of `T` ids with at least two digits and an optional lowercase letter suffix found in the feedback, comma-joined; without any id it is `text:` plus the SHA-256 of the feedback without lines matching `^VERDICT <hex>:`.
The diagnostician is invoked with `SPECSTRIDE_ROLE=diagnostician` and without `--verification-plan` and `--max-rejects`.

In mode `required` the fixed-argv gate runs before the critic on every attempt; when it exits non-zero the critic is not called at all, the attempt result is forced to 10 and the orchestrator writes `GATE<N>-FEEDBACK.md` itself.
In modes `plan` and `required` the critic receives `--verification-plan`, so the obligations become criteria; in mode `plan` no command is executed and the verdict is the critic's alone.
