`python3 lib/banner.py` prints the startup splash (mark, name, caption and the gate rail) sized to the terminal.
`banner.py --states A,R,C,P,...` gives per-phase states (first letter, case-insensitive); unknown letters become `P`, missing states are pending, at most 40 are used.
`banner.py --phases N` sets the number of gates, clamped to 1..40.
`banner.py --plain` prints full-width ASCII with no escape codes (the run.log copy).
`banner.py --bg dark|light` forces the background.
`banner.py --color always|never|auto` (default `auto`).
`banner.py --no-motion` prints only the final frame.
`banner.py --rail-only` prints just the two rail lines (no mark, no name).
`banner.py --preview` prints every tier x background x depth plus the motion frames and the plain copy, and ignores `SPECSTRIDE_BANNER=off`.
`banner.py --cols N` / `--rows N` (hidden from help) override the detected terminal size (default 80x24).
`SPECSTRIDE_MOTION=0` disables animation.
`CI` set (non-empty) or `TERM=dumb` disables animation; animation also requires a TTY.
`SPECSTRIDE_BANNER` = `off`|`0`|`false`|`no` (case-insensitive) makes `banner.py` print nothing and also turns the live rail off.
`SPECSTRIDE_LIVE_RAIL` = `off`|`0`|`false`|`no` suppresses rail re-stamps: `banner.py --rail-only` prints nothing and the live timeline draws no rail.
`banner.py` exits 0 on every path, including when the banner is switched off; a closed pipe also exits 0.
The splash text is the name `specstride`, the description `From specs to tested code.` and the caption `Every step, signed off.`
Plain rail labels are `<n> ok` (approved), `<n> rej` (rejected), `<n> now` (current), `<n> -` (pending); the tight form uses `+`, `x`, `>`, `.`.
Width tiers: 72+ columns `full`, 40-71 `compact`, under 40 columns or under 14 rows `line` (one line).
The splash animation is 9 frames at 75 ms; only the two rail lines are redrawn, with the cursor hidden and synchronized-output escapes, and cursor/SGR restored on exit or SIGINT/SIGTERM.
With no `--phases` and no `--states` the rail is decorative: five gate posts, all in the brand color, no labels.
When the rail cannot fit the width it is replaced by a summary `<glyph><frontier>/<total>` (or `✓ n/n` when all approved).
In the one-line rail, runs of 3 or more equal states collapse to `<glyph>×<count>`.
`banner.py` falls back to plain ASCII output when stdout is not a TTY unless `--color always` is given; plain output is at least 80 columns wide and always the `full` tier.
`learn.py resolve --knob K --phase N --default D` is the shell integration point: it prints one line `<value><TAB><arm>` where arm is `applied` or `baseline`, and always exits 0.
`learn.py` requires one subcommand of `summarize`, `advise`, `apply`, `revert`, `off`, `resolve`, `observe`, `evaluate`; a missing or unknown one is an argparse usage error (exit 2).
`learn.py summarize` computes the metric summary from events streams and prints it as JSON (or writes it with `--out`).
`learn.py advise` prints one suggestion line per phase and writes nothing unless `--out` is given.
`learn.py apply` applies the current suggestion for one phase: it appends one decision to `applied.json` and one `knob_adjusted` event.
`learn.py revert <run_id>` undoes exactly one prior apply, restoring the value that was current before it.
`learn.py off` reverts every (knob, phase, shape) whose latest decision is an apply, one revert entry and one event each.
`learn.py observe --events ... --phase N [--out FILE]` writes the per-phase observation document (schema `specstride.learn.observation/1`) or prints it.
`learn.py evaluate` labels every active decision `helped`/`neutral`/`regressed`/`insufficient` against its recorded baseline.
`summarize --verification-dir DIR` attaches `gate_duration_ms` and `gate_live_share` per attempt from files named `phase-<N>-attempt-<M>.json`.
`summarize --verdicts-dir DIR` attaches `critic_prompt_bytes` per attempt from transcripts named `phase<N>.attempt<A>.<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>.txt`.
`summarize --run-log FILE` adds `totals.proposer_live_invocations`: the count of run.log lines starting `→ ` that match `--live-regex`.
`--feature-dir DIR` derives `<DIR>/learning/applied.json` and `<DIR>/events.jsonl`; explicit `--applied-file` / `--events-file` win.
`apply --force` applies a value an auto-revert quarantined; the entry then carries `force: true` and `forced_over: <auto-revert run id>`.
`summarize --out FILE` writes the JSON there (creating parent directories) and prints a one-line digest instead; `--pretty` indents by 2.
`--specs FILE` (with optional `--spec-format native|speckit-tasks|openspec-change`) computes every phase's shape digest through `specstride_spec`.
`--phase-shape DIGEST` keys `--phase` on that shape digest; it overrides the shape computed from `--specs` for that phase.
`--verdicts-dir DIR` for advise/apply/evaluate defaults to `<feature-dir>/verdicts` when that directory exists.
`advise/apply --events PATH` (repeatable) or `--summary FILE` (a `summarize --out` document) supplies the telemetry; `--summary` wins when both are given.
`advise --out FILE` also writes the advice rows as indented JSON.
`evaluate --report` is read-only: it prints the last recorded evaluation of every active decision, `learn: no active decisions`, or `...: not evaluated yet`.
`evaluate --dry-run` prints the evaluation and writes no entry, emits no event and reverts nothing.
`summarize --events PATH` (required, repeatable): an `events.jsonl`, a run directory holding one, or a directory of run directories (sorted by name).
`summarize --live-regex RE` defaults to `runners/live`.
`advise/apply/resolve --knob` accepts only `proposer_timeout` or `yield_poll_interval` (argparse choices); default `proposer_timeout` for advise/apply, required for resolve.
`advise --phase N` restricts to one phase; default is every phase seen.
`advise/apply/resolve --default N` (integer, required) is the global default the knob falls back to and the base of the step window.
`apply --phase N` is required (integer).
`apply --run-id ID` overrides the generated decision run id.
`evaluate --phase N` limits evaluation to decisions for that phase.
`SPECSTRIDE_LEARNING`: only the exact value `apply` makes `resolve` return a learned value; unset, `off`, `suggest` or anything else returns `--default` unchanged and the applied log is not opened.
`SPECSTRIDE_LEARNING_THROUGH=<decision run id>` makes `resolve` ignore every `apply` entry after the named entry; reverts after it still count; an id that names no entry means no apply counts at all.
`run_start` is read for `ts`, `feature`, `backend`, `resume`.
`phase_start` is read for `phase`, `title`, `shape`; it resets the current attempt and pass.
`proposer_start` is read for `phase`, `attempt` and sets the attempt start time.
`iter_start` is read for `iter`; it opens a pass in the current attempt.
`agent_tool` is read for `tool` and `target`; each counts one tool call, and a `Bash` target is classified wait vs work.
`agent_result` is read for `is_error`, `duration_ms`, `cost_usd`, `cache_creation_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `output_tokens`.
`yield_resume` is read for `job_duration_sec`, else `waited_sec`.
`pass_killed` is read for `reason` (default `unknown`), `elapsed`, `detail`.
`iter_done` is read for `evidence`; any value other than absent or `missing` marks the pass as having written evidence.
`evidence_written` increments the attempt's evidence count and marks the current pass productive.
`verification_passed` / `verification_failed` are read for `phase`, `attempt`, `rc` (failed only).
`critic_start` is read for its `ts`; `critic_sec` is the time to the following `verdict`.
`diagnostician_done` is read for `case` (default `unknown`).
`grounding_gap` is read for `paths` (comma-separated).
`verdict` is read for `phase`, `attempt`, `result`, `reason`.
`phase_done` and `attempt_archived` close an attempt that has no end time yet.
`proposer_cap` is read for `phase`, `seconds`, `source`, `yield_poll`, `yield_poll_source`, `arm`, `yield_poll_arm`, `tamper_bracket`; only the first per (run, phase) counts.
`events_tampered` marks the whole run as tampered; the run is excluded from every baseline and evaluation.
`run_stop` is read for `reason` and `phase`.
`knob_adjusted` (apply of `proposer_timeout`): fields `event`, `ts`, `knob`, `phase`, `from`, `to`, `reason`, `metric`, `samples`, `run_id`; no `time` field is written.
`knob_adjusted` (apply of `yield_poll_interval`): same fields, `metric=job_duration_p50`.
`knob_adjusted` (revert): fields `event`, `ts`, `knob`, `phase`, `from`, `to`, `reason`, `samples=null`, `metric=null`, `run_id`, `reverts_run_id`.
`knob_auto_reverted`: fields `event`, `ts`, `knob`, `phase`, `guardrail` (comma-joined names), `from`, `to`, `run_id`, `reverts_run_id`; emitted after the `knob_adjusted` of the same revert.
`knob_evaluated`: fields `event`, `ts`, `knob`, `phase`, `label`, `action`, `reset`, `cost_r`, `cost_mde`, `wall_r`, `wall_mde`, `n_applied`, `n_baseline`, `run_id`, `evaluates_run_id`.
`learn.py summarize` exits 2 with `learn: no events.jsonl found under: <paths>` on stderr when no events file is found.
`learn.py summarize` exits 0 on success.
`learn.py advise` exits 2 when neither `--events` nor `--summary` is given (`learn: one of --events or --summary is required`) or no events file is found.
`learn.py advise` exits 1 with `learn: no telemetry for phase <N>` / `learn: no telemetry for any phase` on stderr when there are no rows.
`learn.py advise` exits 0 when at least one row was printed, including rows with no suggestion.

`learn.py apply` exits 2 for a knob outside the allowlist (`learn: '<knob>' is not in the adjustable-knob allowlist (...) — refusing`), a missing summary/events input, or no `--applied-file`/`--feature-dir`.
`learn.py apply` exits 4 with `learn: refusing to apply — quarantined: <detail>` when the value is quarantined and `--force` is absent; nothing is written.
`learn.py apply` exits 3 with `learn: refusing to apply — <reason>` when the phase has no telemetry or is below the 3-sample floor; nothing is written.
`learn.py revert` exits 2 when no applied file can be derived, when the run id names no apply entry (`no applied entry with run_id '<id>'`), or when it is not the active decision.
`learn.py off` exits 0 (2 only when neither `--applied-file` nor `--feature-dir` is given).
`learn.py observe` exits 2 when no events file is found, else 0 (a phase with no telemetry is not an error: `observation` is null).

`learn.py evaluate` exits 2 when no applied file can be derived or when neither `--events` nor `--report` is given (`learn: --events is required (or --report)`); otherwise 0, also when there are no active decisions.
Apply refusal reason `fewer than 3 non-futility-killed samples (have <n>)` for `proposer_timeout`.
Apply refusal reason `fewer than 3 non-futility-killed job-duration samples (have <n>)` for `yield_poll_interval`.
Apply refusal reason `no telemetry for phase <N>`.
`knob_adjusted reason=learned_from_work_sec_p90` (apply of `proposer_timeout`).
`knob_adjusted reason=learned_from_job_duration_p50` (apply of `yield_poll_interval`).
`knob_adjusted reason=revert` (manual `revert` and `off`).
Revert refusal `run_id '<id>' is not the active decision for <knob>[<phase>] — nothing to revert`: only the entry currently on top of its (knob, phase, shape) stack may be undone.
Evaluation reason `no baseline recorded (applied before evaluate existed)` gives label `insufficient`.
Evaluation `reset=shape`: the phase's shape changed since the decision; label `insufficient`.
Evaluation `reset=backend`: the phase's latest run used another backend label than the baseline; label `insufficient` and applied-arm samples are discarded.
`knob_adjusted reason=auto_revert` (guardrail breach during evaluate).
`knob_evaluated action` is `evaluated`, `auto_reverted` or `skipped_superseded`.
The summary document has `schema` = `specstride.learn.summary/7`, `inputs`, `runs`, `attempts`, `phases`, `totals`.
Events files are read leniently: blank lines, non-JSON lines (a half-written tail) and JSON values without an `event` key are skipped.
Gate-duration files are JSON with a `commands` list; `durationMs` is summed and the `live` share is the part from commands whose `args` or `executable` contain `live`.
Verdict transcripts are read for the byte size of the section between the `═══════════ PROMPT ═══════════` and `═══════════ REPLY ═══════════` markers.
The applied-entry schema written is `specstride.learn.applied/2`; `/1` entries are still read but never match a shape.

`<feature-dir>/learning/applied.json` is a JSON-lines decision log opened in append mode (one entry per apply/revert/evaluate); the directory is created on demand and existing lines are never rewritten.
Learning events are appended to `<feature-dir>/events.jsonl` (the feature directory itself, not a run's `runs/<id>/events.jsonl`) unless `--events-file` is given.
An `apply` entry has the fields `schema`, `action=apply`, `run_id`, `knob`, `phase`, `shape`, `value`, `previous`, `samples`, `source_runs`, `metric`, `applied_at`, `baseline`.
A `revert` entry has `schema`, `action=revert`, a new `run_id`, `reverts_run_id`, `knob`, `phase`, `shape`, `value` (the apply's `previous`), `previous` (the apply's `value`), `applied_at`.

An apply entry's `baseline` holds `backend`, `shape`, `runs`, `cost` and `wall` sample lists of `[run, value]`, and `guardrails` counts; runs under another backend label or flagged tampered are left out.
An automatic revert entry additionally carries `auto: true`, `guardrail` (list), `evaluated_from`, `quarantined_value`, `backend`, `reverted_ts`.
An `evaluate` entry is the evaluation result plus `schema`, `action=evaluate`, a new `run_id` and `evaluated_at`; it never modifies the apply entry.

The observation document (`observe --out`, conventionally `<feature-dir>/learning/phase-<N>.json`) has `schema`, `phase`, `shape`, `generated_at`, `observation`, `inputs` and is overwritten whole on each call.

Decisions recorded without a phase shape print the stderr notice `learn: notice — <n> decision(s) for <knob>[<phase>] predate phase-shape keys and are not applied; re-derive with `specstride learn --apply` under the current spec`.
A primary below the floor prints `<name> n=<a>/<b> (need 6/6)`.

An evaluation prints `learn: phase <N> <knob> <prev>s→<value>s [<run-id>]: <label>[ (baseline reset: shape|backend) | (<reason>)] — cost r=... (MDE ±..., n=a/b); wall ...; guardrails ok (<k> unknown below their minimum n) | guardrails: BREACH <names>[ [<action>]]`.

`summarize --out` prints `learn: run(s), attempt(s),

pass(es), $, kills= → `.
A spec that cannot be read prints `learn: cannot read phase shapes from <specs>: <error>` on stderr and continues with no shape restriction.
A quarantined suggestion prints `learn: phase <N> <knob>: suggestion <v> is QUARANTINED — auto-reverted by <run-id> (<guardrails>); <k>/6 new samples since; --apply refuses without --force`.
Below the sample floor advise prints `learn: phase <N> <knob>: <n> sample(s) — <reason>; no suggestion (need >=3)`.

A `proposer_timeout` suggestion prints `learn: phase <N> proposer_timeout: <n> sample(s), work p50=<x>s p90=<y>s, current=<c>s → suggest <v>s (bounds=[lo, hi], step_cap=[lo, hi]) [not applied — run `specstride learn --apply` to take effect]`.
A `yield_poll_interval` suggestion prints `learn: phase <N> yield_poll_interval: <n> sample(s), job_duration p50=<x>s, current=<c>s → suggest <v>s (bounds=..., step_cap=...) [not applied — ...]`.
A successful apply prints `learn: applied <knob>[<phase>] <previous>s -> <value>s (samples=<n>, run_id=<id>) → <applied file>`.
A revert prints `learn: reverted <run-id> — <knob>[<phase>] back to <value>s`.
`off` prints one `learn: reverted ...` line per reverted decision, or `learn: nothing was applied — already at defaults`.
`off` always ends with the note that `SPECSTRIDE_LEARNING=off` (or unset) in the run's environment is what makes `resolve` ignore `applied.json`; the command only clears recorded decisions.
`observe --out` prints `learn: phase <N> observation — <a> attempt(s), work p50=<x>s p90=<y>s → <out>` or `learn: no telemetry for phase <N> yet → <out>`.
An automatic revert prints `learn: auto-reverted <run-id> — guardrail <names>; <knob>[<phase>] back to <value>s`.
`learn.py` applies the legacy-to-`SPECSTRIDE_*` environment name mapping at import.

A Bash target is a wait call when it matches `sleep <n>`, `tail -f|-c`, `while pgrep|true`, `until grep`, `pgrep -`, `ps aux ... grep` or `watch -n`, or declares any `sleep` seconds; declared sleep seconds are summed.
Kill classes: `hard_cap` = budget, `repeat_stall` and `progress_stall` = futility, `idle_timeout` = hang; other reasons = unknown.
Percentiles use linear interpolation between sorted samples and are rounded to 0.1.
Pass outcome: `budget_kill` (killed for `hard_cap`), `worker_error` (any other kill, or `is_error`), `open` (no result yet), `productive` (evidence written), else `clean_no_progress`.
A pass is billed when it is closed and its result carried `cost_usd`; while open `billed` is null.
`work_sec_estimate` = max(0, sum of pass elapsed − declared sleep seconds); attempts with any futility kill are excluded from the phase's `work_sec` samples.
Events without a `run_id` are attributed to the run id last seen in the same file; events seen before any run id in that file are dropped.
A transcript is matched to the (phase, attempt) whose verdict time is nearest to the transcript's local timestamp, within 900 s.
The evaluation sample unit is a billed pass that was not killed for futility.
With phase shapes given, a phase's figures use only attempts recorded under that shape; a phase with none is omitted from `phases`, and `other_shape_attempts` counts those left out.
The adjustable-knob allowlist is the locked literal set {`proposer_timeout`, `yield_poll_interval`}; a former third knob `inject_yield_hint` was removed.
Hard minimums: `proposer_timeout` 900 s, `yield_poll_interval` 10 s.
Hard maximums: `yield_poll_interval` 300 s fixed; `proposer_timeout` 2 x the supplied default.
Every numeric knob moves at most ±50 % per step from the value currently in effect (or the default when none is applied).
The `yield_poll_interval` target is 0.1 x the phase's `job_duration_p50`, clamped to the step window and [10, 300], rounded to a whole second.
The `ts` of learning events is the string form of `time.time()` (epoch seconds).
Generated decision run ids are `learn-` followed by 12 hex characters.
The effective value is a last-one-wins replay of the decision entries (`apply` and `revert`; `evaluate` entries never move a value; entries without `action` count as decisions).
With a `through` id that is not in the log, only `revert` entries are kept, so every knob resolves to its default.
A decision applies only to the phase shape it was learned under: a decision recorded under another shape, or under no shape, resolves to the default.
No suggestion is made (value null) with fewer than 3 samples: `work_sec_samples` for `proposer_timeout`.

The `proposer_timeout` target is 1.25 x the phase's `work_sec_p90` (p50 when p90 is missing), clamped to the step window and hard bounds, rounded to the nearest 60 s, then clamped to the hard bounds again.
When the step window and the hard bounds do not overlap, the hard bounds alone are used.
No `yield_poll_interval` suggestion is made with fewer than 3 `job_duration_samples`.
`resolve` clamps a stored value into [hard min, hard max] at read time and always prints an integer.
A primary (cost or wall) is `insufficient` unless both arms have at least 6 samples.
MDE = 2.80 x max(sd, 0.50) x sqrt(1/n_a + 1/n_b) x sqrt(1 + (mean passes per episode − 1) x 0.5).
Values are floored before the log: cost at 0.0001, wall at 1.0 s.
The effect r is the difference of mean log values (applied − baseline); `helped` when r <= −MDE, `regressed` when r >= MDE, else `neutral`.
The combined label is `regressed` if either primary regressed, else `helped` if either helped, else `neutral` if either is neutral, else `insufficient`.
The arbitration proxy counts episodes whose run stopped at the phase with reason `max_rejects`, `gate_oscillation`, `critic_config` or `proposer_no_progress`.

A run belongs to a decision's applied arm when its `proposer_cap` recorded arm `applied` with the decision's value and `tamper_bracket=on`; with no arm recorded, when the source is `learned` at that value. The decision's own source runs are never in its applied arm.
The counterfactual for `proposer_timeout` is `censored` for a longer cap, `shorter_cap_wall_only` for a shorter one, `none` otherwise; it never feeds the label.
The `critic_input_size` guardrail needs 6 prompt sizes per arm and breaches on an exact rank test with p < 0.01.

Quarantine: after an automatic revert, a suggested value within ±10 % of the reverted value for the same (knob, phase, shape, backend) is refused until 6 new non-futility samples from runs started after the revert exist.
The baseline rate is shrunk to (k + 0.5) / (n + 1).

Guardrail states are `ok`, `breach` or `unknown`; a rate guardrail is `unknown` below 10 applied-arm trials, and breaches when the exact one-sided binomial tail against the baseline rate is below 0.01.
The `verification` guardrail breaches at any n when the applied arm has a failed verification and the baseline had none; with no applied attempts it is `unknown`.
Guardrail names: `grounding_gap_rate`, `malformed_rate`, `verification`, `diagnostician_grounding_share`, `critic_input_size`, `arbitration_proxy`, `first_attempt_approval` (two-sided).
If a newer apply overtook the evaluated decision, the breach is recorded as `action_taken=skipped_superseded` and nothing is reverted; after a manual revert or `off` it is a silent no-op.
A guardrail breach makes a non-dry-run `evaluate` revert the decision automatically (the only automatic write to a decision), recording the evaluation with `action_taken=auto_reverted`.
An evaluation is recorded (entry + `knob_evaluated`) only when its signature (label, reset, action, arm sizes, guardrail states) differs from the last evaluation of the same decision.

The arm printed by `resolve` is `applied` when the latest bound decision for (knob, phase, shape) is an apply under `SPECSTRIDE_LEARNING=apply` (even if its value equals the default), else `baseline`.
`resolve` prints the shape-less-decisions notice on stderr only when `SPECSTRIDE_LEARNING=apply`.
`evaluate` without `--specs`/`--phase-shape` treats each decision's own recorded shape as the current shape, so no shape reset is reported.
`lib/present.py` is the live presenter: a pure consumer of one events.jsonl that never affects loop control flow.
`present.py --debug` makes the timeline print unknown events as a dim `<ts>  · <event> <json of other keys>` line.
`present.py --no-color` forces color depth `none`.
`present.py --workdir DIR` (default `.`) locates the events file when `--events` is absent.
`present.py --mode timeline|card|plain` (default `timeline`); any other value is an argparse error (exit 2).
`present.py --follow` tails the file for new events.
`present.py --detail milestones|tools|full` sets timeline verbosity; default `tools`.
`present.py --events PATH` names the events file; default is `<workdir>/<state dir>/events.jsonl`.
`present.py --quiet` prints each parsed event as one `json.dumps` line (JSONL passthrough) and takes precedence over `--mode`.
`SPECSTRIDE_LIVE_DETAIL` supplies the default of `--detail` (`milestones`, `tools` or `full`; default `tools`); an invalid value falls back to `tools`.
`_reopen` is a synthetic event made by the follower (never in the file); the timeline renders it as `── new run detected — following it ──`.
`run_start` is rendered as `┏ run start — <phases> phases · <proposer>→<critic> · resume @ phase <resume>`; fields read: `phases`, `proposer`, `critic`, `resume`, `workdir`, `states`.
`phase_start` is rendered as `◆ phase <phase>/<total>[ — <title>]`; fields read: `phase`, `total`, `title`.

`proposer_start` is rendered as `✱ proposer working — phase

, attempt , `; fields read: `phase`, `attempt`, `backend`.

`accelerator_start` is rendered as `✚ accelerator acting on the hint — phase

, attempt , [ · ]`; fields read: `phase`, `attempt`, `backend`, `criteria`.

`acceleration_note` is rendered as `↦ acceleration note written (phase

, attempt )`.
`iter_start` is rendered as `↻ pass <iter>/<max_iter>` (hidden at detail `milestones`); fields read: `iter`, `max_iter`.

`agent_init` is rendered as `● agent up — <provider> / <model>` (or `backend`) with optional `(session <session_id>, schema v<schema_version>, <tools> tools, updated)`; fields read: `provider`, `model`, `backend`, `session_id`, `schema_version`, `tools`, `update`.

`agent_tool` is rendered per `status`: `… <tool> progress`, `✓ <tool> done` / `✗ <tool> failed` for `end` (by `is_error`), else `<glyph> <tool>[ start]`; fields read: `tool`, `status`, `target`, `summary`, `targets`, `result_summary`, `is_error`, `duration_ms`.
`agent_text` is rendered only at detail `full` as `│ final|partial <text>`; fields read: `text`, `final_fragment`.
`evidence_writing` is rendered as `↑ evidence being written (<tool> <target>)[ · <match or detection_reason>]`.
`agent_diagnostic` is rendered as `! <code> — <message>`, red when `severity` is `error`/`fatal`, else yellow; fields read: `code`, `message`, `severity`.
`agent_observability` is rendered as `◈ observability <mode>[ — <reason>]` plus `provider_format`, `signals`/`supported_signals`, `role`; green for `structured`, red for `degraded`, yellow otherwise.

`telemetry_delivery` is rendered as `✓|! sink <sink> <status>[ — <reason>]` with `HTTP <http_status>`, `batch_id`, `<event_count> events`; a status other than `accepted`/`ok`/`success` counts as failed.

`agent_result` is rendered as `◦ pass done` or `◦ pass <status>` (error when `is_error` or status in `error`,`timeout`,`cancelled`,`degraded`) with `$cost`, tokens out/in, duration, turns, reason, source; fields read: `status`, `is_error`, `cost`/`cost_usd`, `output_tokens`, `input_tokens`, `duration_ms`, `turns`/`num_turns`, `reason`/`reason_code`, `source`.
`evidence_written` is rendered as `◇ evidence → <file>  (<iters> iter)`.
`evidence_present` is rendered as `◇ evidence present (resume → critic)`.

`diagnostician_trigger` is rendered as `! diagnosing phase

, after attempt — writing a hint for the next pass`.

`critic_start` is rendered as `┿ critic judging phase

, `.

`verdict` with `result=APPROVED` is rendered as `✓ APPROVED phase

`.

`verdict` with `result=REJECTED` is rendered as `✗ REJECTED phase

(attempt )[ — ]`; any other result is shown as `✗ MALFORMED` in yellow.
`reject` is consumed but never rendered by the timeline (the `verdict` line already covers it).

`attempt_archived` is rendered as `↦ archived rejected attempt (phase

)`.

`phase_done` is rendered as `◆ phase

done (attempt )`.

`git_checkpoint` is rendered as `⎇ git checkpoint (phase

)`.

`run_stop` with `reason=stop_flag` is rendered as `■ stopped cleanly at phase

— resume with: specstride resume`.

`run_stop` with any other reason is rendered as `■ halt — (phase

)`.
`run_end` is rendered as `■ run complete — <outcome>`.
`present.py` exits 0 on a closed pipe (BrokenPipeError), after redirecting stdout to the null device.
The presenter treats a stop as requested when `stop.flag` exists in the events file's directory or two levels above it.
Plain mode renders `agent_observability` as `<HH:MM:SS>  observability <mode>[ — <reason>]  <other k=v>`.
Plain mode prints one line per event: `<HH:MM:SS>  <event padded to 18> k=v ...`.
The rail's status tail is `<approved>/<total> approved[ · <extra>]`.
The re-stamped rail is indented 10 columns (the message column) and never wider than the terminal; under 40 columns it collapses to a one-line rail or a summary.
On `run_end` the TTY follow timeline prints a totals line `  Σ <$cost> · <tokens> tok out · <n> pass · <elapsed>`.
On a TTY in follow mode, after 2.0 s without a printed line a heartbeat line is drawn in place: `<spinner><pulse> <activity> · <dwell>  · run <totals>`, refreshed every 0.25 s.
While `stop.flag` exists the heartbeat status is `‖ stop requested — finishing current pass…`.
The card outcome line is `■ STOPPED — resume with: specstride resume` for `run_stop reason=stop_flag`, `■ HALT: <reason>` for other stops, and `■ <outcome>` (default `done`) for `run_end`.
The card shows the gate rail, `  phase <cur>/<total> (attempt n)  <title up to 40 chars>`, an activity line with spinner, `  run: <totals>`, a divider, a rolling feed and a footer.
The card footer is `  Ctrl-C to detach — the run keeps going`.
Plain mode prints `────── new run ──────` when the followed symlink is retargeted to a new run.
`present.py` applies the legacy-to-`SPECSTRIDE_*` environment name mapping at import (`specstride_env.apply()`).

Tool glyphs by tool name (case-insensitive): `read` ◎, `write` ✚, `edit`/`multiedit`/`notebookedit` ✎, `bash` ❯, `grep`/`glob`/`ls` ❍, `task`/`agent` », `webfetch`/`websearch` ⇆, todo/task-list tools ≡ (muted), `mcp__*` ◇, else ›.
The timestamp is the 8 characters after `T` in the event's `time`; else local time from `ts`; else `--:--:--`.
Token counts are shown as `<n>`, `<n.n>k` (>=1000) or `<n.n>M` (>=1,000,000); durations as `<s>s`, `<m>m<ss>s` or `<h>h<mm>m`.
Event booleans are truthy when a real `true` or one of the strings `1`, `true`, `yes`, `error`, `failed`, `failure` (case-insensitive).
Run totals add `agent_result` cost (`cost`, else `cost_usd`), `output_tokens` and `input_tokens`, and count one pass per `agent_result`.

The current-activity text is driven by `run_start`, `phase_start`, `proposer_start`, `accelerator_start`, `iter_start`, `agent_tool`, `agent_text`, `evidence_writing`, `agent_diagnostic`, `critic_start`, `verdict`, `run_stop` (`stopped`) and `run_end` (`complete`).
Detail level `milestones` hides `iter_start`, `agent_init`, `agent_tool`, `agent_diagnostic`, `agent_observability`, `telemetry_delivery` and `agent_result`.
A successful `telemetry_delivery` is shown only at detail `full`; a failed one is shown at `tools` and above.
Events with any other name produce no timeline line unless `--debug` is set.
Plain mode omits the keys `time`, `ts`, `event`, `task`, `backend`, `run_id` from the `k=v` list.
Without `--follow` a missing events file ends the presenter silently; with `--follow` it waits, polling every 0.3 s, until the file exists.
Lines that are not valid JSON are skipped silently by the presenter.
Follow mode polls every 0.4 s and, when the path's device/inode changes (symlink retargeted or file replaced), reopens the new file from the top.
`--quiet` output drops lines that are not valid JSON and, with `--follow`, includes a synthetic `{"event": "_reopen"}` object when the symlink is retargeted.
The gate rail is seeded from `run_start.states` (comma list of A/R/C/P) and `run_start.phases`; without `states` every phase starts pending.
A `verdict` REJECTED marks the phase `R` and re-stamps the rail with `attempt <attempt>/<max_rejects>` (field `max_rejects` or `MAX_REJECTS`); MALFORMED changes nothing on the rail.
`phase_done` marks the phase approved and re-stamps the rail with the elapsed time since `run_start`.
`run_end` marks every phase 1..total approved on the rail.
Two consecutive `run_stop` events with the same rail states stamp the rail only once.
The terminal size defaults to 100 columns by 24 rows when it cannot be detected.
Outside a TTY or without `--follow` the timeline prints lines and rails only: no spinner, no motion, no `Σ` summary.
The card feed keeps at most 200 lines, drops a line identical to the previous one, and shows the last `max(4, rows - 9)` of them.
A new `run_start` clears the card's outcome, so a card left open survives stop + resume.
The card shows `(attempt n)` only when the attempt is not 1.
Card mode clears the screen (`ESC[2J ESC[H`), replays the whole file once, then follows and redraws whenever events arrive or every 0.5 s.
Card mode forces color on (`always`) even off a TTY unless `NO_COLOR` is set or `--no-color` is given.
The presenter never queries the terminal for its background: it uses `SPECSTRIDE_BANNER_BG` or `COLORFGBG`, else dark.
`present.py` swallows KeyboardInterrupt (Ctrl-C) and ends normally.
`python3 lib/theme.py bg` prints `dark` or `light` once (treating the stream as interactive when stdin or stderr is a TTY).
`COLORTERM` equal to `truecolor` or `24bit` (case-insensitive) selects depth `truecolor`.
`TERM` containing `256color` selects depth `256`; otherwise depth is `16`.
`NO_COLOR` (set and non-empty) gives color depth `none` unless the caller passed `--color always|never`.
`FORCE_COLOR` (set and non-empty) enables color even when the stream is not a TTY; `NO_COLOR` is checked first.
`TERM=dumb` (or a non-TTY stream) gives color depth `none`.
`SPECSTRIDE_COLOR` = `none`|`16`|`256`|`truecolor` overrides the resolved color depth last, even over `--color` and `NO_COLOR`; other values are ignored.
`SPECSTRIDE_BANNER_BG` = `dark`|`light` fixes the background and skips detection.
`COLORFGBG`: the last `;` field, when numeric, means light if >= 11 else dark.
`TMUX` or `STY` set skips the terminal background query and yields `dark`.
`SPECSTRIDE_ASCII` set to anything but empty or `0` maps every glyph to ASCII.
`LC_ALL`, else `LC_CTYPE`, else `LANG`: a non-empty locale that does not contain `utf8`/`utf-8` forces ASCII glyphs.
`lib/theme.py` with any other arguments exits 1 printing `usage: theme.py bg` on stderr.
16-color SGR codes per role (dark, light): accent 95/35, approved 32/32, warn 33/33, reject 31/31, muted 90/2.
An explicit color argument `never` gives `none`; `always` gives the terminal's depth regardless of TTY, `NO_COLOR` or `FORCE_COLOR`.
Background detection on a TTY writes the OSC 11 query `ESC ] 11 ; ? ESC \` to `/dev/tty` in raw mode, waits up to 0.2 s, and classifies luminance >= 128 as light; the fallback is dark.
Color roles are `brand`, `accent`, `approved`, `warn`, `reject`, `muted`; `brand` always uses the terminal's own foreground (SGR 39).
Depth `256` quantises each role's hex color to the nearest xterm-256 index; `truecolor` emits `38;2;r;g;b`.
ASCII glyph substitutions: track `=`, ahead `-`, gate `+`, tip `>`, approved `ok`, rejected `x`, current `>`, pending `.`, times `x`, arrow `->`.
`specstride reverse <SRC> ...` and `specstride --reverse <SRC> ...` are the same entry point (`reverse_main`), handled before any other parsing.
`specstride run [flags]` replaces the front-door process with `bash orchestrator.sh` given every remaining argument (exec, so the exit code is the orchestrator's).
`specstride start [flags]` is an exact alias of `specstride run` (same `exec bash orchestrator.sh "$@"`).
A first argument that starts with `-` (other than `-h`/`--help`/`--reverse`) starts a run: all arguments, including that flag, are passed to `orchestrator.sh` via exec.
`specstride status [-w DIR] [--feature S]` prints a one-screen state and writes nothing.
`specstride status --all` prints one row per feature directory and exits 0.
`specstride tail` replaces itself with `tail -f <run.log>` of the selected run log.
`specstride events` renders the event stream through `lib/present.py --events <file> --mode plain`.
`specstride verdicts [N]` dumps every `*.txt` transcript in `<feature>/verdicts/`, or only `phase<N>.*.txt` when N is given.
`specstride feedback <N>` prints `<feature>/gates/GATE<N>-FEEDBACK.md` to stdout; it does not require the state directory check first.
`specstride watch` replaces itself with `present.py --workdir <workdir> --mode card`; it ignores `--feature` and always follows the workdir's root events symlink.
`specstride phases` lists every phase with its state; it needs only the spec file, not the state directory.
`specstride stop` requests a clean stop of the run on the workdir (mutating).
`specstride resume` relaunches the orchestrator from a saved config and replaces the front-door process with it.
`specstride learn [mode] [passthrough...]` dispatches to `lib/learn.py`; the mode is the first non-flag/unknown argument and defaults to `--show`.
`specstride`, `specstride -h`, `specstride --help` and `specstride help` print the inspection usage to stdout and exit 0.
An unknown subcommand prints `specstride: unknown subcommand '<SUB>'` and the usage text to stderr.
`reverse --src <DIR>` is forwarded to the linter as `--src` (lint mode only).
`reverse --upto <N>` is forwarded to the linter as `--upto` (lint mode only).
`reverse --dry-run` prints the plan summary and the orchestrator command without launching anything.
`reverse -h` / `--help` prints the front-door usage and exits 0.

`reverse` passes these launch flags with their value through to the orchestrator: `--proposer`, `--critic`, `--max-rejects`, `--max-iter`, `--proposer-timeout`, `--proposer-timeout-phase`, `--critic-timeout`, `--start-phase`, `--loki-url`, `--otel-url`, `--long-job-phase`, `--long-job-cmd`.
Any other `-*` argument to `reverse` is passed through to the orchestrator as a valueless flag.
`reverse --json` is forwarded to the linter as `--json` (lint mode only).
`reverse --lint <FEATURE_DIR>` switches to lint mode and execs `python3 lib/reverse.py lint <dir>` (no LLM, no run).
`reverse --mode <value>` accepts only `source-aware` (or absence); any other value is refused.
`reverse --out <DIR>` is forwarded to `reverse.py plan --out`.
`reverse --name <SLUG>` is forwarded to `reverse.py plan --name`.
`reverse --tasks done|open` is forwarded to `reverse.py plan --tasks`.
`-w DIR` / `--workdir DIR` selects the project workdir for every inspection subcommand; default is `$PWD`; a missing value aborts through `${2:?}`.
`-s SPEC` / `--specs SPEC` selects the spec file for inspection subcommands and marks it explicit; default is `<workdir>/SPECS.md`.
`--feature SLUG` selects the feature namespace under `<state>/features/`; missing value aborts through `${2:?}`.
`--all` (used by `status`) lists every feature; it also makes `need_state` skip the per-feature directory check.
`-f` / `--follow` (used by `events`) follows the stream for new events.
`--json` (used by `events`) switches the event output to one JSON object per line.
`--now` (used by `stop`) additionally kills the in-flight agent pass.
`-h` / `--help` anywhere after an inspection subcommand prints usage and exits 0 without running the subcommand.
`specstride events -f` adds `--follow` to the presenter call.
`specstride events --json` runs `present.py --events <file> --quiet` (one JSON object per line).
`learn --show` (default) runs `learn.py advise` then `learn.py evaluate --report`; the exit code is that of `advise` (the report's failure is ignored).
`learn --apply [--phase N ...]` execs `learn.py apply --feature-dir <feature> [--events ...] [--specs ...]` with the pass-through arguments.
`learn --summarize` execs `learn.py summarize --events <runs dir>` (read-only, JSON on stdout).
`learn --evaluate` execs `learn.py evaluate --dry-run --events <runs dir> --feature-dir <feature>`: it prints what evaluate would conclude and writes nothing.
`learn --revert <run-id>` execs `learn.py revert <run-id> --feature-dir <feature>`.
`learn --off` execs `learn.py off --feature-dir <feature>`.
`reverse` exports `SPECSTRIDE_GIT_COMMITS=off` before launching the orchestrator, so a reverse run never commits into the source repo.
`resume` exports `SPECSTRIDE_GIT_COMMITS` from the conf key `GIT_COMMITS` when non-empty (it is env-only, not a flag).
`SPECSTRIDE_YIELD_POLL` (default 30) is injected as `--default` for `learn --show/--apply` when `--knob yield_poll_interval` is passed and no `--default` was given.
`SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_TIMEOUT` (default 1800) is injected as `--default` for `learn --show/--apply` when the knob is `proposer_timeout` and no `--default` was passed.

`reverse` exits 3 with `specstride reverse: <flag> is set by the reverse run itself; it cannot be passed` for `-w`, `--workdir`, `-s`, `--specs`, `--spec-format`, `--feature`, `--verification`, `--verification-commands`, `--test-plan`, `--generate-tests`.
`reverse` exits 2 with `specstride reverse: unexpected argument '<arg>'` on a second positional argument.

`reverse --mode <other>` exits 3 with a stderr message starting `specstride reverse: Runtime-assisted reverse engineering requires an explicit permission and side-effect policy` (`Black-box` when the mode is `black-box`).
`reverse` without SRC (and without `--lint`) exits 2 with a `usage: specstride reverse <SRC> ...` line on stderr.
`reverse` exits with the exit code of `reverse.py plan` when planning fails.
`reverse --dry-run` exits 0.
Any subcommand guarded by `need_state` (status, tail, events, verdicts, watch, stop, resume, learn) exits 1 when the state directory is missing.
A `need_state` subcommand exits 1 when the selected feature directory does not exist (unless `--all`).
`specstride status` exits 0 after printing (the embedded python helpers are `|| true`).
`specstride tail` exits 1 with `no run.log yet for feature '<slug>' in <state>` on stderr when the log is missing.
`specstride events` exits 1 with `no events.jsonl yet in <state>` on stderr when the stream does not exist.
`specstride verdicts` exits 1 with `no verdicts recorded yet (<dir>)` when the verdicts directory is missing.
`specstride verdicts N` exits 1 with `no verdicts for phase <N>` when no transcript matches.
`specstride feedback` without N exits 1 with `usage: specstride feedback <N> [-w DIR]` on stderr.
`specstride feedback N` exits 1 with `no feedback for phase <N> (<path>)` on stderr when the file is missing.
`specstride phases` exits 1 with `no SPECS.md in <workdir>` on stderr when the spec file does not exist.
`specstride phases` exits 3 after printing `SPEC INVALID:` and the validator's stderr when the spec does not validate.
`specstride stop` exits 0 in every branch once the state directory and feature exist (its last command is an `echo`).
`resume --feature X` exits 1 with `specstride resume: no last-run config for feature '<slug>' (<path>).` when the feature's conf is missing.
Bare `resume` exits 1 with `specstride resume: no <conf> — launch the run once via orchestrator.sh first.` when the root conf is missing.
`resume` exits 1 with `specstride resume: a run is already ACTIVE on <workdir> (lock held) — nothing to resume.` when the lock is held.
`specstride learn --revert` without a run id exits 1 with `usage: specstride learn --revert <run-id>` on stderr.
`specstride learn <unknown mode>` exits 1 with `specstride learn: unknown option '<mode>' (expected --show|--apply|--revert <run-id>|--off|--summarize|--evaluate)`.
`specstride <unknown subcommand>` exits 1.

`run_stop reason=stop_flag` is shown by `status` as `state: STOPPED at phase

— resume with: specstride resume`.

`run_stop reason=max_rejects` is shown by `status` as `state: HALTED at phase

— needs human (max-rejects exceeded)`.
`run_stop reason=proposer_yield_budget` is shown by `status` as a HALTED line saying a declared yield's wait ran out and the job was left running.
`run_stop reason=proposer_yield_timeout` gets the same `status` text as `proposer_yield_budget`, pointing at `.specstride/features/*/yield-jobs/`.
`run_stop reason=proposer_cap_exhausted` is shown by `status` as HALTED with the remedy `--long-job-cmd` or splitting the phase (consecutive `hard_cap` kills).
`reverse` sources `<install dir>/.env` when present; values the caller already exported win (the caller's environment is re-applied after sourcing).
The state directory is `<workdir>/<STATE_BASENAME>` where the basename is `.specstride` or a legacy directory name chosen by `specstride_resolve_state_dir`.
The root `<state>/last-run.conf` is read (first `FEATURE=` line, quotes stripped) to choose the default feature of every inspection command.
Per-feature state is read from `<state>/features/<slug>/` and gate files from `<state>/features/<slug>/gates/`.
Without `flock` the run lock is detected through the directory `<state>/lock.d`.
`status` reads the first 200 bytes of `<state>/lock` as the lock owner line.
`status` reads `TELEMETRY`, `OTEL`, `LOKI_URL`, `OTEL_URL` from the feature's `last-run.conf`, falling back to the root `last-run.conf`.
`verdicts` reads `<state>/features/<slug>/verdicts/*.txt`.
`phases` writes the validator's stderr to the fixed path `/tmp/specstride-spec-err` and deletes it afterwards.
`specstride stop` creates/touches `<state>/stop.flag` (per workdir, not per feature).
`stop --now` reads `<state>/proposer.pid`.
Bare `resume` sources the root `<state>/last-run.conf`; `resume --feature X` sources `<state>/features/<X>/last-run.conf`.
The usage text is lines 2-54 of the front-door script itself with the leading `# ` stripped (so the header comment is the user-visible help).
The `--mode` refusal ends `Specstride will not infer those permissions; only --mode source-aware is supported.`
`reverse --dry-run` starts with `specstride reverse — dry run (no LLM call, nothing launched)`.

`reverse --dry-run` prints labelled lines `source`, `inventory` (files/skipped/bytes/oversize/units), `languages`, `frameworks`, `constitution`, `output dir`, `tasks mode`, `inventory`, `driver`, `commands`, then `phases:` with `<n>. <title>  (lint --upto <level>)`.
`reverse --dry-run` ends with `  orchestrator (not executed):` and the shell-quoted command prefixed `SPECSTRIDE_GIT_COMMITS=off`.
`reverse` prints `reverse: launching <argv>` before exec.
A missing state directory prints `no .specstride/ state dir in <workdir>` to stderr.
A missing feature prints `no feature '<slug>' in <workdir> (<state>/features/<slug> missing).` followed by `known features:` and one `  - <name>` line per existing feature, all on stderr.
`status --all` starts with `specstride status --all — <workdir>`.
`status --all` prints `  (no features yet)` when `<state>/features` does not exist.
`status --all` prints a table with columns `FEATURE`, `PHASES`, `STATE` (widths 32, 10).
`status --all` STATE is `running/crashed` when the feature's newest events file holds no `run_stop`/`run_end`.
`status --all` STATE is `DONE:<outcome>` when the last terminal event is `run_end`.
`status --all` STATE is `HALTED:<reason>@<phase>` when the last terminal event is `run_stop`.
`status --all` STATE is `—` when the feature has no events file; each row shows `<approved>/<total>`.
`status` starts with `specstride status — <workdir>  (feature: <slug>)`.
`status` prints `  state: RUNNING (<owner>)` when the lock is held; the owner is the first line (at most 200 bytes) of `<state>/lock`.
`status` prints `  state: not running (no clean end recorded — crashed or never finished a run)` when no `run_stop`/`run_end` exists.
`status` prints `  state: DONE — <outcome>` from `run_end.outcome`.

Any other `run_stop` reason is shown by `status` as ` state: HALTED at phase

— `.
`status` prints `  state: no run recorded yet` when no events file exists and no lock is held.
`status` prints a phase table with columns `PHASE`, `TITLE` (truncated to 28), `EVIDENCE`, `APPROVED`, `FEEDBACK`.
`status` prints `  current phase: <n>` (first unapproved phase) or `  current phase: <all approved>`.
`status` prints `  (no SPECS.md found)` when the resolved spec file does not exist.
`status` prints a `  telemetry:` section only when `TELEMETRY` or `OTEL` is `true` in the saved config, one line per enabled sink from `specstride_telemetry_status_line`.
`status` prints `  observability: <mode>[ — <reason>]` from the last `agent_observability` event among the last 400 lines.
`status` prints `  latest tool: <tool>[ (<summary or status>)]` from the last `agent_tool` event among the last 400 lines.
`status` prints `  last events:` followed by the last 5 non-`agent_*`, non-`iter_*` events of the last 200 lines.
Each `last events` line is `<last 8 chars of time>  <event>  k=v ...`, omitting keys `time`, `ts`, `event`, `task`, `backend`, `run_id`.
Each transcript is framed by a rule line of 64 `═`, `# <path>`, the rule again, the file content and a blank line.
`phases` prints `<spec path> — <count> phase(s):` then `  Phase <n> <title, 40 cols> [<state>]` per phase.
`stop` prints `stop requested → <state>/stop.flag`.
`stop --now` prints `killed in-flight agent pass (pid <pid> + descendants)` after killing.
`stop --now` prints `recorded pass (pid <pid or ?>) is not running — nothing to kill` when the pid is dead or empty.
`stop --now` prints `no in-flight pass recorded (<path> missing) — flag-only stop` when `proposer.pid` is absent.
`stop --now` ends with `the run will exit 6 (clean stop) momentarily; resume with: specstride resume -w <workdir>`.
`stop` without `--now` prints `the run finishes its current pass, then exits 6 (clean stop).` and a resume / `stop --now` hint.
`resume` prints `resuming: <orchestrator> <args>` before exec.
The front door sources `specstride-lib.sh` from its own directory at startup and runs with `set -uo pipefail` (no `-e`).
`reverse` reads the plan JSON keys `src`, `driver`, `feature`, `verification_commands`, `test_plan`, `generate_tests` to build the launch.
A reverse run launches `orchestrator.sh -w <src> -s <driver> --spec-format native --feature <feature> --verification-commands ... --test-plan ... --generate-tests ...` plus pass-through flags.
Every argument that is not a recognised flag is collected as a pass-through extra, in order; the first extra is the positional `N` / learn mode.
A relative `-s` path is resolved against the directory the command was launched from, not against the workdir.
The workdir is canonicalised with `cd && pwd`; if that fails the raw value is kept and later checks report the missing state dir.
When `-s` is absent the inspection spec defaults to `<workdir>/SPECS.md`.
A `--feature` value is sanitised: every character outside `A-Za-z0-9._-` becomes `-` and leading/trailing `-` are trimmed.
Feature selection order for inspection commands: `--feature` (sanitised), else `FEATURE=` in the root `last-run.conf`, else `default`.
When `-s` was not given and `<workdir>/SPECS.md` does not exist, the spec for read-only commands is the `SPECS=` value of the feature's `last-run.conf` if that file exists.
`lock_held` means: with `flock` available, `<state>/lock` exists and a non-blocking `flock -n` on it fails; without `flock`, the directory `<state>/lock.d` exists.
`kill_tree` uses signal TERM only (no KILL escalation) and ignores kill failures.
With `--feature`, status/events read the feature's newest `runs/*/events.jsonl` by modification time; without it they read the root `<state>/events.jsonl` symlink (the last run of any feature).
With `--feature`, `tail` reads the feature's newest `runs/*/run.log` by modification time; without it the root `<state>/run.log` symlink.
In `status --all` the approved count is the number of `gates/GATE*-APPROVED` files of the feature.
In `status --all` the phase total comes from validating the `SPECS=` file of the feature's `last-run.conf` with format auto-detection; it is `?` when the conf or spec is missing or invalid.
`status` derives the run state from the LAST `run_stop` or `run_end` event in the events file; unparsable lines are skipped.
The phase table marks `✓`/`✗` by file existence of `GATE<n>-EVIDENCE.md`, `GATE<n>-APPROVED`, `GATE<n>-FEEDBACK.md` in the feature's gates directory.
The telemetry status lines default the endpoints to `http://localhost:3100` (loki) and `http://localhost:4318` (otel) when the saved URL is empty.
`status` scans only the last 400 lines of the events file for observability and tool state.
`events --feature S` with no run of that feature falls back to the root `<state>/events.jsonl`.
`verdicts` with no N and an empty verdicts directory prints nothing and exits 0.
Phase state precedence in `phases`: `pending`, then `evidence-written`, then `rejected(has-feedback)`, then `APPROVED` (the later file wins).
`stop` with no lock held still writes `stop.flag` and warns on stderr `no run appears to be active on <workdir> (lock is free).` plus `writing stop.flag anyway (a starting run will honor it).`
`stop --now` reads the pid in `<state>/proposer.pid` and, if that process is alive, sends TERM to it and recursively to all its descendants (children first via `pgrep -P`).
`resume` checks that the conf exists BEFORE checking the lock, so a missing conf is reported even while a run is active.
`resume` sources the conf as shell code (`. "$CONF"`), so its `WORKDIR`, `SPECS` and `FEATURE` values overwrite the values parsed from the command line before the launch arguments are built.
`resume` uses the conf's `ORCHESTRATOR` path when that file exists, else the `orchestrator.sh` beside the front door.
`resume` always replays `-w $WORKDIR -s $SPECS --proposer $PROPOSER_BACKEND --critic $CRITIC_BACKEND --max-rejects $MAX_REJECTS --max-iter $MAX_ITER`.
`resume` does not replay the conf key `VERIFICATION_PLAN`, a critic timeout, `--start-phase`, `--live`/`--no-live` or `--debug`; those fall back to env/defaults.
`resume` replays `--feature $FEATURE` only when the conf key is non-empty.
`resume` replays `--spec-format $SPEC_FORMAT` only when the key is non-empty (older confs auto-detect).
`resume` replays `--verification $VERIFICATION` when non-empty.
`resume` replays `--test-plan $TEST_PLAN` when non-empty.
`resume` replays `--verification-commands $VERIFICATION_COMMANDS` when non-empty.
`resume` replays `--generate-tests $GENERATE_TESTS` when non-empty.
`resume` replays `--proposer-timeout $PROPOSER_TIMEOUT` when non-empty.
`resume` replays one `--proposer-timeout-phase <item>` per whitespace-separated item of `PROPOSER_TIMEOUT_PHASES`.
`resume` replays `--telemetry --loki-url $LOKI_URL` only when `TELEMETRY` is exactly `true`.
`resume` replays `--otel --otel-url $OTEL_URL` only when `OTEL` is exactly `true`.
`resume` replays `--long-job-phase` and `--long-job-cmd` only when BOTH `LONG_JOB_PHASE` and `LONG_JOB_CMD` are non-empty.
Extra arguments given to `resume` are appended after the replayed flags, so they override the saved config (the orchestrator parses last-wins).
`learn` feeds learn.py the directory `<feature>/runs` (every run of the feature) when it exists, else the single newest events stream.
`learn` passes `--specs <spec>` when the spec file exists and `--spec-format <fmt>` from the feature's `last-run.conf` `SPEC_FORMAT=` line, so samples are keyed on the current phase shape.
`reverse.py` requires a subcommand (`plan`, `lint` or `guard`); none or an unknown one is an argparse usage error (exit 2).
`python3 lib/reverse.py plan <SRC>` writes the inventory, the driver spec and the verification-commands document, then prints the plan as JSON on stdout; it never calls an LLM.
`python3 lib/reverse.py lint <FEATURE_DIR>` runs the deterministic Spec Kit linter over a feature directory and prints findings.
`python3 lib/reverse.py guard <SRC> --baseline <inventory.json> --out <DIR>` re-walks the source and fails when anything outside the output dir and state dir changed.
`guard --baseline` is required (argparse exit 2 when missing); an unreadable or non-JSON file fails with `cannot read inventory <path>: <error>` (exit 3).
`guard --baseline` and `lint --baseline` reject a JSON document that is not an object with `fingerprint` and `files` keys: `not an inventory: <path>` (exit 3).
`plan` positional `src`: the source directory; a path that is not a directory fails with `source is not a directory: <src>` (exit 3); it is resolved with realpath.
`plan --name SLUG`: the run name, slugified; default is the basename of the source directory.
`lint` positional `feature_dir`; a missing directory fails with `feature directory not found: <dir>` (stderr `reverse: ...`, exit 3).
`lint --upto N` (int, default 5) selects the lint level; a value outside 0..5 fails with `--upto must be one of 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5` (exit 3); a non-integer is an argparse error (exit 2).
`lint --baseline INV` loads an inventory.json so citations resolve against the inventory's file list and line counts instead of the live filesystem.
`lint --src SRC` enables evidence citation checks against the source; a non-directory fails with `--src is not a directory: <src>` (exit 3).
`plan --out DIR`: output feature directory, made absolute; default `<SRC>/specs/NNN-as-is-<slug>`.
`plan --tasks done|open` (argparse `choices`, so any other value exits 2); default None, which falls back to `SPECSTRIDE_REVERSE_TASKS`, then `done`.
`lint --upto` default is 5.
`lint --claims FILE` additionally lints a scratch claims file (used by level-0 unit phases of an oversize run).
`lint --json` prints the findings as one JSON object `{errors:[...], warnings:[...]}` (indent 1, sorted keys) instead of text lines.
`guard` positional `src` is the source tree to re-walk (realpath).
`guard --out` is required; it is the output directory excluded from the comparison and named in the failure line.
`SPECSTRIDE_CONTEXT_BUDGET` (positive integer, default 24000) caps the character size of the INVENTORY.md that `plan` writes; a non-positive or non-integer value fails the plan (exit 3).

`SPECSTRIDE_REVERSE_TASKS` (values `done` or `open`, default `done`; empty counts as `done`) sets the tasks mode of `plan` when `--tasks` is not given; the legacy-prefixed variable is read as a fallback.
An invalid `SPECSTRIDE_REVERSE_TASKS` fails `plan` with `SPECSTRIDE_REVERSE_TASKS must be done or open (got '<v>')` and exit 3.
`reverse.py` documents exit codes as 0 ok, 3 findings or invalid input, 2 usage (argparse).
`reverse.py` exit 3 (`E_FINDINGS`) is the single code for findings and for invalid input.
`reverse.py plan` exits 0 after printing the plan JSON.
`reverse.py lint` exits 3 when there is at least one error finding and 0 otherwise; warnings alone never fail the linter.
`reverse.py guard` exits 3 when at least one problem was found.
`reverse.py guard` exits 0 when the source is untouched.
Any `ReverseError` or `InventoryError` in any subcommand is written to stderr as `reverse: <message>` and exits 3.
Refusal `--out cannot be the source root itself; choose a dedicated output folder: <out>`.
Refusal `--out must be inside the source tree <src> (got <out>)`.
Refusal `--out cannot be inside the project's .git directory: <out>` (first path component is `.git`).
Refusal `--out cannot be inside the state directory <name>/: <out>` when the first path component is the active state dir name, `.specstride`, the legacy state dir name or `.lisa`.
Refusal `--out cannot be inside .specify/ (the run never touches it): <out>`.
Refusal `--out exists and is not a directory: <out>`.
Refusal `--out already exists and is not empty: <out> (resume an existing reverse run with specstride resume --feature reverse-<slug>)`; an existing EMPTY directory is accepted.

`plan` writes `<run_state>/INVENTORY.md` atomically, rendered from the inventory under the context budget.

`plan` prints one JSON object on stdout with indent 1 and sorted keys.

Failure line `guard: FAILED — <n> change(s) outside <out> and the state dir`.

Feature layout: `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `research.md`, `data-model.md`, `quickstart.md`, `tasks.md`, `checklists/requirements.md`, `memory/constitution.md`, plus `contracts/*.md` as the only pattern.
Lint level 0 owns no artifact: it is the level of an oversize run's unit phases, which only write a claims file checked with `--claims`.
Lint level 1 owns `spec.md`, `checklists/requirements.md` and `memory/constitution.md`.
Lint level 2 owns `plan.md` and `research.md`.
Lint level 3 owns `data-model.md`, the `contracts/` directory and `quickstart.md`.
Lint level 4 owns `tasks.md`.
Lint level 5 owns no new artifact; it adds the FR-coverage check across spec.md and tasks.md.
Template-driven checks apply to five artifacts: spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md, checklists/requirements.md and memory/constitution.md, each mapped to its `*-template.md`.
The evidence comment is `<!-- evidence: <citations> | kind=... | confidence=... | contradicts=... | validation=... -->` on one line.
A citation is `path:START` or `path:START-END`; the path holds no whitespace, comma or `|`.
Allowed `kind` values: `observed`, `inferred`, `declared`.
Allowed `validation` values: `verified`, `unverified`, `disproved`.
`confidence` must match `0.dd` or `1.00` (exactly two decimals).
The tasks mode is read from the marker `<!-- specstride-reverse: tasks=<mode> -->`; without a marker no box-state check is made.
An FR line must match `- **FR-ddd**: <text>` at column 0.
An SC line must match `- **SC-ddd**: <text>` at column 0.
The story heading grammar allows a trailing target emoji suffix after the priority.
Task line grammar: `- [ |x|X] Tddd`, optional ` [P]`, optional ` [USn]` (in that order), then a description that does not start with another `[P]`/`[USn]` marker; task id is exactly 3 digits.
A research claim is a line starting (after an optional `-`/`*` bullet) with `**Decision**`.
A data-model claim is every `### ` (exactly level 3) heading; each needs an evidence comment on the next line.
The fixed placeholder list is seven patterns.
`MAX_CLARIFICATIONS` is 3.
The state directory name used by reverse is resolved silently (the legacy-dir notice is sent to a discarded stream).
`SLUG_MAX` is 40.
Policy: source-aware mode; source, configuration, tests, schemas, documentation, manifests and Git history are read-only evidence.
Policy: no network access, no dependency install, no services, containers or daemons.

Policy: the product, its tests, builds, generators, migrations, linters and formatters are not executed; only read-only discovery (`ls`, `cat`, `grep`, `find`, `wc`) and `git log`/`git show`/`git blame` are allowed.
Policy: the only permitted writes are the output directory and the state directory; never touch `.specify/`, never write `.specify/feature.json`, never create a git branch or commit.
Policy: describe current behaviour only; no To-Be design, no remediation or enhancement backlog.

Policy: evidence precedence is executable source, schemas and configuration > tests > templates and command definitions > user docs > comments and git history; a disagreement lowers confidence and is recorded in `contradicts=`.
Policy: every linter-checked claim (each FR, SC, research Decision, data-model entity heading) carries an evidence comment on the line directly after it.

Policy: evidence paths are relative to the source, ranges must exist in the file, and at most 3 `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION` markers are allowed in spec.md; other unknowns go under Assumptions with `validation=unverified`.
The slug is lower-cased, every run of characters outside `a-z0-9` becomes `-`, leading/trailing `-` are stripped, and it is cut to 40 characters (`SLUG_MAX`).
An empty slug (nothing usable in the name) becomes `project`.
Output-dir containment is judged on realpaths, so a symlinked `--out` that resolves outside the source is refused.
An oversize run prepends one level-0 phase per inventory unit, titled `Investigate unit <path> (1<letter>)`, before the specification phase.
In an oversize run the specification phase is titled `Synthesis — constitution and specification` or `Synthesis — specification`.
Phase 1 title is `Constitution and specification` when a constitution must be written, else `Specification`.
A non-oversize run has 5 driver phases, numbered from 1: specification (level 1), `Plan and research` (2), `Design artifacts` (3), `Tasks (<mode>)` (4), `Cross-artifact analysis and sign-off` (5).
Tasks phase title carries the mode: `Tasks (done)` or `Tasks (open)`.
Driver phases are numbered contiguously from 1 in list order (the phase number is also the gate number).
Unit phase letters run a..z; from the 27th unit on the suffix is `-<index+1>`.
The unit key used in claims file names is `root` for unit `.`, else the unit path with every run outside `A-Za-z0-9._-` replaced by `-`.
Every driver phase names `<run_state>/INVENTORY.md` (full record inventory.json) as ground truth for what exists and tells the agent not to re-derive it.
The policy is repeated verbatim inside every phase (`### Policy`), not only in the run boundaries.
The `### Gate` block lists the phase's lint command and the guard command in a bash fence and tells the agent to run them first and fix every error before writing evidence.
The driver tells the agent to keep `GATE<n>-EVIDENCE.md` short (critic grounding budget 32 KB), to paste the linter's `--json` output and to cite artifacts by workdir-relative path.
Acceptance criteria are emitted as unticked `- [ ] ` checkbox lines; every phase's list ends with `<lint command> exits 0.` and `<guard command> exits 0.`.

Unit phase work: investigate only that unit and append claims, one per line as `- <claim>` each followed by its evidence comment, to `<run_state>/claims-<unit-key>.md`; nothing is written under the output dir.
Oversize specification phase work: synthesize from the scratch claims files `<run_state>/claims-*.md`.
When the source has no constitution the spec phase writes `<out>/memory/constitution.md` from the constitution template with principles recovered from evidence.
When the source has a constitution the spec phase reads it and must not copy it into the output.

Spec phase work prescribes the spec.md grammar: `### User Story <n> - <title> (Priority: P<n>)` numbered from 1, **Why this priority**, **Independent Test**, a Given/When/Then scenario, `- **FR-###**:` and `- **SC-###**:` lines with evidence comments.
Spec phase work prescribes `checklists/requirements.md`: every item evaluated `[x]`, or `[ ]` followed by an indented `Fails:` line carrying an evidence comment.
Spec phase work forbids leaving any template placeholder, sample text or template HTML comment behind.

Plan phase work: write plan.md from the plan template with real Technical Context, Constitution Check and structure; delete `[REMOVE IF UNUSED]` options; keep Complexity Tracking as a heading with None.
Plan phase work: research.md is a list of `- **Decision**: ...` entries each followed by an evidence comment, then Rationale and Alternatives; an unrecoverable rationale is written `unknown`.
Design phase work: data-model.md has one `### <Entity>` heading per entity, each followed by its evidence comment.
Design phase work: `contracts/*.md`, one file per external surface that exists (CLI, HTTP API, events, files on disk, config/env).
Design phase work: quickstart.md commands come from manifests and docs and each is labelled not executed by the reverse run.
Tasks phase work: every task box is `[x]` in `done` mode (work that already exists) and `[ ]` in `open` mode (a rebuild step).

Tasks phase work prescribes phases `## Phase 1: Setup`, `## Phase 2: Foundational`, one `## Phase <n>: User Story <k> - <title> (Priority: P<k>)` per story in priority order, then a final numbered Polish phase.
Tasks phase work requires each `FR-###` to be mentioned in at least one task description, e.g. `(FR-003)`.
Tasks phase work requires the marker comment `<!-- specstride-reverse: tasks=<mode> -->` on its own line right after the front matter, and the template's YAML front matter to be kept.
Common criteria are the two lines `` `<lint>` exits 0.`` and `` `<guard>` exits 0.``.
Spec phase criterion: `No desired behavior is represented as current behavior.`
Design phase criterion: data-model.md, quickstart.md and at least one `contracts/*.md` exist and every quickstart command is labelled not executed.
Tasks phase criterion: tasks.md passes `python3 <root>/lib/specstride_spec.py validate --specs <out>/tasks.md --format speckit-tasks`.
Final phase criterion: ANALYSIS.md exists and lists every finding with its resolution, and the linter reports zero errors at `--upto 5`.
The feature namespace of a reverse run is `reverse-<slug>`; its gate state lives in `<SRC>/<state>/features/reverse-<slug>/`.

`plan` refuses when `<state>/features/reverse-<slug>/gates/` exists and is not empty: `a reverse run for '<slug>' already has gate state in <dir>; resume it with specstride resume -w <src> --feature reverse-<slug>, or pass --name` (exit 3).
The inventory that `plan` builds excludes exactly the output directory (`excludes=[out_rel]`).
A constitution has to be written by the run only when the source has no `.specify/memory/constitution.md` (`constitution_needed`).
The lint command of a unit phase adds `--claims <run_state>/claims-<unit-key>.md`.
The lint and guard commands shown in the driver are the same argv, shell-quoted with `shlex.quote` and prefixed with `python3`.

The generated driver is validated with the `native` spec adapter before it is written; a failure raises `generated driver is not a valid native spec: <errors>` (exit 3) and is a generator bug, not an input problem.

Each driver phase N contributes command `lint-N`: `executable` = the running Python interpreter, `cwd` = SRC, `args` = `[reverse.py, lint, <out>, --src, <src>, --baseline, <inventory.json>, --upto, <level>]`, `timeoutSec` 120.
Lint command timeout is 120 seconds.
Each driver phase N contributes command `guard-N`: `args` = `[reverse.py, guard, <src>, --baseline, <inventory.json>, --out, <out>]`, `timeoutSec` 300.
Guard command timeout is 300 seconds.
`phaseTimeouts` gives 3600 seconds to every phase whose lint level is 0 or 1 (unit investigation and specification phases); other phases get no entry.
The template directory named in the driver is `<SRC>/.specify/templates` when that directory exists, else the vendored `lib/speckit_templates`.
Findings are sorted by file, line, rule, message (errors before warnings in text mode), so the output is deterministic.
Templates are loaded from `<SRC>/.specify/templates/` first and from the vendored `lib/speckit_templates/` otherwise; required headings are never listed in the code.
Headings are compared normalised: `*(...)*` annotations removed, emoji and ornaments replaced by spaces, whitespace collapsed, lower-cased.
Only `## ` headings outside fenced code blocks count, in both template and artifact; YAML front matter is stripped first.
A template heading with a sample `User Story <n>` and no bracket (e.g. `Parallel Example: User Story 1`) matches any story number and only warns when missing.
A template heading marked `*(mandatory)*` is required (exact normalised match).
A template heading marked `*(optional)*`, `*(include if ...)*`, `OPTIONAL` or `[REMOVE IF UNUSED]` produces no rule.
A template heading containing a `[placeholder]` is a family: each bracket matches any text; identical family patterns are de-duplicated.
Every other template heading is `expected`: missing it is a warning, not an error.
Template headings `Phase <n|N>:` collapse into one phase-family rule satisfied by any artifact heading `phase <digits>:`.
A family rule cannot be satisfied by a heading that an explicit (required or expected) template heading already accounts for.
Template paths in messages are printed relative to the Specstride root when vendored, else as the full path.
Only template comments longer than 20 characters (stripped) are checked for verbatim copy.
A contract is a file matching `contracts/<name>.md` directly inside `contracts/`; nested files are extras.
When the source already has a constitution, `memory/constitution.md` in the output is `structure.extra` with the suffix `(the source already has .specify/memory/constitution.md)`.
With a baseline, a path exists when it is in the inventory's `files` or `skipped`; without one the live filesystem is used and workspaces are any non-root directory holding a `package.json`.
A cited path is tried SRC-relative first, then relative to each workspace package; exactly one workspace hit resolves it.
Several citations are separated by comma-plus-space (`, `); an empty field reports `no citation`.
A claim block extends over wrapped continuation lines; it ends at a blank line, a line starting with `<!--`, `#`, `- `, `* `, `|`, a code fence or `<n>. `, or at the next claim.
Without `--src` only the presence of evidence comments is checked; their content is not validated.
EVERY evidence comment in a linted file is validated, whether or not it is attached to a claim.
Claims in spec.md are lines starting `- **FR-<digits>**` or `- **SC-<digits>**`.
A checklist item is a line `- [ ] ` / `- [x] ` / `- [X] ` at column 0.
Paths in a task description are backticked tokens, `dir/file.ext` tokens or `dir/` tokens; FR/SC/US/T ids and URLs are not paths.
Checkbox lines inside fenced code and inside the YAML front matter are ignored by the tasks linter.
Phase-order checks consider only numbered `## Phase <n>` sections that hold at least one task.
Without `--src` the constitution is neither required nor forbidden, templates come only from the vendored copy, and the warning `evidence.skipped` is raised.
Citations into the feature directory (when inside SRC) and into the state directory are rejected as generated artifacts.
Levels are cumulative: `--upto N` checks every artifact owned by levels 1..N; artifacts of higher levels are not required and their content is not linted.
research.md, data-model.md, quickstart.md and each `contracts/*.md` get the fixed placeholder check only (no template), when owned at the level.
FR coverage is checked only when `upto >= 5`.
In a claims file every line starting with `- ` is a claim needing an evidence comment; findings name the file by basename.
The guard re-walks the source with the baseline's `excludes` plus the output dir and compares `(bytes, sha256)` of every walked and skipped entry.
File-level comparison happens only when the recomputed fingerprint differs from the baseline fingerprint.

`testautomation/` is never walked, so the guard compares it separately against the baseline's `testautomation` snapshot: a new directory, a new file or a changed file is a problem; deletions there are not reported.
With a baseline that predates the snapshot (no `testautomation` key), any `testautomation/` directory is reported as added unless the baseline already lists files under it.
Git checks run only when the baseline was walked in `git` mode.
Git status entries under the output dir or the state dir are exempt.
Git status entries identical to one already in the baseline's `git_status` are exempt, so a tree that was dirty before the run still passes.
Problems are de-duplicated and printed in first-seen order.
`python3 lib/reverse_inventory.py <SRC> --out <inventory.json>` builds the inventory standalone and prints the absolute path of the written file.
`reverse_inventory.py` positional `src`; a non-directory fails with `source is not a directory: <src>`.
`reverse_inventory.py --out` (required): the inventory.json path.
`reverse_inventory.py --md PATH` (default none): also write INVENTORY.md there.
`reverse_inventory.py --exclude PATH` (repeatable): a SRC-relative path never walked.
`SPECSTRIDE_REVERSE_MAX_FILE_BYTES` (positive integer, default 1048576): a text file larger than this is skipped as `oversize`.
`SPECSTRIDE_REVERSE_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES` (positive integer, default 20971520): when the total text bytes exceed it the inventory is `oversize` and the run is split by unit.
`SPECSTRIDE_CONTEXT_BUDGET` (default 24000) is the INVENTORY.md character budget of the standalone CLI.
`reverse_inventory.py` exit codes: 0 ok, 3 invalid input, 2 usage (argparse).
`reverse_inventory.py` exits 3 (`E_INVALID`) on invalid input, printing `reverse_inventory: <message>` on stderr.
An integer env var that is not an integer or is <= 0 raises `<NAME> must be a positive integer (got '<v>')`; unset or empty means the default.
A failing `git ls-files` raises `git ls-files failed in <src>: <stderr>`.
inventory.json `schema_version` is 1.
inventory.json `files[]` entries hold `path`, `bytes`, `lines`, `sha256`, `language`, `role`.
inventory.json key `src` is the realpath of the source.
inventory.json key `walk` is `git` or `walk`.
inventory.json key `excludes` is the sorted normalised exclude list.
inventory.json key `limits` holds `max_file_bytes` and `max_total_bytes` in effect.
inventory.json key `totals` holds `files`, `skipped`, `text_bytes`, `lines`.
inventory.json key `oversize` is true when total text bytes are strictly greater than the total cap.
inventory.json key `project` holds `manifests`, `languages`, `frameworks`, `entry_points`, `workspaces`.
inventory.json key `git_head` is set only in git mode, else null.
inventory.json key `git_status` is the porcelain list in git mode, else null.
inventory.json key `testautomation` is the snapshot map or null.
INVENTORY.md title is `# Inventory — <src basename>`.
INVENTORY.md intro names the source, the walk mode and the inventory.json path as the full record.
INVENTORY.md bullet `- Files: <n> text (<lines> lines, <bytes> bytes); <n> skipped`.
INVENTORY.md bullet `- Oversize: yes|no (limit <n> bytes of text)`.
INVENTORY.md bullet `- git HEAD: <sha>` or `not a git work tree`.
INVENTORY.md bullet `- Fingerprint: `<sha256>``.
INVENTORY.md bullets `- Languages:` (`none` when empty) and `- Frameworks:` (`none detected`).
INVENTORY.md bullet `- Existing Spec Kit: yes|no; constitution present|absent; specs <NNN list>|none`.
INVENTORY.md section `## Manifests`: one bullet per manifest, facts as JSON cut to 600 characters, or `- none`.
INVENTORY.md section `## Entry points`: `- <kind>: `<target>` (<manifest>)` or `- none detected`.
INVENTORY.md section `## Workspaces and units`.
INVENTORY.md section `## Skipped`: `- `<path>`: <reason>` or `- none`.
INVENTORY.md section `## Files` is a table `| Path | Lines | Language | Role |`.
When rows are dropped INVENTORY.md ends with `_<k> of <n> file rows dropped to stay within <budget> characters; every file is in `<json>`._`.
Files are written atomically: parent dirs created, content written to `<path>.tmp`, then `os.replace`.
`reverse_inventory.py` prints the absolute inventory path on stdout on success.
Skipped entries still carry `bytes` and `sha256`, so a change to a binary or oversize file is caught by the guard.
Determinism rule as documented: keys and paths sorted, no timestamp in the body.
Without `tomllib` (Python < 3.11) TOML manifests yield no parsed facts.
Default per-file cap is 1 MiB.
Default total cap is 20 MiB.
Default INVENTORY.md budget is 24000 characters.
`SNIFF_BYTES` is 8192.
State dir names never walked: `.specstride`, the legacy state dir name and `.lisa`.
Non-git walk skips directories named `.git`, `node_modules`, `.venv`, `venv`, `__pycache__`, `dist`, `build`, `target`, `vendor`, `testautomation` and the state dirs, at any depth.
Role `test` is decided by path patterns (`tests/`, `__tests__/`, `test_*.py`, `*_test.go`, `*.spec.ts`, `conftest.py`, ...).
Role `doc` applies to README/CHANGELOG/CONTRIBUTING/LICENSE/AGENTS/CLAUDE style names, markdown/rst/text files and anything under `docs/`.
Integer env vars are read under the `SPECSTRIDE_` name first, then under the legacy prefix.
File hashes are sha256 of the content, read in 64 KiB chunks.
Git mode is used only when SRC is inside a work tree AND is its top level; a subdirectory of a repository is walked with the filesystem walk.
`git_head` is `git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD`, or null when there is no commit or git fails (30 s timeout).
`git_status` is the sorted list of `XY path` entries from `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all` (60 s timeout); the source path of a rename/copy is dropped.
Non-git walk honours only the ROOT `.gitignore`, as a glob subset: `**/` removed, `/**` read as `/*`, no nested ignore files.
Ignore rules: `!` negates, trailing `/` is directory-only, a pattern with `/` is anchored to the SRC-relative path, others match the basename or the path; the last matching rule wins.
Git mode lists `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard -z` (tracked plus untracked-not-ignored), 300 s timeout.
