In git mode a path is dropped when any of its directory components is a state dir name or when it is under an exclude; `DENY_DIRS` is NOT applied in git mode.
Non-git walk never follows symlinks; a symlinked directory is recorded as one link entry and not descended.
Candidate paths are sorted; the walk mode is reported as `git` or `walk`.
Language is decided by exact file name, then `Dockerfile*`/`*.dockerfile`, then lower-cased extension, then shebang, else `unknown`.
Role precedence: `ci`, `test`, `schema`, `template`, `doc`, `script`, `source`, `config`, else `other`.
Role `script` applies to shell files, anything under `scripts/` or `bin/`, and any file starting with a shebang (so an executable Python entry script is `script`, not `source`).
Excludes are normalised by stripping leading/trailing `/`, de-duplicated and sorted; an exclude matches itself and everything under it.
A symlink resolving outside SRC is skipped with reason `symlink-escape` (still fingerprinted by its target).
A symlink resolving inside SRC is a file entry with `symlink: true`, `target`, `bytes` = length of the target string, `sha256` of the target string, `lines` 0, language `symlink`, role `other`.
A path listed by git but absent from the work tree is silently dropped from the inventory.
A file with a NUL byte in its first 8192 bytes is skipped with reason `binary` (checked before the size cap).
A file strictly larger than the per-file cap is skipped with reason `oversize` and records `limit`.
Line count is the number of newline bytes plus 1 when the file is non-empty and does not end with a newline.
`totals.text_bytes` sums only text files; symlinks and skipped entries do not count towards the oversize limit.
The `testautomation` snapshot maps each regular, non-symlink file under `<SRC>/testautomation/` to `[bytes, sha256]`, or is null when the directory does not exist.
`fingerprint` is the sha256 of the compact JSON list of sorted `(path, bytes, sha256)` triples over files plus skipped entries.

`package.json` facts: name, bin, exports (plus main/module/types), scripts, workspaces; dependency names from dependencies, devDependencies, peerDependencies; an unparseable file records `error: unparseable`.
`pyproject.toml` facts: name, scripts (PEP 621 and poetry), build backend; any mention of `pytest` in the text counts as the pytest framework.
`setup.cfg` facts: metadata name, console_scripts, install_requires.
`go.mod` facts: module name, go version, required module paths.
`Cargo.toml` facts: package name, `[[bin]]` names, workspace members, dependencies.
`Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.*`, `Containerfile` facts: FROM, ENTRYPOINT, CMD, EXPOSE values.
`Makefile`/`GNUmakefile` facts: sorted unique target names.
`pom.xml`, `build.gradle`, `build.gradle.kts` facts: first `<artifactId>` as name.
Compose files (`compose*.y(a)ml`, `docker-compose*.y(a)ml`) facts: sorted service names.
`.github/workflows/*.yml|yaml` facts: workflow name and job ids.
Root `pnpm-workspace.yaml` facts: the `packages:` globs.
Manifest records drop keys whose value is None, empty string, empty list or empty dict.
Frameworks are derived only from manifest dependency names through a fixed hint table and are reported sorted.
Entry point kind `bin` (package.json `bin`, Cargo `[[bin]]`).
Entry point kind `console-script` for manifest scripts, except `package.json` scripts, which are not entry points.
Entry point kind `export` with the manifest-relative `resolved` path.
Entry point kind `container-entrypoint` from Dockerfile ENTRYPOINT.
Entry-point detection reads at most the first 256 KiB of a file.
Entry point kind `python-main` for a Python source/script file with an `if __name__ == "__main__":` line.
Entry point kind `go-main` for a Go file with `package main` and `func main()`.
Entry point kind `script` for a role-script file starting with a shebang.
`languages` counts files per language, sorted by name, excluding `unknown` and `symlink`.
Entry points are sorted by their sorted-key JSON text.
Workspaces are directories holding a `package.json` or `Cargo.toml` that match a root workspace glob (`**` read as `*`, `!` globs exclude).
Units are the workspace packages plus `.` for the rest when workspaces exist, else the top-level directories plus `.` for root files; each has `path`, `files`, `bytes`; sorted by path.
`specify` facts are read from the filesystem directly (not from the walk): `present`, `constitution`, `templates`, `feature_json`, `spec_numbers`.
Existing spec numbers are the leading 3-or-more-digit prefixes of DIRECTORIES under `<SRC>/specs/` named `<digits>-...`; files are ignored.
inventory.json is serialised with sorted keys, indent 1, non-ASCII kept as is, plus a trailing newline; it carries no timestamp, so two runs over the same tree are byte-identical.
File rows are added in order until the text plus the row plus 200 characters would exceed the budget; project facts are never dropped.
The five vendored templates are read at run time by the linter when the source has no `.specify/templates/`; they are an unchanged copy of Spec Kit's templates at a recorded commit.
checklist-template.md `## [Category 1]` and `## [Category 2]` reduce to one family met by any heading other than the explicit `## Notes`.
constitution-template.md upper-case tokens such as `[PROJECT_NAME]` are placeholders the linter rejects in a written constitution.
constitution-template.md `## Core Principles` and `## Governance` are expected headings (warnings); `## [SECTION_2_NAME]` is a family.
plan-template.md headings (Summary, Technical Context, Constitution Check, Project Structure, Complexity Tracking) carry no mandatory mark, so each missing one is only a warning.
spec-template.md makes `## User Scenarios & Testing` mandatory.
spec-template.md makes `## Requirements` mandatory.
spec-template.md makes `## Success Criteria` mandatory.
spec-template.md `## Assumptions` carries no mark, so a spec without it only gets a `template.expected` warning.
tasks-template.md `## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`` contains brackets, so it is a family rule (error when no heading of that shape exists).
tasks-template.md phase headings form the phase family: a tasks.md with no `## Phase <n>:` section is a `template.family` error.
`specstride_spec.py feature-slug --specs F` prints the feature slug; it is answered before the spec is read, so it works for a missing or odd spec file.
`specstride_spec.py detect --specs F` prints the resolved format name.
`specstride_spec.py context --specs F` prints one `name<TAB>path` line per context document; nothing for the native format.
`specstride_spec.py render-context --specs F` writes the budgeted context block to stdout with no added newline.
`specstride_spec.py validate --specs F` prints the phase count on success; on failure prints each error on its own stderr line and exits 3.
`specstride_spec.py tick <n> --specs F` ticks phase n's unticked task boxes in the file and prints how many lines changed.
`specstride_spec.py numbers --specs F` prints each phase number on its own line.
`specstride_spec.py title <n> --specs F` prints the title of phase n (an empty line when there is no such phase).
`specstride_spec.py shape <n> --specs F` prints the 16-hex shape digest of phase n (empty line when absent).
`specstride_spec.py slice <n> --specs F` writes the raw, unstripped section of phase n followed by one newline.
`specstride_spec.py first-unapproved --specs F` prints the first phase number lacking `GATE<n>-APPROVED` in the gates dir; prints nothing when all are approved; exit 0 either way.
The subcommand is restricted by argparse `choices` to the 11 names; anything else is a usage error (exit 2).
Optional positional `n`: the phase number for title/slice/tick/shape; a non-integer value raises an uncaught ValueError (traceback, exit 1).
`--specs` is required for every subcommand.
`--workdir` (default `.`) locates the default gates dir for `first-unapproved`.
`--gates-dir` (default none): explicit gates dir for `first-unapproved`; else `<workdir>/<state dir>/gates`.
`--format native|speckit-tasks|openspec-change` overrides auto-detection.
Importing the module maps every legacy-prefixed variable onto its `SPECSTRIDE_` name in the process environment (new name wins) and prints one deprecation line on stderr when one was used.
`SPECSTRIDE_SPEC_FORMAT` is the format override used when `--format` is not given (trimmed, lower-cased).
`SPECSTRIDE_CONTEXT_BUDGET` (default 24000) is the total character budget of the rendered context; a non-integer value silently falls back to the default.
`specstride_spec.py` documents exit 0 ok and 3 invalid spec / bad usage; argparse usage errors still exit 2.
An unknown explicit format prints `specstride_spec: unknown spec format: <v> (native|speckit-tasks|openspec-change)` and exits 3.
An unreadable spec file prints `specstride_spec: <os error>` on stderr and exits 3.
`validate` exits 3 on an invalid spec.
Native error `spec has zero phases (need at least one "## Phase <N>")`.
Native error `phase <n> (<raw heading text>) has no "### Acceptance criteria" block`; the block may be empty of checkboxes and still validate.
Error `duplicate phase number: <n>` (all formats); a duplicate also yields the non-contiguous message.
Error `non-contiguous phases: <b> follows <a> (must ascend by 1)` (all formats); the first number is free (0, 1 or any).
Spec Kit error `tasks.md has zero phases (need task-bearing "## Phase <N>:" or "## P<N>" sections)`.
Spec Kit error `phase <n> (<title>) has no task checkboxes ("- [ ] T### ..." lines)`.
OpenSpec error `OpenSpec tasks.md has zero phases (need task-bearing "## <N>. <title>" sections)`.
OpenSpec error `phase <n> (<title>) has no OpenSpec task checkboxes ("- [ ] N.N ..." lines)`.
A tick rewrites the spec atomically through `<spec>.tick.<pid>.tmp`, copies the file mode, then `os.replace`; nothing is written when no line changed.
A truncated context document ends with the marker `… (context truncated at line boundary) …`.
Each context block starts `## Context: <name> (read-only background, NOT a gate) — <path>`; blocks are joined by a blank line.
Missing phase number: `specstride_spec: tick needs a phase number` (exit 3).
Missing phase number: `specstride_spec: title needs a phase number` (exit 3).
Missing phase number: `specstride_spec: shape needs a phase number` (exit 3).
Missing phase number: `specstride_spec: slice needs a phase number` (exit 3).
Native phase heading: `## Phase <digits>` matched case-sensitively at column 0, spaces or tabs as separators.
Native title: the heading text after the number with the leading run of spaces and `-`, em dash or `:` separators removed.
A phase section runs from its heading to the next level-2 heading (or end of file); trailing blank lines are kept in the raw slice.
Native criteria block heading: `### Acceptance criteria` (case-sensitive prefix match); the block ends at the next line starting with `###`.
Checkbox syntax for all formats: optional indent, `-`, optional spaces, `[ ]`, `[x]`, `[X]` or `[]`, then the text.
Native criteria are only the checkbox lines inside the acceptance-criteria block.
Native error order: per-phase missing-criteria messages first in scan order, then duplicate/contiguity messages.
Spec Kit phase heading: `## Phase <digits>` with optional `:` and free title text.
Spec Kit priority form: `## P<N>` / `## p<N>` headings with optional `-`, em dash or `:` separator.
Spec Kit criteria: every checkbox line with non-empty text anywhere in the phase section (not only `T###` lines, and under any `###` subheading).
Priority form: only sections that hold task checkboxes become phases; they are numbered contiguously in document order starting at the first priority number; repeated priorities are valid.
Priority form: level-2 sections after the last task-bearing group are appended to EVERY phase's section as shared constraints.
Priority form title keeps the priority label (the whole heading text after `##`).
Explicit `## Phase N` headings win; the priority form is used only when no explicit phase exists.
OpenSpec phase heading: `## <digits>` with optional `.` or `)`, then a title.
OpenSpec task line: a checkbox followed by a dotted id `N.N[.N...]`; the criterion is `<id> <text>`; checkboxes without such an id are not criteria.

Criteria heading shown to agents per format: native `Acceptance criteria (the phase spec)`, Spec Kit `Tasks to complete (each `- [ ]` is a required deliverable)`, OpenSpec `OpenSpec tasks to complete (each `- [ ]` is required)`.
Detection step 1: a valid explicit override (flag, then env) wins.
Detection step 2: a path shaped `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` is `openspec-change`.
Detection step 3: any other file whose basename is `tasks.md` (case-insensitive) is `speckit-tasks`.
Detection step 4: content with a phase heading (`## Phase N` or `## P<N>`), a `- [ ] T<digit>` task line and NO `### Acceptance criteria` heading is `speckit-tasks`.
Detection step 5: content with a `## <N>. title` heading and a `- [ ] N.N` task line is `openspec-change`.
Detection step 6: everything else is `native`.
`slice_phase()` (the importable form used by the critic) returns the section stripped; the CLI `slice` returns it unstripped.
Phase shape digest: first 16 hex of sha256 over compact JSON `[n, title, [criteria]]` with whitespace runs collapsed; ticking a checkbox never changes it.
`phase_title(section)` with a single argument parses the first heading as native, then Spec Kit, then priority, then OpenSpec form.
The `.specify` project root is found by walking upward from the spec's directory.
Slug sanitising: runs outside `A-Za-z0-9._-` collapse to `-`, leading/trailing `-` trimmed; an empty result falls back to `default`.

Feature slug: an OpenSpec change uses its change directory basename; a spec inside a `.specify` project uses its feature directory basename; anything else, or a spec at the project root, is `default`.
OpenSpec context order: `proposal`, `delta-spec:<name>` (recursive, sorted), `design`, then `current-spec:<name>` for each delta with a matching `openspec/specs/` file.
The constitution is context only when the spec is inside a `.specify` project.
Spec Kit context order: constitution, spec, plan, `contract:<stem>` (sorted), data-model, research, quickstart, `checklist:<stem>` (sorted); each only when the file exists.
Context budget default is 24000 characters across all context documents.
Per-document floor is 1200 characters: a document that would get less is dropped, unless the whole document fits.
Truncation cuts at a line boundary (hard cut only for one over-long line) and closes an unbalanced code fence.
Budget allocation walks documents in priority order, giving each the smaller of its size, a fair share (at least the floor) and what remains; leftover cascades forward.
An unticked line is a checkbox `[ ]` or `[]` followed by non-empty text; it becomes `[x]`. Already ticked lines and empty boxes are untouched.
Ticking handles only `speckit-tasks` with explicit `## Phase N` headings and `openspec-change`; native specs and the `## P<N>` priority form are left untouched (0 ticked).
Only lines inside phase N's section are ticked; any other level-2 heading ends the section. Every unticked checkbox there is ticked, not only task-id lines.
Line endings and every other byte are preserved (the file is read and written with `newline=""`).
A missing phase yields an empty slice, title or shape rather than an error.
The native format renders no context.

`lib/agent_stream.py` (the stream tap) reads a coding agent's JSONL stream on stdin, appends normalized events to the events file, prints a human summary on stdout and optionally ships to Loki/OTLP; it has no subcommands.
`--events PATH` (default `$SPECSTRIDE_EVENTS`, else empty): the JSONL file normalized events are appended to; empty means no local write at all.
`--run-id ID` (default `$SPECSTRIDE_RUN_ID`, else empty): run identity stamped on every event.
`--task NAME` (default `$SPECSTRIDE_TASK`): stamped as `task` on legacy (non-correlated) events and used as the Loki `task` label / OTLP `task` resource attribute.
`--feature SLUG` (default `$SPECSTRIDE_FEATURE`): one of the seven values that must all be present to enable the correlated invocation envelope.
`--role` accepts only `proposer`, `accelerator` or `critic` (default none); any other value is an argparse error (exit 2).
`--backend LABEL` (default `$SPECSTRIDE_BACKEND_LABEL`): stamped as `backend` and used as the Loki `backend` label / OTLP `backend` resource attribute.
`--phase N` (int, no default): part of the invocation identity.
`--attempt N` (int, no default): part of the invocation identity.
`--iteration N` with alias `--iter` (int, no default): part of the invocation identity; on the legacy path it is added to every event as field `iter`.
`--invocation-id ID` (default empty): when empty a correlated invocation gets a generated id.
`--expected-evidence PATH` (default empty): the gate evidence path a tool write is matched against to emit `evidence_writing`.
`--provider-format NAME` (default `claude`): selects the stream adapter by canonical name or alias through the seam table.
`--invocation-model MODEL` (default empty): used only by the shared-behaviour wrapper for a synthesised init / missing terminal; bare adapters ignore it.
`--terminal-sidecar PATH` (default empty): when set the tap writes the provider-terminal observation to this file at exit; the tap never writes `result.json`.
`--loki URL` (default empty = no Loki shipping): base URL of the Loki sink the tap fans events out to.
`--otel URL` (default empty = no OTLP shipping): base URL of the OTLP/HTTP sink the tap fans events out to.
`--list-formats`: print the canonical stream format names one per line and return before reading stdin, emitting no events and building no shipper.
`SPECSTRIDE_EVENTS` is read by the tap as the default of `--events` (default empty).
`SPECSTRIDE_RUN_ID` is read by the tap as the default of `--run-id`.
`SPECSTRIDE_TASK` is read by the tap as the default of `--task`.
`SPECSTRIDE_FEATURE` is read by the tap as the default of `--feature`.
`SPECSTRIDE_BACKEND_LABEL` is read by the tap as the default of `--backend`.
`agent_init` (Claude adapter, from a `system`/`init` record): fields `model`, `tools` (count of the tools list).
`agent_text` (Claude adapter, one per non-empty assistant text block): fields `text`, `redacted`, `truncated`, `original_bytes`, `retained_bytes`.
`agent_tool` (Claude adapter, one per `tool_use` block): fields `tool`, `target`, `targets`, `redacted`, `truncated`, `original_bytes`, `retained_bytes` and `tool_id` when the block has an id.
`evidence_writing` (Claude adapter, at most once per tap process): fields `tool`, `target` (the expected evidence path), `match` = `exact-expected-target`, and `tool_id` when present.
`agent_observability` at invocation start (correlated path only, adapter constructed or format unknown): fields `mode`, `reason`, `provider_format`, `role`, `supported_signals`.

`agent_observability` with `mode=degraded`, `supported_signals=result` and reason `stream adapter for '<format>' failed to start — parsing plain output` is emitted when the adapter constructor raises (on both legacy and correlated paths; `role` only with a context).
`agent_diagnostic` with `code=adapter_error`, `severity=error`, `message` (exception text cut to 200 characters) is emitted for an exception inside an adapter.

`agent_observability` transition (correlated path): emitted once when an `agent_diagnostic` with code `unsupported_schema` or `absent_schema` arrives and the mode differs from the current one; fields `mode=degraded`, `reason` (the diagnostic message), `provider_format`, `role`, `supported_signals=result`.

`agent_result` (legacy path only, on a provider terminal): fields `model`, `is_error`, `subtype`, `cost_usd`, `duration_ms`, `num_turns`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_creation_tokens`.
`agent_result` (legacy path, terminal produced by `finish()` at end of stream) additionally carries `reason_code` and `reason`, and `subtype` falls back to the reason code.
`agent_stream.py` exits 2 (argparse) on an unknown flag, a non-integer `--phase`/`--attempt`/`--iteration` or a `--role` outside the three choices.
`agent_stream.py` exits 0 even when `main()` raises: any exception is swallowed after one stderr line, so a tap failure never produces a non-zero parser status by itself.
`provider_error`: terminal `reason_code` of a Claude `result` record with `is_error` true; `reason` is the record's `result` text or `Provider reported an error`.

`missing_terminal`: terminal `reason_code` the Claude adapter synthesises at end of stream when no `result` record was seen (`status` `error`, reason `Provider stream ended without a terminal result`).
Observability mode `structured` with signals `init,text,tool,evidence,result` is announced when the format is registered.
Observability mode `raw-text` with reason `structured schema unavailable — parsing plain output` and signals `text,result` is announced when the format is not registered.
The events file is opened in append mode per event and one compact JSON line (`ensure_ascii=False`, separators `,` and `:`) is written per event; this is a plain append, not an atomic rename.

Terminal sidecar (path from `--terminal-sidecar`, in practice `<invocation_dir>/provider-terminal.json`): written atomically at tap exit with `contract` = `specstride-provider-terminal/v1`, `provider_terminal` (last terminal dict or null) and `malformed_stream` (bool).
Claude init prints `  · init model=<model|?> tools=<count>` to stdout.
A Claude `result` record prints `  ✓ result: <subtype>  cost=$<4dp>  turns=<n>  out_tok=<n>  <duration>ms` to stdout, also when the result is an error.
Each assistant text block is printed to stdout as the redacted text itself with no prefix.
Each tool call prints `  → <tool> <target>` (or `  → <tool>` when there is no target) to stdout.
A stream that ends without a result prints `  ✗ result: missing_terminal (stream ended before result)` to stdout.
When the Loki shipper cannot be constructed the tap writes `agent_stream: Loki disabled (<error>)` to stderr and continues without that sink.
When the OTLP shipper cannot be constructed the tap writes `agent_stream: OTEL disabled (<error>)` to stderr and continues without that sink.
`--list-formats` prints one canonical format name per line in table order: `claude` then `prime-v3` (aliases are not printed).
When the terminal sidecar cannot be written the tap writes `agent_stream: terminal sidecar write failed (<error>)` to stderr.
On an unexpected exception the tap writes `agent_stream: fatal (ignored): <error>` to stderr.
At import the tap calls `specstride_env.apply()` so legacy environment variable names are mapped onto `SPECSTRIDE_*` before any default is read.
Legacy (no context) event record shape: `ts` (`%f` epoch seconds), `time` (local `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z`), `event`, then `run_id`/`task`/`backend` when non-empty, then the event fields.
An `OSError` while appending an event to the events file is swallowed silently; the event is still shipped to remote sinks.
What the fan-out ships to remote sinks is the locally written record minus `ts`, `time` and `event`, so remote records carry the same identity and `sequence` as the local line.
Event fields whose value is `None` are dropped before writing.

Fields named `text`, `message`, `summary`, `result_summary` or `target` go through text redaction/truncation and add `redacted`, `truncated`, `original_bytes`, `retained_bytes` to the event unless those keys are already present; every other field goes through recursive structural sanitization.

`TEXT_MAX` = 160: the Claude adapter's `agent_text` event text is whitespace-collapsed and cut to 160 bytes, while the line printed to stdout keeps its whitespace and is cut at the policy text limit (4096 bytes).

Claude terminal extraction: `status` from `is_error`, `stop_reason` from `subtype`, `model` from the last seen model, `duration_ms`, `num_turns`, `input_tokens`/`output_tokens` from `usage`, `cache_read_tokens` from `usage.cache_read_input_tokens`, `cache_creation_tokens` from `usage.cache_creation_input_tokens`, `cost_usd` from `total_cost_usd`.

Two stream formats are registered in the seam table: `claude` (alias `claude-stream-json`, adapter `ClaudeAdapter`) and `prime-v3` (adapter `PrimeAdapter`); neither opts into any shared behaviour, so both run as bare adapters.
The `claude` format row announces capability reason `Claude stream-json schema selected` with the default five signals.
The `prime-v3` format row announces capability reason `Prime JSON schema v3 selected` with the default five signals.
`select_provider_adapter` raises `ValueError('unsupported provider format: <name>')` for a name that is neither a canonical name nor an alias.

An adapter is wrapped in the shared-behaviour wrapper only when its format row opts into `synth_init`, `synth_terminal`, `no_activity` or `track_terminal`; otherwise the bare adapter is used and `--invocation-model` has no effect.
Only diagnostic codes `unsupported_schema` and `absent_schema` degrade the capability mode; other diagnostics (for example `malformed_json`) do not.

The correlated (invocation-context) path is enabled only when `--run-id`, `--feature`, `--role`, `--backend`, `--phase`, `--attempt` and `--iteration` are all non-empty; otherwise the tap runs the legacy path with uncorrelated records.
Tap-built Loki sink uses base labels `job=ralph` plus `task` and `backend` when given.
Tap-built OTLP sink uses resource attributes `service.name=ralph` plus `task` and `backend` when given.
The tap builds `ObservabilityPolicy()` with built-in defaults only; no environment variable or flag changes redaction patterns or byte limits.
Invalid identity values on the correlated path (for example phase < 0, attempt < 1, proposer iteration < 1) raise before stdin is read, so the tap ends with `fatal (ignored)` and consumes no input.
Remote sinks receive a second structural sanitization pass of the already sanitized fields; the local JSONL line is not rewritten by it.
The fan-out object exists only when at least one remote sink was constructed; with none, events are written locally only and no `telemetry_delivery` records are produced.
`SIGTERM` does not kill the tap: it sets a stop flag and the read loop ends at the next input line, after which `finish()` and the final flush/sidecar still run.
On the legacy path with `--iteration` given, every event gets field `iter`; on the correlated path the iteration is carried as identity field `iteration` instead.
The legacy path never emits `agent_observability` at start, so a legacy Claude stream yields exactly `agent_init` ... `agent_result`.

Adapter fault policy: only the first 3 adapter exceptions per tap process produce a diagnostic, later ones are only counted; every fault sets the malformed-stream flag and the offending line is skipped.
Pass-through is not byte-identical: each line is stripped of leading/trailing whitespace and blank lines are dropped before anything is printed or parsed.
An unknown format or a failed adapter start turns the tap into a pass-through: every non-blank stdin line is printed to stdout with surrounding whitespace stripped and no events are derived from it.
A non-JSON line is printed raw when the adapter has no `consume_raw` (the Claude adapter); an adapter with `consume_raw` (Prime) receives the raw text instead.
A `malformed_json` diagnostic from the adapter sets the malformed-stream flag recorded in the terminal sidecar.
On the correlated path the tap emits no `agent_result`; the terminal is only recorded for the sidecar and the controller's finalizer emits the event.
A provider terminal is the completion barrier: all remote sinks are flushed and `telemetry_delivery` records written as soon as a terminal is seen, and again at process end.
stdout is flushed after every processed input record so the summary is live.
`finish()` is called at most once per tap process and an exception in it is handled like a consume fault.
`BrokenPipeError` on stdout ends the loop silently; the final flush and sidecar write still run.
`KeyboardInterrupt` in the tap is swallowed silently (no message, exit 0).

`finalize_invocation.py <invocation_dir> <events_path> <breaker_state_path> <limit> [kill_reason] [cap_limit]` reconciles one invocation into `result.json`, emits one `agent_result` and folds it into the error breaker.
Positional 1-4 (`invocation_dir`, `events_path`, `breaker_state_path`, `limit`) are required; fewer than four raise an unhandled exception (Python traceback, exit 1).
Optional positional 5 `kill_reason` (default empty): a watchdog kill reason carried in by the controller.
Optional positional 6 `cap_limit` (default 0): threshold of the hard-cap breaker.

`agent_result` (finalizer): appended to the run events file as one compact JSON line with envelope `ts`, `time`, `event`, identity, `sequence` and fields `status`, `is_error`, `reason_code`, `reason`, `source`, `provider_status`, `provider_stop_reason`, `producer_exit_code`, `producer_signal`, `parser_exit_code`, `timed_out`, `duration_ms`, `finalized_at` plus copied provider/kill fields.
`finalize_invocation.py` exits 0 whenever reconciliation completes, whatever the decision.
Decision `cap_halt`: the hard-cap breaker reached its limit (checked first).
Decision `halt`: the consecutive-error breaker reached its limit.
Decision `continue`: neither breaker tripped.

Reads `<invocation_dir>/metadata.json` as the required identity source (`run_id`, `feature`, `role`, `backend`, `phase`, `attempt`, `iteration`, `invocation_id`; optional `observability_mode`, `provider_format`, `expected_evidence`); a missing file is an unhandled error.
Reads optional `<invocation_dir>/producer.json` with `producer_exit_code`, `producer_signal`, `parser_exit_code`, `timed_out`, `launch_failed`, `duration_ms`.
Reads optional `<invocation_dir>/provider-terminal.json` for `provider_terminal` and `malformed_stream`.
`<invocation_dir>/result.json` is written atomically with no-overwrite semantics, exactly once per invocation.
Breaker state file (path from argument 3) is loaded if present and rewritten atomically with `count`, `cap_count`, `last_invocation_id`, `last_reason_code`, `last_kill_class`.
stdout is exactly six lines: decision, `reason_code`, `true`/`false` for is_error, consecutive error count, kill class (may be empty), cap count.
The finalizer's `agent_result` goes only to the local events file; it is not shipped to Loki or OTLP by this process, and an empty events path skips the event entirely.
A classifiable kill reason adds `kill_reason` and `kill_class` to the result and to the mirrored event; an unclassified or empty reason adds nothing.
When `result.json` already exists it is consumed as-is: no re-reconciliation, no second `agent_result`, but the breaker still records it.
The finalizer never passes `cancelled` or `unsupported_schema` to reconciliation, so statuses `cancelled` and `degraded` cannot appear in a result it writes.
Duration, exit status and signal come only from `producer.json` (the controller's observation); cost, tokens, model and turns come only from the provider terminal in the sidecar.
`agent_result` mirrored by `ResultFinalizer`: envelope fields plus every result field except `contract` and the identity keys.
`provider_auth` has fixed reason text `Provider authentication failed` when the provider gave no reason.
`timeout` (status `timeout`): highest precedence, when the producer timed out; reason text `Invocation timed out`.
`cancelled` (status `cancelled`): second precedence; reason text `Invocation was cancelled`.
`launch_failed` (status `error`): reason text `Provider process could not be launched`.
`producer_signaled` (status `error`): producer ended by a signal; reason text `Provider process terminated by signal`.
`producer_nonzero` (status `error`): producer exit code non-zero and the provider did not claim success; reason text `Provider process exited nonzero`.
`status_conflict` (status `error`): provider terminal said success but the producer exit code was non-zero; reason text `Provider and process terminal observations conflict`.
`parser_failed` (status `error`): parser (tap) exit code non-zero; reason text `Provider stream parser failed`.
`unsupported_schema` with status `degraded` (the only non-error, non-success status besides timeout/cancelled) when the caller passes `unsupported_schema=True`.
`malformed_stream` (status `error`): the tap flagged a malformed or truncated stream; reason text `Provider stream was malformed or truncated`.
Provider-reported error: `reason_code` is the provider terminal's code (for example `provider_auth`), defaulting to `provider_error`; `reason` is the provider's own text.

`missing_terminal` (status `error`): provider terminal absent or not success, or success without both producer and parser exit codes being 0; reason text `Provider stream ended without a terminal observation`.
`success` (status `success`): only when the provider terminal is success and producer and parser exit codes are both exactly 0.

Atomic JSON write discipline: temp file `.<name>.<random>.tmp` in the target directory, JSON with sorted keys, 2-space indent and trailing newline, `fsync`, then `os.replace`; parent directories are created.
With `replace=False` the temp file is hard-linked to the target so an existing file is never overwritten (the write fails instead).

`result.json` schema: `contract`, the eight identity fields, `status`, `is_error` (status != success), `reason_code`, `reason`, `source`, `provider_status`, `provider_stop_reason`, `producer_exit_code`, `producer_signal`, `parser_exit_code`, `timed_out`, `duration_ms` (clamped >= 0, int), `finalized_at` (UTC ISO with microseconds and `Z`).
Invocation artifact directory: `<feature_root>/debug/invocations/<run_id>/<role>/phase-<n>/attempt-<n>/iter-<n>/<invocation_id>` with every identity component sanitized.
Per-invocation files: `metadata.json`, `result.json`, and the raw, prunable `prompt.txt`, `provider.jsonl`, `events.jsonl`, `response.txt`.
Invocation context contract string is `specstride-invocation/v1` (field `contract` of `metadata.json`).
Invocation result contract string is `specstride-invocation-result/v1` (field `contract` of `result.json`).
Valid observability modes are `structured`, `raw-text` and `degraded`.

Identity path components have every run of characters outside `A-Za-z0-9_.-` replaced by `-`, leading/trailing `.` and `-` stripped, and are cut to 128 characters; an empty result raises `identity component is not path-safe`.
Valid invocation roles are `proposer`, `accelerator` and `critic`; any other role raises `role must be proposer, accelerator or critic`.
Identity validation: `phase` >= 0, `attempt` >= 1, `iteration` >= 1 for proposer/accelerator and >= 0 for critic; booleans and non-integers are rejected.
A missing invocation id is generated as `inv-<iteration, 6 digits>-<8 hex chars>`.
The expected evidence path is stored as an absolute, user-expanded, symlink-resolved path.
Identity fields stamped on every correlated event and on the result: `run_id`, `feature`, `role`, `backend`, `phase`, `attempt`, `iteration`, `invocation_id`.
`sequence` starts at 1 and increases by 1 per event per envelope instance; the tap and the finalizer use separate envelopes, so the finalizer's `agent_result` carries `sequence` 1 again.

Correlated event envelope: `ts` (epoch seconds with 9 decimals), `time` (UTC ISO-8601 with offset), `event`, the eight identity fields, `sequence`, then non-null event fields (which may override earlier keys).
`load_event` rejects an event line that is not a JSON object or lacks `event`, `run_id` or `invocation_id`.
Result field `source` is `synthesized` when the reason code is `missing_terminal` and `reconciled` otherwise.

Every other non-null key of the provider terminal and of extra metrics (for example `model`, `cost_usd`, `input_tokens`, `num_turns`, `no_activity`, `kill_reason`, `kill_class`) is copied onto the result; `status`, `reason`, `reason_code` and `stop_reason` are not copied.

Creating an invocation artifact set is exclusive: an existing directory raises `invocation directory already exists: <dir>`; `metadata.json` (context fields plus `created_at`) is then written atomically.
A result is finalized at most once: a second finalize or an existing `result.json` raises `invocation result has already been finalized`.
Invocation age in whole days uses `result.json` `finalized_at`, else `metadata.json` `created_at`; a missing or unparsable stamp means age 0 (treated as fresh).
An invocation without `result.json` is active and is skipped by retention with `{"skipped": "active"}`.
Retention removes raw files first and `metadata.json` second, never `result.json`; the sweep visits every directory under `debug/invocations` that holds a `metadata.json`.
The redaction placeholder is the literal `[REDACTED]`.
Dict keys `thinking`, `reasoning`, `chain_of_thought`, `chainofthought` (case-insensitive) are dropped entirely from sanitized values and count as a redaction.

Values of dict keys exactly equal (case-insensitive) to `api_key`, `apikey`, `authorization`, `cookie`, `credential`, `password`, `secret`, `token`, `access_token`, `refresh_token` or `client_secret` are replaced by `[REDACTED]`.
Secret value pattern 1: `bearer ` followed by 8 or more token characters (case-insensitive) is redacted in any text.
Secret value pattern 2: `sk-` followed by 8 or more of `A-Za-z0-9_-` is redacted.
Secret value pattern 3: `ghp_`, `gho_`, `ghu_`, `ghs_` or `ghr_` followed by 8 or more alphanumerics is redacted.
Secret value pattern 4: `api_key`/`api-key`/`apikey`, `token`, `secret` or `password` followed by `=` or `:` and a value is redacted as a whole, including the key name.
Keys whose string values are treated as paths: `file`, `file_path`, `filename`, `notebook_path`, `path`, `paths`, `target`, `targets`, `destination`, `source` (also camelCase spellings).
Keys whose string values are tokenised as shell commands to find paths: `command`, `cmd`, `script`.
Sanitization metadata fields are `redacted`, `truncated`, `original_bytes`, `retained_bytes`.
Default byte limits: text 4096, tool arguments 2048, tool result 4096, diagnostic 1024, target 512, and at most 8 target paths.
Any limit that is not a positive integer raises `observability limits must be positive integers`.
Truncation is by UTF-8 bytes and drops a partial trailing character; no ellipsis or marker is appended.
Redaction runs before truncation, and `original_bytes` is measured before redaction.

Path extraction is purely lexical: commands are split with `shlex` (whitespace split on a quoting error); tokens starting with `-`, `http://` or `https://`, shell operators and non-path-shaped tokens are discarded; duplicates are removed.
Tool argument summary: `targets`, `summary` (redacted JSON cut to 2048 bytes), `redacted`, `truncated`, `original_bytes`, `retained_bytes`.
Retention policy version string is `specstride-retention/v1`.
Retention defaults: raw capture disabled, raw retention 7 days, metadata retention 30 days, tool result limit 4096 bytes.
Metadata retention shorter than raw retention raises `metadata retention must not be shorter than raw retention`; negative or non-integer day counts raise `<name> must be a non-negative integer`.
Retention policy metadata fields: `policy_version`, `raw_capture_enabled`, `raw_retention_days`, `metadata_retention_days`.
Retention decision: raw content is removed when age in days is strictly greater than the raw retention, metadata when strictly greater than the metadata retention (which also forces raw removal).
`agent_diagnostic` `code=malformed_json` `severity=error` (message `Prime record is not a JSON object`) for a JSON value that is not an object.

`agent_diagnostic` `code=absent_schema` `severity=error` (message `Prime stream has no schema declaration`, field `provider_record_type`) emitted once when a non-session record arrives before any session record; all records are then ignored.

`agent_diagnostic` `code=provider_retry` `severity=warning` for `auto_retry_start`: fields `message` (the `reason` or `Prime started an internal retry`), `provider_record_type`, `attempt`, `delay_ms` (from `delayMs`).
`agent_diagnostic` `code=unknown_record` `severity=warning` (message `Unknown Prime record type: <type|<absent>>`) for a record type outside the known set.
`agent_diagnostic` `code=malformed_json` `severity=error` (message `Malformed Prime JSON: <error>`) for a line that does not parse as JSON.
`agent_diagnostic` `code=absent_schema` with message `Prime session omitted schema version` when the session record has no `version`.

`agent_diagnostic` `code=unsupported_schema` `severity=error` (message `Unsupported Prime schema version <v>`) when the session declares a version other than 3; later records are ignored without further diagnostics.
`agent_init` (Prime adapter, from a v3 `session` record): fields `schema_version` = 3, `session_id`, `cwd`, `provider`, `model` (null values dropped).

`agent_init` with `update=true` (fields `schema_version`, `session_id`, `cwd`, `model`, `provider`, `update`) is emitted when an assistant `message_start` names a model or provider different from the current one.

`agent_text` (Prime adapter, one per closed text block): fields `message_key` (`<message_id>:<index>`), `message_id`, `content_index`, `text`, `final_fragment=true`, `redacted`, `truncated`, `original_bytes`, `retained_bytes`.
`agent_tool` `status=start` (Prime `tool_execution_start`): fields `tool_id`, `tool`, `status`, `targets`, `summary`, `redacted`, `truncated`, `original_bytes`, `retained_bytes`.
`evidence_writing` (Prime adapter): fields `tool_id`, `tool`, `target` (expected evidence path), `match=exact-expected-target`; emitted per matching tool start, not limited to once.

`agent_tool` `status=progress` (Prime `tool_execution_update` with non-empty message): fields `tool_id`, `tool`, `status`, `summary` (cut to 1024 bytes), `redacted`, `truncated`, `original_bytes`, `retained_bytes`; nothing is printed.

`agent_tool` `status=end` (Prime `tool_execution_end`): fields `tool_id`, `tool`, `status`, `is_error`, `duration_ms` (from `durationMs`), `result_summary` (cut to 4096 bytes), `redacted`, `truncated`, `original_bytes`, `retained_bytes`.

`agent_diagnostic` for a provider error: `code` `provider_auth` or `provider_error`, `severity=error`, `message`, `provider_record_type` (`error`, `message_end` or `agent_end`), plus redaction metadata.

`agent_diagnostic` `code=abandoned_tool` `severity=warning` (fields `message`, `provider_record_type=tool_execution`, `tool_id`, `tool`) for each tool that started or had arguments but never ended when the agent ends or the stream finishes.

`agent_diagnostic` common fields (Prime adapter): `code`, `severity`, `message` (cut to 1024 bytes), `provider_record_type`, `redacted`, `truncated`, `original_bytes`, `retained_bytes` plus code-specific extras; null values dropped.
`unsupported_schema`: terminal the Prime adapter produces at `finish()` when the declared schema version was present but not 3 (`status=error`).
`provider_auth`: Prime error whose message matches `auth`, `authentication`, `authorization`, `credential` or `api key` (any of space, `_`, `-` separator), case-insensitive.
`provider_error`: any other Prime-reported error; the error terminal carries `status=error`, `reason_code`, `reason`, `stop_reason` (default `error`) and the usage fields.
Prime init prints `  · init prime-v3 session=<id|?>`.
Prime assistant text is printed to stdout as the redacted text (up to 4096 bytes), without whitespace collapsing.
Prime tool start prints `  → <tool> <argument summary>` where the summary is the redacted JSON of the arguments cut to 2048 bytes.
Prime tool end prints `  ← <tool> error` or `  ← <tool> done`.
Every Prime diagnostic prints `  ! <code>: <message>` to stdout.

Prime evidence detection is lexical: `Path('

').write_text|write_bytes|open(`, `open('

', ''`, or a variable assigned from `Path('

')` that is later written; relative paths resolve against the session `cwd`, and the result must equal the expected evidence path.

Known Prime v3 record types: `session`, `message_start`, `message_update`, `message_end`, `turn_start`, `turn_end`, `agent_start`, `agent_end`, `auto_retry_start`, `auto_retry_end`, `error`, `toolcall_start`, `toolcall_delta`, `toolcall_end`, `tool_execution_start`, `tool_execution_update`, `tool_execution_end`.
A Prime error recorded before `agent_end` (from `error` or `message_end`) is exposed as the terminal only at `finish()` if no `agent_end` delivered one.
Prime messages whose role is present and not `assistant` are ignored for text and model tracking.
Prime text deltas (`delta.type` `text_delta` or `text`) are accumulated per message id and content index and are not emitted until `message_end`; a negative or non-integer index is treated as 0.
At `message_end` a content snapshot replaces the accumulated text only when it starts with it (or nothing was accumulated); otherwise the accumulated deltas win.
A Prime message ending with `stopReason`/`stop_reason` = `error` or an `errorMessage` records a provider error terminal (default message `Prime message ended with an error`).
A Prime tool record without `toolCallId`/`tool_call_id` gets a generated id `prime-tool-<n>`.
A Prime tool end counts as an error when `status` is `error`, `failed` or `failure` (case-insensitive) or `isError` is truthy.

Prime tool arguments that are not a dict/list are summarised as `{"script": <text>}`; quoted path literals containing `/` or named `GATE<n>-EVIDENCE.md` inside the text are added to `targets` up to 8 paths.

Prime `agent_end` is an error terminal when `status` is `error`/`failed`/`failure`, `stopReason` is `error` or an `error` value is present; it is a success terminal only when `status` is `success`, `completed`, `complete` or `ok`; any other status produces no terminal at all.
Prime success terminal fields: `status=success`, `stop_reason`, `model`, plus usage fields.

Prime usage extraction accepts camelCase and snake_case names: `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens` (also `cacheReadInputTokens`), `cache_write_tokens` (also `cacheCreationInputTokens`), `total_tokens`, `cost` (also `totalCost`); negative, boolean or non-numeric values are ignored.

Prime reports cost under terminal key `cost` and cache writes under `cache_write_tokens`, not `cost_usd`/`cache_creation_tokens`, so the OTLP cost/token metrics and the dashboard `unwrap cost_usd` get no value from a Prime result.
Prime usage from `turn_end` records is summed; usage on `agent_end` is merged as the maximum of the running total and the terminal value.
Prime `total_tokens` is derived as input + output when the provider gave none; the turn count is reported twice, as `num_turns` and `turns`.
`ralph_loki_ship.py event`: push one lifecycle event whose fields come from `KEY=VALUE` arguments and/or a JSON object on stdin.
`ralph_loki_ship.py stream`: read Claude stream-json JSONL on stdin, push `api_request` and `tool_use` to Loki, echo a human summary to stdout.
`--loki URL` (default `$RALPH_LOKI_URL`, else `http://localhost:3100`): Loki base URL.
`--task NAME` (default empty): becomes Loki label `task` when non-empty.
`--backend NAME` (default `claude`): becomes Loki label `backend`.
`--run-id ID` (default empty): added to the log line as `run_id` (never a label).
`--iter N` (default empty): added to the log line as `iter`.
`--event NAME` (default empty): required in `event` mode.
`--json-stdin`: in `event` mode read a JSON object from the last line of stdin and flatten it into fields, skipping keys `event` and `time`; unparsable input is ignored.
Positional `fields`: `KEY=VALUE` pairs (split on the first `=`); a bare `KEY` becomes `KEY=true`; they override stdin JSON fields.
`RALPH_LOKI_TIMEOUT` (default `2.5` seconds, float): timeout of each Loki push request, read once at import.
`RALPH_LOKI_MAX_BATCH_BYTES` (default 3145728): upper bound on one Loki push body; larger batches are split into several ordered pushes.
`RALPH_LOKI_URL`: default Loki base URL of the standalone shipper (fallback `http://localhost:3100`).
`tool_use` (standalone shippers, `stream` mode): fields `run_id`, `iter`, `tool`, `model`; extra Loki label `model`.

`api_request` (standalone shippers, one per Claude `result` record): fields `run_id`, `iter`, `model`, `is_error`, `subtype`, `cost_usd`, `duration_ms`, `duration_api_ms`, `num_turns`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_creation_tokens`, `result_preview` (first 300 characters, unredacted); extra Loki label `model`.
`ralph_loki_ship.py` exits 0 on every runtime failure (bad JSON, Loki down, HTTP error); an unexpected exception only prints `fatal (ignored): <error>`. Argparse errors exit 2.
Delivery `reason_code` `http_<status>` for an HTTP-level rejection.
Delivery `reason_code` `transport_error` for any non-HTTP failure (connection refused, timeout).
All Loki shipper warnings are stderr lines prefixed `ralph_loki_ship: `.
Loki failure warnings: `Loki push HTTP <status>`, `Loki push failed HTTP <code> <first 200 chars of body>`, `Loki push error: <exception>`.
`stream` mode prints `  · init model=<model|?> tools=<n>`, assistant text verbatim, `  → tool: <name>` per tool call and `  ✓ result: <subtype>  cost=$<4dp>  turns=<n>  out_tok=<n>  <ms>ms`.
In `event` mode without `--event` the shipper warns `ralph_loki_ship: event mode needs --event NAME` on stderr and pushes nothing (exit 0).
For normalized tap events only `role` is promoted to a Loki label; `run_id`, `invocation_id`, `sequence`, cost and tokens stay in the logfmt body.

logfmt encoding: `None` fields are omitted, booleans are `true`/`false`, numbers use `repr`, newlines become spaces, and a string that is empty or contains space, `"`, `=` or backslash is double-quoted with backslash and quote escaped.
Loki push endpoint is `<base without trailing slash>/loki/api/v1/push`.
Loki stream labels are the base labels (`job=ralph`, `task`, `backend`) plus `event`, plus optional extras; every other value stays in the logfmt line.
Loki entry timestamps are the shipper's own wall clock in nanoseconds (string), not the event's `ts`.
Loki push payload shape: `{"streams": [{"stream": {labels}, "values": [["<ns>", "<logfmt line>"], ...]}]}` sent as `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json`.
A Loki push counts as accepted only on HTTP 200 or 204.

Loki flush returns one aggregate delivery record: `sink=loki`, `batch_id` (`loki-<time_ns>-<seq>`), `event_count`, `status` (`accepted` or `failed`), `http_status`, `reason_code`; nothing buffered returns no record.
There is no retry and no spool: buffered streams are cleared after a flush even when the push failed, so a failed batch is lost to that sink.
In `stream` mode a non-JSON stdin line is echoed to stdout and not shipped.
`result_preview` on `api_request` is the first 300 characters of the model's final text and does not pass through the redaction policy.
Shipper base label `job` is always `ralph`.
In `event` mode `run_id` and `iter` from the flags are appended as fields after the positional fields (last wins).
`ralph_otel_ship.py event`: push one lifecycle event as OTLP log + metrics + spans.
`ralph_otel_ship.py stream`: same stdin contract and stdout summary as the Loki shipper, shipping OTLP logs, metrics and traces.
`--otel URL` (default `$RALPH_OTEL_URL`, else `http://localhost:4318`): OTLP/HTTP base URL.
OTLP shipper `--task NAME` (default empty): resource attribute `task`.
OTLP shipper `--backend NAME` (default `claude`): resource attribute `backend`.
OTLP shipper `--run-id ID` (default empty): field `run_id`.
OTLP shipper `--iter N` (default empty): field `iter`.
OTLP shipper `--json-stdin`: flatten the last stdin line (JSON object) into fields, skipping `event` and `time`.
OTLP shipper positional `fields`: `KEY=VALUE`, bare key means true.
OTLP shipper `--event NAME`: required in `event` mode, otherwise `ralph_otel_ship: event mode needs --event NAME` and nothing is sent.
`RALPH_OTEL_TIMEOUT` (default `2.5` seconds): timeout of each OTLP request.
`RALPH_OTEL_MAX_BATCH_BYTES` (default 3145728): upper bound on one OTLP logs request body; metrics and traces are sent unsplit.
`RALPH_OTEL_URL`: default OTLP base URL of the standalone shipper (fallback `http://localhost:4318`).
`gate` is recognised by the OTLP shipper as a metric-driving event (field `result`).
`ralph_otel_ship.py` exits 0 on every runtime failure; an unexpected exception prints `ralph_otel_ship: fatal (ignored): <error>`. Argparse errors exit 2.
All OTLP shipper warnings are stderr lines prefixed `ralph_otel_ship: `.
If the span module cannot be loaded the shipper warns `trace spans disabled (<error>)` and still ships logs and metrics.
A span derivation failure warns `trace span error: <error>` and the log record is still buffered.
OTLP failure warnings: `OTLP push HTTP <status> to <url>`, `OTLP push failed HTTP <code> <first 200 chars>`, `OTLP push error: <exception>`.
Instrumentation scope name for logs and metrics is `specstride.ralph`.
Metric `ralph.iter.duration_ms`: delta Histogram (unit `ms`), attribute `model`, explicit bounds 100, 500, 1000, 5000, 10000, 30000, 60000, 120000.
OTLP attribute typing: bool to `boolValue`, int to `intValue` as a string, float to `doubleValue`, everything else to `stringValue`.
OTLP endpoints: `<base>/v1/logs`, `<base>/v1/metrics`, `<base>/v1/traces`.
For normalized tap events the OTLP log body is the same logfmt string the Loki sink receives; `model` is the only attribute promoted alongside the fields.
Metric `ralph.cost_usd`: monotonic delta Sum (double, no unit), attribute `model`, fed by field `cost_usd` of `api_request` and `agent_result` events.

Metric `ralph.tokens`: monotonic delta Sum (int), attributes `model` and `type` in `input`, `output`, `cache_read`, `cache_creation`, fed by `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_creation_tokens`.
Metric `ralph.errors`: Sum (int), attribute `model`, incremented when `is_error` is true or the string `true`, `1` or `yes`.
Metric `ralph.tool_use`: Sum (int), attribute `tool`, incremented only for event name `tool_use`; the tap's `agent_tool` events do not feed it.
Metric `ralph.gate`: Sum (int), attribute `result`, incremented for event name `gate`.

OTLP log record shape: `timeUnixNano` (shipper clock), `observedTimeUnixNano`, `severityNumber` 9, `severityText` `INFO`, `body.stringValue` = the logfmt line, `attributes` = `event` plus every non-null field, and `traceId`/`spanId` when spans are active.
All metrics use DELTA aggregation temporality (value 1) with start time = shipper process start; sums are monotonic.
An OTLP request counts as accepted only on HTTP 200, 202 or 204.

OTLP flush returns one delivery record with `sink=otlp`, `batch_id` (`otlp-<time_ns>-<seq>`), `event_count`, `status`, `http_status`, `reason_code`; a failure on logs or metrics marks the batch failed.
The traces POST never changes the delivery verdict: a collector without a traces pipeline does not mark the batch failed.
No retry and no spool for OTLP: logs, sums and histograms are cleared after flush whether or not the push succeeded.
Standalone OTLP shipper resource attributes: `service.name=ralph`, `task`, `backend`.
`SPECSTRIDE_OTEL_TRACES` (default `true`): `false`, `0`, `no` or `off` (case-insensitive) disables span derivation and log/trace correlation.
`SPECSTRIDE_TRACE_ID`: when it is 32 hex characters (dashes ignored, not all zeros) it is used as the trace id, taking precedence over an event's `trace_id` field.
`SPECSTRIDE_OTEL_STATE_DIR`: directory of per-run span state; default `~/.cache/specstride/otel`.
`SPECSTRIDE_RUN_ID` is the fallback run id for span derivation when an event has no `run_id`; without any run id no span is produced.
`run_start` is recognised as opening scope span `run` (name `run <feature|task|run_id>`).
`phase_start` is recognised as opening scope span `phase` (name `phase <n>: <title>` or `phase <n>`).
`proposer_start` is recognised as opening scope span `attempt` (name `attempt p<phase>#<attempt>`).
`iter_start` is recognised as opening scope span `iter` (name `iter <iter>`).
`verification_start` is recognised as opening scope span `verification` (name `verification p<phase>`).
`critic_start` is recognised as opening scope span `critic` (name `critic p<phase>#<attempt>`).
`yield_wait` is recognised as opening scope span `yield`.
`long_job_start` is recognised as opening scope span `long_job`.
`run_end` is recognised as closing the `run` span.
`phase_done` is recognised as closing the `phase` span.
`reject` is recognised as closing the `attempt` span with error status.
`iter_done` is recognised as closing the `iter` span.
`iter_error` is recognised as closing the `iter` span with error status.
`iter_cap` is recognised as closing the `iter` span.
`iter_no_progress` is recognised as closing the `iter` span.
`verification_passed` is recognised as closing the `verification` span.
`verification_failed` is recognised as closing the `verification` span with error status.
`yield_resume` is recognised as closing the `yield` span.
`yield_timeout` is recognised as closing the `yield` span with error status.
`long_job_ended` is recognised as closing the `long_job` span.
`critic_malformed`, `pass_killed`, `yield_invalid` and `plugin_install_failed` are recognised as error events: their point spans get status ERROR with message `reason` or the event name.
`verdict` is recognised as closing the `critic` span; a `result` other than `APPROVED` (case-insensitive) sets error status with the result as message.
`run_stop` is recognised as closing the `run` span with error status, but only when the event has no `iter` field (a proposer-level `run_stop` becomes a point span).

Per-run span state file `<state_dir>/<run_id with unsafe chars as _, max 200>.json` holding `trace_id` and the open-scope `stack`; rewritten via `<path>.<pid>.tmp` + rename under an exclusive `flock` on `<path>.lock`.
Trace resource `service.name` is always `specstride` (the shipper's own `service.name` is discarded); other resource attributes are kept.
Trace instrumentation scope name is `specstride.trace`; every span has kind INTERNAL (1).
String span attribute values are cut to 512 characters; non-scalar values are JSON-encoded first.
Span state files older than 7 days are deleted when a `run_start` event is processed.
Span start time comes from the event's `ts` field (epoch seconds) when present, else the shipper clock; since the tap strips `ts` before shipping, tap events use the shipper clock.
Trace id derivation fallback: first 32 hex characters of `sha256("specstride:" + run_id)`, so every process of one run lands in the same trace.
Span ids are 8 random bytes (16 hex characters).

Scope spans are emitted only when they close; attributes are the opener's fields plus `specstride.scope`, `specstride.closed_by` and the closer's fields that do not collide; `ts`, `time`, `event` are never attributes.
Opening a scope type that is already open closes it and everything nested above it with `specstride.closed_by=superseded`; closing a scope closes everything nested above it.

Every event that is neither opener nor matched closer becomes a zero-length point span under the innermost open scope with attribute `specstride.event`; name is `tool <tool>` for `agent_tool`/`tool_use`, else the event name.
An `agent_tool`/`tool_use` point span stays open until the next event seen by the same process (or the flush) and takes that time as its end.

Traces payload shape: `resourceSpans[0].resource.attributes`, `scopeSpans[0].scope.name`, `spans[]` with `traceId`, `spanId`, `parentSpanId`, `name`, `kind`, `startTimeUnixNano`, `endTimeUnixNano`, `attributes`, and `status.code=2` with `message` on error.
`agent_tool` (shared builder): fields `tool`, `target`, `targets`, `redacted`, `truncated`, `original_bytes`, `retained_bytes`, optional `tool_id`.
`evidence_writing` (shared builder, at most once per builder instance): fields `tool`, `target`, `match=exact-expected-target`, optional `tool_id`.
`agent_init` synthesised by the shared-behaviour wrapper (formats with `synth_init`) on the first consumed record: fields `model` (the invocation model) and `tools` (null, hence dropped).

`agent_diagnostic` with `code=duplicate_terminal`, `severity=warning`, `message` `duplicate terminal dropped: the pass already had one` when a wrapped adapter delivers a second terminal; the second terminal is discarded.

`missing_terminal` synthesised by the wrapper (formats with `synth_terminal`) when the stream ended with no terminal: `status=error`, reason `Provider stream ended without a terminal result`, `model` = invocation model.
A synthesised init prints `  · init model=<model|?>` (no tools count).
The wrapper's synthesised terminal prints `  ✗ result: missing_terminal (stream ended before result)`.
`TARGET_MAX` = 120: a tool target is collapsed to one line and cut to 120 characters, the last one replaced by `…` when truncated.
Tool target key precedence is the fixed order `file_path`, `path`, `notebook_path`, `command`, `pattern`, `url`, `query`, `skill`, `description`, `prompt`, `subject`.
Nested target search is bounded: dicts deeper than 6 levels are not expanded and the search stops after 256 visited values, returning an empty target.
Only tools named `Write`, `Edit`, `MultiEdit`, `NotebookEdit` or `Bash` can trigger `evidence_writing`.
Canonical tool vocabulary an adapter's `TOOL_NAMES` may map to: `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `MultiEdit`, `NotebookEdit`, `Bash`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `Task`, `TodoWrite`, `WebFetch`, `WebSearch`.
Signal vocabulary and order: `init`, `text`, `tool`, `evidence`, `result`.
A stream format name or alias must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9]$` (lowercase, at least two characters).

Target resolution order for a tool call: for `Bash` the `command` (else `description`); otherwise exact top-level target keys, then camelCase keys converted to snake_case, then the bounded nested search.
No expected evidence path configured means `evidence_writing` is never emitted.
A write counts as evidence only when a lexically extracted path or the display target resolves (`expanduser().resolve()`) to exactly the expected evidence path; nothing from the provider is executed.
The shared tool-event builder reports the canonical tool name `TOOL_NAMES.get(harness_name, harness_name)`, i.e. an unmapped harness tool name passes through unchanged.
Default capability signals of a format are `init,text,tool,evidence,result`.
A format row's options and defaults: `has_init_record` true, `synth_init` false, `synth_terminal` false, `no_activity` false, `track_terminal` false, `aliases` empty.
Registry lookup resolves a canonical name or an alias to the same row and returns nothing for an unknown name.
A repeated format name or alias fails registry construction at import with `duplicate stream format: <label>`.
An invalid name or alias fails registry construction with `invalid stream format name: <name>`.
An empty capability reason fails registry construction with `empty capability reason for stream format: <name>`.
A format declaring `synth_init` together with `has_init_record` fails registry construction.
An adapter `TOOL_NAMES` value outside the canonical tool vocabulary fails registry construction with `maps tool to non-canonical name`.

Capability signals must be a non-empty, in-order, non-repeating comma-joined subset of the signal vocabulary; violations raise `declares no signals`, `has empty signal entries`, `declares unknown signal` or `declares out-of-order or repeated signals`.
The wrapper exposes `consume_raw` only when the inner adapter has it, and its `finish()` is idempotent.

With `no_activity` opted in, a success terminal gets additive field `no_activity` = true when no `agent_tool`/`evidence_writing` event was seen in the pass; `status`, `reason_code` and `is_error` are never altered.
`telemetry_delivery.py line <name> <state>` prints `<name>: <phrase>` for a state in the receiver vocabulary.
`telemetry_delivery.py probe <name> <url> [--events FILE] [--no-probe]` prints `<name>: <phrase> (<url>)` for the highest provable state.
`probe --events FILE`: read `telemetry_delivery` records from an events file to elevate the state; a missing file or malformed lines are tolerated.
`probe --no-probe`: skip the TCP probe so the state starts at `configured`.

`telemetry_delivery`: written to the local events file only, one per sink per flush that had a batch; fields `sink`, `batch_id`, `event_count`, `status`, `http_status`, `reason_code` (null values dropped) plus the envelope identity.
`telemetry_delivery.py line` exits 2 unless exactly two arguments are given and the state is one of the four known states; otherwise 0.
`telemetry_delivery.py probe` exits 2 with fewer than two arguments or any unrecognised trailing argument (including `--events` without a value); otherwise 0 even when the endpoint is unreachable.
`telemetry_delivery.py` exits 2 with no output when called with no arguments or an unknown command.
Receiver state phrases: `export configured`, `endpoint reachable`, `events accepted`, `query-verified`; a status line is `<sink>: <phrase>`.
`probe` output line shape: `<name>: <phrase> (<url>)`.
Delivery status vocabulary is `attempted`, `accepted`, `failed`, `unknown`; a shipper record with any other status is rewritten to `unknown`.
Local first: the event is written to the local JSONL synchronously before any remote sink is touched, so a total remote outage loses no local events.
Recursion guard: `telemetry_delivery` events are never shipped to any remote sink.
An exception while handing an event to one sink is swallowed so the other sinks still receive it.
There is no delivery ledger or spool file: delivery evidence exists only as `telemetry_delivery` lines in the run's events file.
A sink whose `flush()` raises yields a local record `{sink, status=failed, reason_code=transport_error}`.
Receiver state vocabulary in escalating order: `configured`, `reachable`, `request_accepted`, `query_verified`.
The OTLP shipper labels its records `sink=otlp` while the status surfaces ask for sink name `otel`, so OTLP delivery records never elevate the displayed OTLP state above `endpoint reachable`.

Only records with matching `sink` and `status=accepted` elevate a sink's state: to `request_accepted`, or to `query_verified` when the record has a truthy `query_verified` field; nothing in these modules ever sets that field.
Reachability probe is a plain TCP connect to the URL's host and port (default port 443 for https, else 80) with a 1.5 s timeout; any failure means not reachable.
`agent_observability` from the proposer when a registry-named format still parses plain output: fields `mode=raw-text`, `reason`, `role`, `provider_format`, `supported_signals=text,result`.
Route reason `structured capture disabled by SPECSTRIDE_AGENT_STREAM=false — parsing plain output` when a registry format exists but structured capture was switched off.
Route reason `stream tap unavailable (agent_stream.py or python3 missing) — parsing plain output`.
Route reason `stream format '<name>' has no registered adapter — parsing plain output` when the registry format is not printed by `agent_stream.py --list-formats`.
The proposer resolves a backend's stream format once per run from the backend registry's `stream` field; an empty value means plain-output parsing with no registry routing.

The tap is given the correlated flags plus `--provider-format prime-v3` and `--terminal-sidecar <invocation_dir>/provider-terminal.json` for the `prime` backend; other tapped backends default to the `claude` format on the legacy path unless registry-routed.
`--loki` / `--otel` are passed to the tap only when the respective sink is enabled for the run.
`specstride_stream_formats` is the bash shim over `agent_stream.py --list-formats`; stderr is discarded and it always returns 0.
When the python helper fails, the bash shim prints the fallback line `<name>: export configured (<url>)`.
The bundled dashboard has uid `ralph-loops` and title `Ralph Loops`.
Dashboard run and iteration counts rely on events named `run_start` and `iter_start`.
Dashboard error panel counts `api_request`/`agent_result` lines with `is_error="true"` or `status="error"`.

Dashboard cost, token, duration and request panels read events `api_request` or `agent_result` and unwrap logfmt fields `cost_usd`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_creation_tokens`, `duration_ms`.
Dashboard tool panels read events `tool_use` or `agent_tool` and group by logfmt field `tool`.
Dashboard gate panel reads event `gate` and groups by logfmt field `result`.
Every dashboard query selects streams by labels `job="ralph"`, `event`, `task`, `backend` and `role`, then filters the logfmt fields `run_id` and `invocation_id`.
Dashboard variables: `task`, `backend`, `role` (label value queries on `{job="ralph"}`) and free-text `run` and `invocation` (default `.*`).
`SPECSTRIDE_LOKI_PORT` (fallback `WIGGUM_LOKI_PORT`, default 3110): host port published for Loki's container port 3100.
`SPECSTRIDE_OTEL_PORT` (fallback `WIGGUM_OTEL_PORT`, default 4318): host port for the collector's OTLP/HTTP receiver.
`SPECSTRIDE_OTEL_GRPC_PORT` (fallback `WIGGUM_OTEL_GRPC_PORT`, default 4317): host port for OTLP/gRPC, unused by the shippers.
`SPECSTRIDE_PROMETHEUS_PORT` (fallback `WIGGUM_PROMETHEUS_PORT`, default 9091): host port for Prometheus 9090.
`SPECSTRIDE_GRAFANA_PORT` (fallback `WIGGUM_GRAFANA_PORT`, default 3010): host port for Grafana 3000.

Bundled Grafana allows anonymous access with org role `Admin` and the login form disabled.
